title: Accept this from us
who: Prophet Ibrahim and his son Ismail
situation: As they raised the foundations of the Kaaba in Mecca, they asked God to accept their work and to make their descendants a community devoted to Him.
arabic: وَاِذۡ يَرۡفَعُ اِبۡرٰهٖمُ الۡقَوَاعِدَ مِنَ الۡبَيۡتِ وَاِسۡمٰعِيۡلُؕ رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلۡ مِنَّا ​ؕ اِنَّكَ اَنۡتَ السَّمِيۡعُ الۡعَلِيۡمُ‏  رَبَّنَا وَاجۡعَلۡنَا مُسۡلِمَيۡنِ لَـكَ وَ مِنۡ ذُرِّيَّتِنَآ اُمَّةً مُّسۡلِمَةً لَّكَ وَاَرِنَا مَنَاسِكَنَا وَتُبۡ عَلَيۡنَا ۚ اِنَّكَ اَنۡتَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيۡمُ‏ ﻿﻿
translation: (127) And ˹remember˺ when Abraham raised the foundation of the House with Ishmael, ˹both praying,˺ “Our Lord! Accept ˹this˺ from us. You are indeed the All-Hearing, All-Knowing. (128) Our Lord! Make us both ˹fully˺ submit to You and from our descendants a nation that will submit to you. Show us our rituals, and turn to us in grace. You are truly the Accepter of Repentance, Most Merciful.
ai_translation: (127) When Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House, they prayed, "Our Rabb, accept this from us. You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing." (128) Our Rabb, make us submit to You, and from our descendants a community that submits to You. Show us our rites and turn to us in mercy. You are the Accepter of Repentance, the Rahim.

ai.m: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
ai.g: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

ai.m: He raises / is raising up — to lift, elevate, or build something up high. The verb rafaʿa covers physically raising as well as exalting in rank or status.
ai.g: A present-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular, with the prefix ya- ('he') marking the doer. The final -u ending is the indicative, normally marking a plain ongoing or repeated action. The verb means to raise up, lift, or elevate.
ai.r: ر-ف-ع (r-f-ʿ) — to raise, lift, elevate, exalt

ai.m: Ibrāhīm (Abraham), the proper name of the patriarch and prophet, revered as a model of pure devotion to Allah.
ai.g: A proper name (of non-Arabic origin). The final -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject or the one doing/being something in a sentence. Being a foreign name, it does not take nunation (no '-un').
ai.r: — (proper name, no Arabic root)

ai.m: Al-qawāʿid — the foundations, bases, or supporting structures on which something is built; figuratively the underlying principles or seated women past childbearing, but at root the parts that hold something up.
ai.g: A definite broken (irregular) plural of qāʿida ('base, foundation'). The final -a ending is accusative, the case that typically marks the object of a verb (the thing acted upon). The word names the foundations or supporting bases of a structure.
ai.r: ق-ع-د (q-ʿ-d) — to sit, settle; base, foundation

ai.m: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
ai.g: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

ai.m: Al-bayt — the house, dwelling, or home; a place of residence or a building set apart, often used for a household or a place of worship.
ai.g: A definite noun. The final -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition or oath particle. The word denotes a house, dwelling, or set-apart sacred building.
ai.r: ب-ي-ت (b-y-t) — to spend the night; house, dwelling

ai.m: Ismāʿīl (Ishmael), the proper name of the prophet, son of Ibrāhīm.
ai.g: Conjunction wa- ('and') plus a proper name (of non-Arabic origin). The final -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject or the one doing/being something. Being a foreign name, it takes no nunation (no '-un').
ai.r: — (proper name, no Arabic root)

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: Accept! / Receive favorably! — a plea that an act of worship or supplication be graciously received and approved. The verb taqabbala stresses willing, gracious acceptance.
ai.g: A second-person masculine singular imperative ('you, accept!'), built on the reflexive-intensive (Form V) pattern, which stresses willingly taking something to oneself. The silent (jussive) ending with no final vowel marks the command addressed to one male. It asks for an act to be graciously received.
ai.r: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to accept, receive, take willingly

ai.m: "from us" — the preposition 'from' (indicating origin, source, or starting point) fused with the attached pronoun 'us'. It can also carry a partitive sense, 'some of us / a part of us'.
ai.g: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The base 'min' normally takes a vowelless final consonant, but before the pronoun '-nā' the nūn is doubled (assimilation), giving 'minnā'. The suffix '-nā' is the first-person plural object/possessive pronoun meaning 'us' or 'our'.
ai.r: — (preposition; the pronoun has no triliteral root)

ai.m: 'Indeed you' — an emphasis particle meaning 'truly / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'you', used to open a statement with certainty and stress about the person addressed.
ai.g: The emphasis particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with an attached pronoun. 'inna' adds strong assertion to a sentence and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The suffix '-ka' means 'you' (masculine singular) as its subject.

ai.m: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
ai.g: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

ai.m: "the All-Hearing" — one who hears, perceiving all sounds completely and constantly; used as a divine name it denotes the One whose hearing is perfect and all-encompassing.
ai.g: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, which conveys a deep, enduring quality ('ever-hearing,' not merely 'hearing once'). The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form a word takes when it is the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description following it.
ai.r: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — hearing, listening

ai.m: The All-Knowing — one whose knowledge is complete, perfect, and all-encompassing; an intensive form stressing that knowing is an essential, constant attribute.
ai.g: A definite noun/adjective in an intensive pattern (faʿīl) that stresses depth and permanence of the quality. The prefix 'al-' means 'the'; the final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it.
ai.r: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: "and make us / and appoint us" — a plea: 'render us into,' 'cause us to become,' or 'set us as.' The verb 'jaʿala' means to make, form, render, or appoint something into a state or role.
ai.g: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single 'you,' with an attached object pronoun '-nā' ('us'). The 'wa-' is the connector 'and.' The vowelless ending on the verb stem (sukūn) is characteristic of the imperative. 'jaʿala' often takes two objects: the thing made and what it is made into.
ai.r: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint, place

ai.m: "two who submit / two submitters" — the dual of 'muslim,' one who surrenders and submits wholly (to Allah); thus 'a pair of submitters,' two who give themselves over in willing obedience.
ai.g: An active participle (from the form-IV verb aslama, 'to submit/surrender') in the dual, denoting exactly two. The '-ayni' ending marks the dual in the accusative/genitive (oblique) case — the form used for an object of a verb or after a preposition, as opposed to the '-āni' used for the subject.
ai.r: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — soundness, peace, submission, surrender

ai.m: 'For You / to You' — a 'for/to' particle attached to the pronoun 'You,' indicating that something is directed toward, or done for the sake of, a single addressee.
ai.g: A small phrase: the particle li- ('for / to,' vowelled la- before a pronoun) joined to the attached pronoun -ka, 'you' (one masculine addressee). The pronoun is in the form used as the object of a preposition, marking the person as the one to whom or for whom the action is directed.
ai.r: — (particle + pronoun, no triliteral root)

ai.m: 'And from / and out of / and among.' A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'from,' which marks origin, source, a starting point, or 'some of' a larger whole.
ai.g: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

ai.m: "our offspring / our descendants / our progeny" — one's children and the line of descendants that issue from a person; 'dhurriyya' denotes seed, lineage, the generations springing from someone.
ai.g: A feminine noun with the first-person plural possessive pronoun '-nā' ('our') attached. Its tā' marbūṭa is pronounced as a 't' once a suffix follows (so the word reads 'dhurriyyati-nā'). The '-i' vowel is the genitive case ending, signalling that the noun is possessed (linked to the following 'our') or governed by a preceding preposition/oath particle — the general sense of '… of …'.
ai.r: ذ-ر-ر (dh-r-r) — to scatter, disperse (seed); hence progeny (debated; some relate it to ذ-ر-أ, to create/multiply)

ai.m: "a community / a nation / a people" — a single group bound together as one body, typically by shared faith, way of life, or leadership; 'umma' is a collective people united around something.
ai.g: A feminine singular noun, indefinite ('a community'). The '-an' ending (tanwīn fatḥ) is the indefinite accusative case, the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or as a predicate after certain verbs of making/becoming; the final alif is the written seat of this ending.
ai.r: أ-م-م (ʾ-m-m) — to head toward, intend; a community/leadership (cf. imām)

ai.m: "submissive / surrendering (feminine)" — feminine form describing one (a group, a soul, a community) that submits and surrenders wholly to Allah; the feminine of 'muslim.'
ai.g: A feminine active participle (from form IV, aslama 'to submit'), indefinite. The tā' marbūṭa marks it as feminine. The '-an' ending (tanwīn fatḥ) is the indefinite accusative case, used for an object or for a description agreeing with an accusative noun.
ai.r: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — soundness, peace, submission, surrender

ai.m: "to You / for You" — the preposition 'to/for' (denoting direction, belonging, or benefit) joined to the singular pronoun 'You,' expressing devotion or attribution directed toward a single addressee.
ai.g: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. When 'li-' takes a pronoun its vowel shifts to 'a,' giving 'la-.' The suffix '-ka' is the second-person masculine singular pronoun, 'you' (object), here conveying 'to/for you.'
ai.r: — (preposition; the pronoun has no triliteral root)

ai.m: "and show us / and let us see" — a plea to be shown or made to perceive something; the verb 'arā' (form IV of 'to see') means to cause someone to see, to display or reveal a thing to them.
ai.g: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single 'you,' with the object pronoun '-nā' ('us') attached; 'wa-' is 'and.' It comes from a root whose weak final letter has dropped in the imperative, leaving the short form 'ari.' Being form IV (causative), it means 'make (us) see' = 'show (us).'
ai.r: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive; (form IV) to show, cause to see

ai.m: "our rites / our rituals of worship" — the appointed acts and ceremonies of devotion (especially the rites of pilgrimage); 'manāsik' are prescribed places or acts of worship and sacrifice.
ai.g: A plural noun (of place/act, plural of mansak/mansik) with the possessive pronoun '-nā' ('our') attached. The 'a' vowel before the pronoun is the accusative case ending, the form a noun takes as the direct object of a verb.
ai.r: ن-س-ك (n-s-k) — devotion, worship, ritual sacrifice

ai.m: "and turn (in mercy) / and relent / accept repentance" — when used of Allah, 'tāba ʿalā' means to turn toward someone with mercy, to forgive and accept their repentance; the verb 'tāba' is to turn back.
ai.g: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single 'you,' from a hollow root whose middle weak letter is shortened in the imperative (giving 'tub' rather than 'tūb'). The vowelless ending (sukūn) marks the imperative. Directed at Allah, it is a plea for mercy/forgiveness; when its subject is a person, the same verb means 'to repent.'
ai.r: ت-و-ب (t-w-b) — to turn back, repent; (of Allah) to turn in mercy, accept repentance

ai.m: 'Upon us' / 'over us' / 'against us' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, upon') with an attached 'us'. It conveys something resting on, incumbent upon, or bearing against the group.
ai.g: A preposition (ʿalā, 'upon/over') with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'us'). When a pronoun is attached, ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay-. Such prepositional phrases put their pronoun in the object/genitive role.

ai.m: 'Indeed you' — an emphasis particle meaning 'truly / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'you', used to open a statement with certainty and stress about the person addressed.
ai.g: The emphasis particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with an attached pronoun. 'inna' adds strong assertion to a sentence and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The suffix '-ka' means 'you' (masculine singular) as its subject.

ai.m: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
ai.g: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

ai.m: A name/quality meaning 'the One who constantly turns with forgiveness' — the Ever-Relenting, who again and again accepts the repentance of those who turn back to Him. The intensive form stresses how abundantly and repeatedly He forgives.
ai.g: The definite article l- ('the') with a noun in the intensive pattern (faʿʿāl), which signals doing something abundantly or habitually — here, turning to forgive again and again. The -u ending marks nominative case, typical of a subject or a word describing/identifying the subject.
ai.r: ت-و-ب (t-w-b) — turning back, repentance, returning

ai.m: A name/quality meaning 'the Most Merciful' or 'the Bestower of mercy' — the One whose mercy is deeply felt and continually shown to His creation.
ai.g: The definite article l- ('the') with an intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep, enduring quality of mercy. The -u ending marks nominative case, typical of a subject or of a word describing/identifying the subject.
ai.r: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion, tenderness

title: Good in this world and the next
who: Taught in the Qur'an as the prayer of the believer
situation: Revealed during the Hajj to contrast the believer, who asks for good in both worlds, with those who ask only for the gains of this life.
arabic: وَمِنۡهُمۡ مَّنۡ يَّقُوۡلُ رَبَّنَآ اٰتِنَا فِى الدُّنۡيَا حَسَنَةً وَّفِى الۡاٰخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَّ قِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ‏
translation: Yet there are others who say, “Our Lord! Grant us the good of this world and the Hereafter, and protect us from the torment of the Fire.”
ai_translation: And among them are those who say, "Our Rabb, give us good in this world and good in the Akhirah, and protect us from the Fire."

ai.m: 'And among them / and some of them' — a connective 'and' plus a preposition meaning 'from / among / part of,' joined to the pronoun 'them'; often introduces a subgroup ('among them are …').
ai.g: A connective wa- ('and') with the preposition min ('from / among'), which always governs a following word in the genitive. Here that word is the attached pronoun -hum ('them'), giving 'and among them / and from them.' Particles like these do not themselves carry case or tense.

ai.m: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
ai.g: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

ai.m: He says / he is saying — the act of speaking or uttering words, attributed to a single male (or generic) subject in the ongoing or habitual sense.
ai.g: A present/imperfect-tense verb. The prefix ya- marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). Here the ya is written with a shadda (doubled, yya-) because a preceding word's final consonant assimilates into it and merges (idghām); the doubling belongs to that sound-merger, not to the verb itself. The final -u is the indicative ending, the default mood used for a plain statement of fact about an action that is ongoing or habitual ('he says / he is saying').
ai.r: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

ai.m: An address to Allah meaning 'Our Lord' — invoking the Sustainer, Master, and Nurturer who creates, owns, provides for, and brings His servants to maturity. 'Rabb' is a rich term: not merely 'lord' but the One who cherishes and governs all that He has made. The attached 'our' makes it a direct calling upon Him.
ai.g: A noun ('Lord / Sustainer') with an attached possessive pronoun. The -a ending reflects the accusative, used here in the vocative sense (calling out, 'O our Lord') — the implied 'O' (yā) is dropped before a noun joined to a pronoun. The suffix -nā means 'our'. So it reads 'O our Lord / our Lord!'.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship and cherishing care

ai.m: An imperative plea meaning 'give us / grant us / bring to us.' It is a request addressed to a single party (commonly Allah in supplication) asking that something be conferred upon 'us.'
ai.g: A command (imperative) verb from the form-IV verb 'to give/bring.' It is directed at a single addressee ('you give!'). The attached -nā is an object pronoun meaning 'us,' marking who receives the action.
ai.r: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to bring/give

ai.m: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
ai.g: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
ai.r: — (particle)

ai.m: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
ai.g: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
ai.r: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

ai.m: Something good, fine, or beautiful; a good deed, a benefit, or a blessing. As a noun it denotes a good thing or good fortune.
ai.g: A feminine singular noun/adjective (the -a marks feminine gender). The final -tan (tanwīn fatḥa) marks it as indefinite ('a good thing') and in the accusative case, typically used for the direct object of a verb or as the thing requested/described.
ai.r: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — to be good, beautiful, fine

ai.m: A connective phrase meaning 'and in / and within.' It joins a new item to what precedes and places something inside or amid a sphere, time, or place.
ai.g: A compound of the connector 'wa' (and) plus the preposition 'fī' (in). 'fī' governs a following noun, putting it in the genitive case and locating something inside it, whether in place, time, or situation.

ai.m: The Hereafter — the final, lasting life that comes after death and the present world; literally 'the last/latter (abode or life)', as opposed to the first, nearer life.
ai.g: A feminine adjective used as a noun, with 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …'), or follows a preposition or oath particle.
ai.r: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, end

ai.m: Something good, fine, or beautiful; a good deed, a benefit, or a blessing. As a noun it denotes a good thing or good fortune.
ai.g: A feminine singular noun/adjective (the -a marks feminine gender). The final -tan (tanwīn fatḥa) marks it as indefinite ('a good thing') and in the accusative case, typically used for the direct object of a verb or as the thing requested/described.
ai.r: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — to be good, beautiful, fine

ai.m: An imperative plea meaning 'and protect us / and guard us / and shield us,' asking that 'we' be kept safe from some harm or evil.
ai.g: The connector 'wa' (and) plus a command (imperative) verb 'protect/guard,' addressed to a single party ('you protect!'). The attached -nā ('us') is the object, marking who is to be shielded.
ai.r: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, protect, shield

ai.m: Torment, punishment, or chastisement — severe, painful suffering imposed as a penalty.
ai.g: A singular noun. The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case, the form used for a direct object of a verb, or for the first noun of a possessive pair ('the punishment of …') when that whole phrase is itself an object.
ai.r: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to torment, punish

ai.m: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
ai.g: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').
ai.r: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — fire, blaze, burning

title: Pour patience upon us
situation: As the small band of believers faced the army of Jalut (Goliath), they prayed for patience, firm footing, and victory.
arabic: وَلَمَّا بَرَزُوۡا لِجَـالُوۡتَ وَجُنُوۡدِهٖ قَالُوۡا رَبَّنَآ اَفۡرِغۡ عَلَيۡنَا صَبۡرًا وَّثَبِّتۡ اَقۡدَامَنَا وَانۡصُرۡنَا عَلَى الۡقَوۡمِ الۡکٰفِرِيۡنَؕ‏
translation: When they advanced to face Goliath and his warriors, they prayed, “Our Lord! Shower us with perseverance, make our steps firm, and give us victory over the disbelieving people.”
ai_translation: When they faced Goliath and his army, they prayed, "Our Rabb, pour sabr upon us, make our steps firm, and give us victory over those who reject the truth."

ai.m: A compound meaning 'and when' — it sets up a circumstance in past time, marking the moment at which something occurred, with the result clause typically following. It carries the sense of 'when, at the time that.'
ai.g: A particle phrase introducing a past-time clause. Lammā signals 'when' for completed events and expects a following clause stating what then happened; the wa- prefix means 'and.'

ai.m: 'They went forth / came out (into the open),' especially to step out for battle or to confront an opponent. The verb conveys emerging into open view, advancing prominently.

p.en: to go forth, emerge into the open

ai.g: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The suffix '-ū' marks a completed action by a third-person masculine plural subject ('they went forth'). The trailing silent alif (وا) is a spelling convention after this plural ending and is not pronounced.
ai.r: ب-ر-ز (b-r-z) — to come out, emerge, stand forth

ai.m: The name Jālūt (Goliath) preceded by 'li-', giving the sense 'for / to(ward) / to face' him — directing oneself at or against the named person.
ai.g: The preposition 'li-' ('to', 'for', and by extension 'to face/against') joined to a foreign proper name. Being a diptote non-Arabic name, it takes the single '-a' ending after the preposition instead of the usual genitive '-i', and carries no nunation.
ai.r: — (proper name)

ai.m: 'And his troops/soldiers' — the plural of jund (an army, host, or body of soldiers), joined by 'and' and made possessive by an attached 'his', so: a person's military forces or supporters.
ai.g: Connective 'wa-' ('and') + a broken (irregular) plural noun + the possessive suffix '-hi' ('his'). The '-i' before the suffix is the genitive ending, signalling that the noun is possessed by what follows (here the pronoun 'his') or governed by a preceding preposition. The suffix vowel '-hi' (with kasra) harmonises after that genitive '-i'.
ai.r: ج-ن-د (j-n-d) — to recruit/muster; army, host

ai.m: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
ai.g: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.
ai.r: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, utterance

ai.m: An address to Allah meaning 'Our Lord' — invoking the Sustainer, Master, and Nurturer who creates, owns, provides for, and brings His servants to maturity. 'Rabb' is a rich term: not merely 'lord' but the One who cherishes and governs all that He has made. The attached 'our' makes it a direct calling upon Him.
ai.g: A noun ('Lord / Sustainer') with an attached possessive pronoun. The -a ending reflects the accusative, used here in the vocative sense (calling out, 'O our Lord') — the implied 'O' (yā) is dropped before a noun joined to a pronoun. The suffix -nā means 'our'. So it reads 'O our Lord / our Lord!'.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship and cherishing care

ai.m: 'Pour out! / Pour down!' — a command to make a liquid flow abundantly, and figuratively to bestow or shower something (such as strength or patience) lavishly and completely.
ai.g: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single male ('you, pour!'), from the causative (form IV) verb 'afragha' ('to pour out, to make flow'). The initial alif here is hamzat al-qaṭʿ — the permanent causative prefix that is built into every form IV verb and is always pronounced (never dropped); it is not a prosthetic helping vowel. The final consonant is left vowel-less (jussive), as is normal for an order.
ai.r: ف-ر-غ (f-r-gh) — to be empty; to pour out/empty

ai.m: 'Upon us' / 'over us' / 'against us' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, upon') with an attached 'us'. It conveys something resting on, incumbent upon, or bearing against the group.
ai.g: A preposition (ʿalā, 'upon/over') with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'us'). When a pronoun is attached, ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay-. Such prepositional phrases put their pronoun in the object/genitive role.

ai.m: Patience, steadfast endurance, self-restraint — the inner strength to bear hardship calmly, persevere, and hold oneself firm without complaint. A rich virtue: composure under trial and constancy in obedience.
ai.g: A masculine verbal noun, indefinite. The '-an' ending (written with a following alif) is the indefinite accusative, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb — the thing being given, poured, or brought about.
ai.r: ص-ب-ر (ṣ-b-r) — to be patient, endure, restrain oneself

ai.m: 'And make firm! / and steady! / and plant firmly!' — a command to fix something securely in place and keep it from slipping, whether literally (footing) or figuratively (resolve, hearts).
ai.g: Connective 'wa-' ('and') + an intensive (form II) command verb addressed to a single male ('you, make firm!'). The doubled middle root letter conveys causing/intensifying — 'to make firmly fixed.' The final consonant is left vowel-less (jussive), the normal shape of a command.
ai.r: ث-ب-ت (th-b-t) — to be firm, fixed, steadfast

ai.m: 'Our feet' — the plural of qadam (foot), made possessive by an attached 'our'. By extension 'making the feet firm' is an idiom for granting steadfastness and stability.
ai.g: A broken (irregular) plural noun + the possessive suffix '-nā' ('our'). The '-a' before the suffix is the accusative ending, which here marks the noun as the direct object — the thing being acted upon — while '-nā' shows it belongs to 'us'.
ai.r: ق-د-م (q-d-m) — to precede/advance; foot, step

ai.m: 'And help us! / give us victory! / aid us!' — a command to come to someone's aid and grant them support and triumph, with 'us' as the one helped.
ai.g: Connective 'wa-' ('and') + a command verb addressed to a single male ('you, help!') + the object pronoun '-nā' ('us'). The initial alif is a prosthetic helping vowel (hamzat al-waṣl), added to begin this form I command whose stem starts with a vowel-less consonant; it drops in pronunciation when joined to a preceding word. The stem vowel is left vowel-less (jussive) as is normal for an order, and '-nā' is the one receiving the help.
ai.r: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, aid, grant victory

ai.m: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
ai.g: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
ai.r: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

ai.m: 'The people / the folk' — a collective noun for a community, nation, or group of people regarded as a body. Often it carries the nuance of one's own people or a particular group sharing a trait.
ai.g: A collective noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-i' is the genitive ending, which typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship.
ai.r: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand/rise; a people, community

ai.m: 'The disbelievers / the ungrateful concealers' — those who reject faith and cover over the truth. The active participle of kufr names people characterised by denying Allah and being ungrateful for His favours.
ai.g: An active participle ('one who disbelieves') with the definite article 'al-', in the sound masculine plural. The ending '-īna' is the plural marker used in the genitive or accusative cases — that is, when the word follows a preposition, is linked to a preceding noun, or serves as an object/descriptor of one in those cases (as opposed to '-ūna', used for the subject case).
ai.r: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover/conceal; to disbelieve, be ungrateful

title: Do not burden us beyond our capacity
who: The believers — the closing verses of Surah al-Baqarah
situation: According to hadith these verses were given to the Prophet during the Night Journey. They affirm faith and ask God not to burden the believers beyond what they can bear.
arabic: اٰمَنَ الرَّسُوۡلُ بِمَاۤ اُنۡزِلَ اِلَيۡهِ مِنۡ رَّبِّهٖ وَ الۡمُؤۡمِنُوۡنَ​ؕ كُلٌّ اٰمَنَ بِاللّٰهِ وَمَلٰٓٮِٕكَتِهٖ وَكُتُبِهٖ وَرُسُلِهٖ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيۡنَ اَحَدٍ مِّنۡ رُّسُلِهٖ​ وَقَالُوۡا سَمِعۡنَا وَاَطَعۡنَا​ غُفۡرَانَكَ رَبَّنَا وَاِلَيۡكَ الۡمَصِيۡرُ‏  لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللّٰهُ نَفۡسًا اِلَّا وُسۡعَهَا ​ؕ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتۡ وَعَلَيۡهَا مَا اكۡتَسَبَتۡ​ؕ رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذۡنَاۤ اِنۡ نَّسِيۡنَاۤ اَوۡ اَخۡطَاۡنَا ​ۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحۡمِلۡ عَلَيۡنَاۤ اِصۡرًا كَمَا حَمَلۡتَهٗ عَلَى الَّذِيۡنَ مِنۡ قَبۡلِنَا ​​ۚرَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلۡنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهٖ​ ۚ وَاعۡفُ عَنَّا وَاغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَارۡحَمۡنَا اَنۡتَ مَوۡلٰٮنَا فَانۡصُرۡنَا عَلَى الۡقَوۡمِ الۡكٰفِرِيۡنَ‏ ﻿﻿
translation: (285) The Messenger ˹firmly˺ believes in what has been revealed to him from his Lord, and so do the believers. They ˹all˺ believe in Allah, His angels, His Books, and His messengers. ˹They proclaim,˺ “We make no distinction between any of His messengers.” And they say, “We hear and obey. ˹We seek˺ Your forgiveness, our Lord! And to You ˹alone˺ is the final return.” (286) Allah does not require of any soul more than what it can afford. All good will be for its own benefit, and all evil will be to its own loss. ˹The believers pray,˺ “Our Lord! Do not punish us if we forget or make a mistake. Our Lord! Do not place a burden on us like the one you placed on those before us. Our Lord! Do not burden us with what we cannot bear. Pardon us, forgive us, and have mercy on us. You are our ˹only˺ Guardian. So grant us victory over the disbelieving people.”
ai_translation: (285) The Messenger believes in what was sent down to him from his Rabb, and so do the believers. Each believes in Allah, His angels, His Books, and His messengers: "We make no distinction between any of His messengers." They say, "We hear and obey. Your forgiveness, our Rabb — and to You is the final return." (286) Allah does not burden any soul beyond what it can bear. It will have the reward of what good it earned, and the consequence of what evil it earned. They pray: "Our Rabb, do not hold us accountable if we forget or make a mistake. Our Rabb, do not place on us a burden like the one You placed on those before us. Our Rabb, do not burden us with what we cannot bear. Pardon us, forgive us, and have mercy on us. You are our Protector — so grant us victory over those who reject the truth."

ai.m: 'He believed' — he had faith, trusted, and affirmed. The basic past-tense form of the verb meaning to believe and to find security in faith.
ai.g: A past-tense verb on the causative (Form IV) pattern, from the root for security and faith. The -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he (believed)', stating a completed act of coming to faith.
ai.r: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, safety, trust, faith

ai.m: 'The Messenger' — one sent with a message; in religious usage, a prophet commissioned by Allah to deliver revelation to people.
ai.g: 'al-' is the definite article 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following r, doubling it). 'rasūl' is a noun meaning 'one who is sent, an envoy/messenger'. The final -u is the nominative ending, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence or a word simply being named.
ai.r: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching, a message/envoy

ai.m: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
ai.g: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.
ai.r: — (particle + relative pronoun)

ai.m: 'It was sent down / revealed': the act of being caused to descend, used especially of revelation brought down from Allah. The passive form puts the focus on the thing sent down rather than on the sender.
ai.g: A past-tense passive verb in Form IV (anzala 'to send down' → unzila 'was sent down'). The prefix is only the u- vowel carried on the connecting hamza; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ز-ل), not part of the prefix. The internal vowel pattern u–i marks it as passive ('was/were sent down'), with no named doer. The final -a marks the subject as 'he/it', a single masculine thing, and signals completed action.
ai.r: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (Form IV) to send down

ai.m: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
ai.g: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

ai.m: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
ai.g: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
ai.r: — (preposition)

ai.m: A phrase meaning 'his Lord'. 'Lord' (rabb) denotes the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and governs — far richer than a mere title; here joined to 'his'.
ai.g: The noun 'Lord' with the genitive -i ending followed by the attached pronoun -hi ('his'). The genitive case appears because the noun is linked to a preceding word ('… OF his Lord') or follows a preposition. The lengthened -hī reflects how this pronoun is pronounced after an -i vowel.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, ownership, sustaining and bringing to completion

ai.m: "and the believers" — those who have faith, who accept and trust; wa- joins it on and al- makes it definite ('the believers' as a group).
ai.g: A masculine sound plural noun, 'believers.' The -ūna ending is the subject (nominative) form of the masculine plural, used when the word is the one doing the action; the matching object/possessive form would be -īna.
ai.r: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, faith, trust

ai.m: A noun meaning 'all,' 'each,' 'every,' or 'the whole.' It denotes totality — that the entirety of a group or thing is included.
ai.g: A noun in the nominative case with 'tanwīn' (the -un ending), which marks it as indefinite and as the subject or doer of a sentence. Standing alone with tanwīn it carries the sense 'everyone / all of them' as an independent subject.
ai.r: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — totality, comprising the whole

ai.m: 'He believed' — he had faith, trusted, and affirmed. The basic past-tense form of the verb meaning to believe and to find security in faith.
ai.g: A past-tense verb on the causative (Form IV) pattern, from the root for security and faith. The -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he (believed)', stating a completed act of coming to faith.
ai.r: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, safety, trust, faith

ai.m: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
ai.g: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
ai.r: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

ai.m: "and His angels" — wa- joins it on; refers to the angels, and the attached -hi means 'His,' marking them as belonging to Allah.
ai.g: A feminine plural noun ('angels') with an attached possessive pronoun. The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive (possessive/'of') case, and the suffix -hi means 'his/His'; the i-coloured form -hi (rather than -hu) is what naturally follows that -i ending.
ai.r: ل-ء-ك / م-ل-ك (l-ʾ-k) — message, sending; an angel as a messenger

ai.m: "and His books / scriptures" — wa- joins it on; the plural of 'book,' here in the sense of revealed scriptures, with -hi 'His' marking them as Allah's.
ai.g: A plural noun ('books') with an attached possessive. The -i before the pronoun is the genitive (possessive/'of') case, and -hi means 'his/His'; the i-coloured -hi form is the one used after an -i vowel.
ai.r: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — writing, inscribing, a book

ai.m: "and His messengers" — wa- joins it on; the plural of 'messenger / envoy,' those sent with a message, with -hi 'His' marking them as sent by Allah.
ai.g: A plural noun ('messengers') with an attached possessive. The -i before the pronoun is the genitive (possessive/'of') case, and -hi means 'his/His', the i-coloured form used after an -i vowel.
ai.r: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a messenger, an envoy

ai.m: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
ai.g: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

ai.m: 'We make a distinction / we separate / we differentiate (between things)'. It expresses treating items as separate or unequal, singling some out from others.
ai.g: A present/imperfect verb, first person plural: the 'nu-' prefix means 'we'. The doubled middle root letter marks the intensive (Form II) pattern, giving the sense of actively differentiating or sorting. The final -u marks the plain indicative mood (a simple statement: 'we do …').
ai.r: ف-ر-ق (f-r-q) — to separate, divide, distinguish

ai.m: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
ai.g: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
ai.r: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

ai.m: One; anyone; a single individual. Often used in negative or conditional contexts to mean 'anyone (at all)'.
ai.g: An indefinite noun in the genitive case. The -in ending combines the genitive marker -i (the form taken after a preposition or in a possessive link, '… of …') with nunation (-n), the sign of an indefinite 'a / any'.
ai.r: أ-ح-د (ʾ-ḥ-d) — oneness, unity; one

ai.m: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
ai.g: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

ai.m: "His messengers" — the plural of 'messenger / envoy,' those sent bearing a message, with the attached -hi 'His' marking them as Allah's.
ai.g: A plural noun ('messengers') with an attached possessive. The -i before the pronoun is the genitive (possessive/'of') case, and -hi means 'his/His', the i-coloured form used after an -i vowel.
ai.r: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a messenger, an envoy

ai.m: And they said — to utter or declare in speech, with the action presented as completed by a group.
ai.g: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. 'qāla' is the past-tense verb 'to say'; the '-ū' suffix marks a completed action done by 'they' (a masculine or mixed group). The stem shown here ('qālu') carries only the stem vowel before the suffix, with the plural '-ū' supplied by the separate ending. Past tense, so the speaking is presented as already finished.
ai.r: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak

ai.m: A past-tense verb meaning 'we heard / we listened' — the act of perceiving sound or a message, often carrying the further nuance of heeding or taking in what was said.
ai.g: A completed (past-tense) verb. The attached ending -nā marks the subject as 'we', so the action is something a group did and finished: 'we heard'.
ai.r: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — hearing, listening

ai.m: "and we obeyed / and we have complied" — wa- joins it on; the verb means to obey, submit to, and willingly comply with a command.
ai.g: A past-tense verb with the subject suffix -nā meaning 'we.' Past tense presents the action as already completed ('we obeyed'); the -nā ending shows 'we' are the ones who did it.
ai.r: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — obedience, willing compliance, submission

ai.m: "Your forgiveness" — the noun for forgiveness/pardon, especially Allah covering over and pardoning sins; the attached -ka means 'Your.' As a standalone request it carries the force of 'we beg Your forgiveness.'
ai.g: A verbal noun ('forgiveness') with the attached possessive -ka ('your,' addressing one person). The -a ending is the object (accusative) case, the form a noun takes when it is the thing being sought or acted upon.
ai.r: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, shield; to forgive, pardon

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: "and to You / and toward You" — wa- joins it on; ilā is the preposition 'to / toward,' and the attached -ka means 'You,' giving 'to You' (a direction or destination).
ai.g: A preposition ('to/toward') with an attached pronoun. The base ilā shifts to ilay- before a pronoun, and -ka means 'you' (one person addressed). Prepositions like this point to a direction or destination.
ai.r: — (preposition)

ai.m: Al-maṣīr — the destination, the place or state one finally comes to; the journey's end or ultimate outcome to which things return.
ai.g: A definite noun of place/result on the pattern mafʿil, with the long ī arising from the weak root letter yāʾ (ص-ي-ر). The final -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or what something ultimately is. The word denotes the final place or state to which one comes.
ai.r: ص-ي-ر (ṣ-y-r) — to become, come to, end up at

ai.m: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
ai.g: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

ai.m: "He imposes (a duty/burden) / He charges with" — to lay an obligation on someone, to require of them a task or responsibility, especially something demanding. The doubled middle consonant gives the sense of charging someone with a defined obligation.
ai.g: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), in a derived (intensive) form marked by the yu- prefix. The final -u ending marks the ordinary present, an action ongoing or general ('he imposes / he charges').
ai.r: ك-ل-ف (k-l-f) — to be charged with, burdened with, obligated

ai.m: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
ai.g: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
ai.r: — (proper divine name)

ai.m: A 'self' or 'soul' — the living person, the inner self, and by extension a human being or life. It can mean one's very self, one's soul, or simply 'a person/a life'.
ai.g: A feminine noun. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative case, which typically marks the word as the object of a verb ('a soul / a person' as the thing acted upon).
ai.r: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath, living being

ai.m: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
ai.g: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
ai.r: — (particle)

ai.m: A noun meaning 'its capacity', 'its scope', or 'what is within its power' — the full extent of ability or means that something possesses. From a word for room, breadth, or ability, with a possessive 'its'.
ai.g: A noun with the accusative -a ending, the case typically marking the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). The attached -hā means 'its' or 'her', so the whole means 'its capacity'. The accusative here signals it as what a verb falls upon.
ai.r: و-س-ع (w-s-ʿ) — to be wide, spacious, to have room or capacity

ai.m: 'For it / to it, belonging to it' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to a pronoun referring to a feminine singular thing; it expresses possession or benefit ('it has / it gets').
ai.g: Preposition 'li-' (here vowelled 'la-' before a pronoun) plus an attached object pronoun. The -hā suffix means 'it/her,' a feminine singular. Pronouns that follow a preposition are in the genitive (object-of-preposition) role; -hā is a fixed form and does not change shape.
ai.r: — (preposition + pronoun)

ai.m: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
ai.g: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

ai.m: 'It earned / acquired, gained' — said of deeds and their consequences; the root means to gain or acquire something, especially the moral 'earnings' of one's actions.
ai.g: Past-tense verb. The -t (sukūn-marked -at) suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject, 'she/it.' The past tense presents the action as completed.
ai.r: ك-س-ب (k-s-b) — to earn, acquire, gain (esp. deeds)

ai.m: "and upon it / and against it" — wa- joins it on; ʿalā is the preposition 'upon / on / against,' and -hā means 'it/her,' so 'upon it' — often in the sense of something counting against a person.
ai.g: A preposition ('upon/against') with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- before a pronoun, and -hā means 'it/her' (referring to a feminine or grammatically feminine thing). It conveys something resting on, or held against, that thing.
ai.r: — (preposition)

ai.m: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
ai.g: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

ai.m: "it earned / it acquired" — to gain or acquire something through one's own effort and deliberate action; the derived (eighth) form stresses personal, purposeful acquisition, often of what one is answerable for.
ai.g: A past-tense verb in a derived (reflexive-effort) form, with the suffix -at ('she/it,' feminine). Past tense shows a completed action ('it earned'); the -t marks a feminine singular doer.
ai.r: ك-س-ب (k-s-b) — to gain, earn, acquire by effort

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
ai.g: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

ai.m: "(do not) hold us to account / call us to reckoning" — to take someone to task, to seize and call them to answer for what they have done. The derived (mutual/intensive) form conveys confronting someone over their deeds.

p.en: take to task / call to account

ai.g: Present-tense verb, second-person masculine singular ('you'), in a derived (mutual/confrontational) form, with the object suffix -nā ('us'). The tu- prefix marks 'you (do)'; the bare final consonant (no end-vowel, sukūn on the ذ) is the shortened/jussive form, the form used after words like 'do not' or in requests; the -nā ending marks 'us' as the ones acted upon.
ai.r: ء-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize, grasp

ai.m: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
ai.g: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

ai.m: "we forgot / we have forgotten" — to fail to recall, to let something slip from the mind; can also carry the sense of neglecting or overlooking a duty.
ai.g: A past-tense verb with the subject suffix -nā meaning 'we.' Past tense presents the action as completed ('we forgot'); the -nā shows 'we' are the ones who did it.
ai.r: ن-س-ي (n-s-y) — to forget, to neglect, to overlook

ai.m: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
ai.g: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

ai.m: "we erred / we made a mistake" — to do wrong unintentionally, to miss the mark or slip into a fault without meaning to (as opposed to deliberate wrongdoing).
ai.g: A past-tense verb with the subject suffix -nā meaning 'we.' Past tense shows a completed action ('we erred'); the -nā marks 'we' as the doers.
ai.r: خ-ط-ء (kh-ṭ-ʾ) — to err, miss the mark, make a mistake

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
ai.g: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

ai.m: "(do not) lay / load / impose" — to carry or bear, and so to place a load or burden upon someone, to make them bear it.
ai.g: Present-tense verb, second-person masculine singular ('you'). The ta- prefix marks 'you (do),' and the bare final consonant (no end-vowel, -mil) is the shortened/jussive form, the form used after words like 'do not' or in requests and commands.
ai.r: ح-م-ل (ḥ-m-l) — to carry, bear, load

ai.m: 'Upon us' / 'over us' / 'against us' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, upon') with an attached 'us'. It conveys something resting on, incumbent upon, or bearing against the group.
ai.g: A preposition (ʿalā, 'upon/over') with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'us'). When a pronoun is attached, ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay-. Such prepositional phrases put their pronoun in the object/genitive role.

ai.m: "a heavy burden / a binding load" — a weight or obligation that presses down, often a severe, constraining duty or covenant that holds one back; sometimes a binding pledge.
ai.g: A singular noun, indefinite ('a burden'). The -an ending combines the object (accusative) case with indefiniteness ('a/some'); it marks the noun as the undefined thing being acted upon.
ai.r: ء-ص-ر (ʾ-ṣ-r) — to bind, confine; a heavy, binding burden

ai.m: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
ai.g: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

ai.m: "You laid it / You placed it (as a load)" — to carry or bear, and so to load it onto someone or make them carry it; the attached -hu ('it') is the burden placed.
ai.g: A past-tense verb with the subject suffix -ta ('you,' one male) and the object suffix -hu ('it'). Past tense shows a completed action ('you laid'); -ta marks 'you' as the doer and -hu marks 'it' as the thing laid.
ai.r: ح-م-ل (ḥ-m-l) — to carry, bear, load

ai.m: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
ai.g: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
ai.r: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

ai.m: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
ai.g: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

ai.m: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
ai.g: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
ai.r: — (preposition)

ai.m: "our before / (the time) before us" — qabl is 'before' in time, what came earlier; the attached -nā means 'us,' giving 'before us' (those who preceded us, or the time prior to ours).
ai.g: A time word ('before') with an attached pronoun. The -i ending is the genitive (possessive/'of') case, here because it follows a preposition; -nā means 'us.' Such words point to an earlier point in time.
ai.r: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; priorness, frontness

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
ai.g: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

ai.m: "(do not) make us bear / load upon us" — to make someone carry a load, to impose a burden and force them to bear it. The doubled middle consonant intensifies it to 'make/force to carry.'
ai.g: Present-tense verb, second-person masculine singular ('you'), in a derived (causative/intensive) form ('make to carry'), with the object suffix -nā ('us'). The tu- prefix marks 'you,' the bare final consonant (-mil, no end-vowel) is the shortened/jussive form used after 'do not' or in requests, and -nā marks 'us' as those acted upon.
ai.r: ح-م-ل (ḥ-m-l) — to carry, bear, load

ai.m: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
ai.g: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

ai.m: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
ai.g: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

ai.m: Strength, capacity, or the power to endure; the ability to bear or withstand something, the energy one can muster for a task.
ai.g: A feminine singular noun in the 'construct' state (iḍāfa), where it leans on a following noun ('strength OF / for …'). The tell-tale sign is that the final -a carries NO nunation: a free-standing accusative would normally take -an (tanwīn), so the bare -a without it marks the word as bound to what follows. The vowel itself is accusative, the form taken here as the noun governed in the 'no … whatsoever' negating construction with lā ('no strength to …').
ai.r: ط-و-ق (ṭ-w-q) — capacity, ability, the utmost one can bear

ai.m: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
ai.g: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

ai.m: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
ai.g: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

ai.m: "and pardon / and efface" — wa- joins it on; the verb means to pardon and wipe away an offence, to overlook it so completely that it leaves no trace (its root sense is 'to erase').
ai.g: A command/request verb addressed to one person ('pardon!'). It comes from a root whose last letter is a weak vowel, which is dropped in the command, leaving the final -u sound; it asks the one addressed to perform the act.
ai.r: ع-ف-و (ʿ-f-w) — to erase, efface; to pardon, excuse

ai.m: "from us / on our behalf" — ʿan is the preposition 'from / away from / concerning,' and the attached -nā means 'us,' giving 'from us' (often in the sense of pardoning faults away from us).
ai.g: A preposition ('from / away from') with the attached pronoun -nā ('us'). The n of ʿan blends into the n of -nā (written doubled). It conveys moving away from, or being concerning, the thing named.
ai.r: — (preposition)

ai.m: "and forgive / and cover over" — wa- joins it on; the verb means to forgive, to cover over and shield a sin so it is not exposed or held against the person.
ai.g: A command/request verb addressed to one person ('forgive!'). The bare consonant ending (-fir, no end-vowel) is the command form, and the helping vowel at the start (i-) lets the cluster be pronounced; it asks the one addressed to perform the act.
ai.r: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, shield; to forgive, pardon

ai.m: "for us / to us" — li is the preposition 'for / to,' marking benefit or recipient, and the attached -nā means 'us,' giving 'for us' (in our favour).
ai.g: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun -nā ('us'). The preposition li- is normally written with i, but takes the vowel 'a' (la-) before an attached pronoun. It marks the one who benefits or receives.
ai.r: — (preposition)

ai.m: A plea joined to what precedes it: 'and show us mercy / be merciful to us.' It is an appeal for Allah's compassion to be extended toward the speakers as a group.
ai.g: A command (imperative) verb: it requests or pleads for an action to be done. The bare, vowelless stem (rḥam) is the singular command form, addressed to one party. The attached -nā is the object pronoun 'us,' marking the speakers as those toward whom the action is directed. The opening wa- means 'and,' linking it to a preceding statement.
ai.r: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion, tenderness

ai.m: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
ai.g: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

ai.m: 'Our master / patron / protector.' Mawlā denotes one bound to another by a tie of loyalty and care — a guardian, lord, helper, or ally who is responsible for those under his charge; with the ending 'our,' it names such a one belonging to the speakers.
ai.g: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun: the final -nā means 'our,' marking the noun as belonging to the speakers as a group. The base mawlā is a noun built on the pattern of a place/agent of nearness and loyalty.
ai.r: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, guardianship, alliance, patronage

ai.m: A plea introduced by 'so/then': 'so grant us help / give us victory.' It asks for support and aid to be given to the speakers, especially the kind that brings triumph over an opponent.
ai.g: A command (imperative) verb: it requests an action. The bare, vowelless stem (nṣur) is the singular command, addressed to one party; the inner vowel u is characteristic of this verb's command form. The attached -nā is the object 'us,' marking the speakers as the recipients of the aid. The opening fa- means 'so' or 'then,' linking this request as a consequence of what came before.
ai.r: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — help, support, victory

ai.m: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
ai.g: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
ai.r: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

ai.m: 'The people / the folk' — a collective noun for a community, nation, or group of people regarded as a body. Often it carries the nuance of one's own people or a particular group sharing a trait.
ai.g: A collective noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-i' is the genitive ending, which typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship.
ai.r: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand/rise; a people, community

ai.m: 'The disbelievers / those who reject faith' — also 'those who cover up or are ungrateful.' It names people characterized by rejecting the truth and concealing or denying it, in contrast to those who believe.
ai.g: A definite plural noun: the prefix al- means 'the,' and the -īna ending marks a masculine 'sound' plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state — the form used when the word is an object of a verb or follows a preposition, as opposed to the subject form -ūna. It denotes many male persons (or a mixed group) of this description.
ai.r: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; hence to disbelieve, reject, be ungrateful

title: Let not our hearts deviate
situation: After reading the Qur'an's clear and allegorical verses, the people of knowledge pray that their hearts not swerve after being guided.
arabic: رَبَّنَا لَا تُزِغۡ قُلُوۡبَنَا بَعۡدَ اِذۡ هَدَيۡتَنَا وَهَبۡ لَنَا مِنۡ لَّدُنۡكَ رَحۡمَةً ​ ۚ اِنَّكَ اَنۡتَ الۡوَهَّابُ‏  رَبَّنَاۤ اِنَّكَ جَامِعُ النَّاسِ لِيَوۡمٍ لَّا رَيۡبَ فِيۡهِ​ؕ اِنَّ اللّٰهَ لَا يُخۡلِفُ الۡمِيۡعَادَ‏
translation: (8) ˹They say,˺ “Our Lord! Do not let our hearts deviate after you have guided us. Grant us Your mercy. You are indeed the Giver ˹of all bounties˺. (9) Our Lord! You will certainly gather all humanity for the ˹promised˺ Day—about which there is no doubt. Surely Allah does not break His promise.”
ai_translation: (8) “Our Rabb! Do not let our hearts deviate after you have guided us. Grant us Your mercy. You are indeed the Bestower of mercy. (9) Our Rabb! You will certainly gather all humanity for the Day—about which there is no doubt. Surely Allah does not break His promise.”

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.

ai.g: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

ai.m: To cause to swerve or deviate; to make a heart turn away from straightness and truth. The transitive counterpart of swerving — making something incline toward crookedness.
ai.g: A present/imperfect verb of the fourth (causative) form, meaning 'to make (something) swerve'. The tu- prefix marks a second-person singular ('you') or third-person feminine singular ('it/she') subject. The stem ends in a vowelless final consonant (jussive/clipped mood), the form that typically follows a negating or requesting particle such as 'do not …'.
ai.r: ز-ي-غ (z-y-gh) — to swerve, deviate, turn aside

ai.m: Our hearts. The base noun is the plural of qalb, the heart, understood not merely as the physical organ but as the seat of understanding, intention, feeling, and faith — the inner core of a person. With the attached possessive it means 'our hearts'.
ai.g: A plural noun carrying the -a (accusative) ending, which generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb or the subject of certain particles. The suffix -nā is a possessive pronoun meaning 'our' when attached to a noun (and 'us' when attached to a verb or preposition).
ai.r: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn over, turn about; hence 'heart' as that which turns and fluctuates

ai.m: After; following in time or order — the point or moment subsequent to something.
ai.g: An adverb of time functioning much like a preposition ('after'). It is fixed in the accusative form ending in -a, and is normally followed by a noun in the 'of' relationship, giving 'after (the) …'.
ai.r: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, that which comes later; distance/remoteness

ai.m: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
ai.g: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

ai.m: You have guided us. From a verb meaning to guide, to lead rightly, to show the way — especially guidance toward truth and right conduct. The form expresses a completed act of guiding directed by 'You' (a single addressee) toward 'us'.
ai.g: A past-tense (perfect) verb denoting a completed action. The -ta ending marks the doer as 'you' (a single masculine person being addressed). The suffix -nā here is the object 'us', so the whole says 'You guided us'.
ai.r: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead to the right way

ai.m: Grant! Bestow! A command from a verb meaning to give freely as a gift, to bestow without expectation of return. It conveys pure, gratuitous giving rather than payment or exchange.
ai.g: An imperative (command) addressed to a single person, asking them to give freely. The bare consonantal ending with a vowelless final letter is typical of the command form of this verb. The prefixed wa- means 'and', linking it to what precedes.
ai.r: و-ه-ب (w-h-b) — to give freely, to bestow as a gift

ai.m: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
ai.g: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

ai.m: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
ai.g: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
ai.r: — (preposition)

ai.m: From Yourself; from Your presence. The base word ladun means 'the presence of', 'the side of', or 'directly from' — pointing to something issuing straight from a source. Here it is preceded by the preposition min ('from'), whose final n assimilates into the following l so that the l is doubled. With the attached pronoun the whole conveys 'from Your own presence', stressing that what is given comes directly from the giver.

p.en: from (preposition; its n merges into the following l)
presence / nearness / 'from with' (doubled l from the merged n)

ai.g: An adverb of place/source ('at, by, in the presence of') joined to the attached pronoun -ka, 'your/you' for a single masculine addressee, together conveying 'from Your presence'. The initial l is written with a shadda (doubled): this gemination results from the preceding preposition min, whose final n assimilates into the l. The word implies immediacy of source — something coming directly from the one referred to.
ai.r: — (an adverbial particle of place; no triliteral verbal root)

ai.m: Mercy: compassion that actively does good — tenderness joined with the will and power to relieve, forgive, and benefit. As a noun it names an instance or measure of such mercy.
ai.g: An indefinite noun with the -an (accusative) ending, marked by tanwīn (the doubled-n sound). The accusative generally signals the word is a direct object or otherwise governed; the tanwīn marks it as indefinite — 'a mercy', 'some mercy'.
ai.r: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion, womb-like tenderness

ai.m: 'Indeed you' — an emphasis particle meaning 'truly / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'you', used to open a statement with certainty and stress about the person addressed.
ai.g: The emphasis particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with an attached pronoun. 'inna' adds strong assertion to a sentence and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The suffix '-ka' means 'you' (masculine singular) as its subject.

ai.m: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
ai.g: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

ai.m: The Bestower; the One who gives lavishly and repeatedly. An intensive form built from the verb 'to give freely', describing one whose giving is abundant, habitual, and generous without limit.
