ai.g: A definite noun (with 'the') in an intensive pattern that denotes one who does an action abundantly or by nature — here, one who gives lavishly. The final -u is the nominative ending, which typically marks the word as the subject or as a predicate naming the subject.
ai.r: و-ه-ب (w-h-b) — to give freely, to bestow as a gift

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: 'Indeed you' — an emphasis particle meaning 'truly / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'you', used to open a statement with certainty and stress about the person addressed.
ai.g: The emphasis particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with an attached pronoun. 'inna' adds strong assertion to a sentence and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The suffix '-ka' means 'you' (masculine singular) as its subject.

ai.m: Gatherer; the one who gathers, assembles, and brings together what was scattered. An active participle — a noun describing the doer of the act of gathering.
ai.g: An active participle (a 'doer' noun) meaning 'one who gathers'. The final -u is the nominative ending, typically marking a subject or predicate. Such a participle can also link to a following noun in a possessive-like construction ('gatherer of …'), in which case it conveys an act about to happen or characteristically done.
ai.r: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ) — to gather, collect, bring together

ai.m: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
ai.g: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
ai.r: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

ai.m: For a day; toward a day. The noun yawm means 'day' — a defined period or appointed time, often a momentous occasion. With the prefixed particle it means 'for / to / on a day', pointing toward an appointed time.
ai.g: A noun preceded by the preposition li- ('for, to'). Because it follows a preposition, it takes the -i (genitive) ending, here with tanwīn (the doubled-n sound) marking it indefinite: '-in' = 'for a day'. The genitive is the case regularly required after prepositions.
ai.r: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a span of time

ai.m: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
ai.g: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

ai.m: Doubt, suspicion, disquieting uncertainty — the kind of wavering that unsettles the heart, stronger than a passing question. It names the state of not being at rest about whether something is true.
ai.g: A masculine singular noun shown with an -a ending and no tanwin. This is the accusative (mansub) noun governed by the negating particle la — its ism — taking a bare form to express absolute negation, conveying that the whole category is ruled out ('there is no doubt whatsoever').
ai.r: ر-ي-ب (r-y-b) — doubt, disquiet

ai.m: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
ai.g: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

ai.m: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
ai.g: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

ai.m: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
ai.g: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
ai.r: — (proper name)

ai.m: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
ai.g: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

ai.m: He breaks / fails to keep (a promise); He goes back on or leaves unfulfilled. From a verb whose core sense is 'to come after / be left behind', in this form meaning to default on a pledge or fail to deliver what was promised.
ai.g: A present/future-tense verb. The yu- prefix marks the doer as 'he' (third-person masculine singular) and, in this vowel pattern, indicates a causative-type form. The final -u is the indicative ending, which marks the plain factual present ('he does / will do'), as opposed to moods that drop or change that vowel.
ai.r: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to come after, succeed, be behind; hence to break a promise (leave it behind unfulfilled)

ai.m: The appointment / the appointed promise or time; a fixed tryst — a settled commitment as to when (or where) something will occur. It names the promised meeting or deadline itself.
ai.g: A definite noun (with 'the') on a pattern denoting the time, place, or instrument of an action — here the appointed time/promise. The final -a is the accusative ending, generally marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
ai.r: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise, to appoint a time

title: Forgive us our sins
situation: Surah Aal Imran describes them as those who, amid the temptations of the world, turn to God admitting their faith and begging forgiveness.
arabic: اَلَّذِيۡنَ يَقُوۡلُوۡنَ رَبَّنَاۤ اِنَّنَاۤ اٰمَنَّا فَاغۡفِرۡ لَنَا ذُنُوۡبَنَا وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ​ۚ‏
translation: who pray, “Our Lord! We have believed, so forgive our sins and protect us from the torment of the Fire.”
ai_translation: Say, “Shall I inform you of what is better than this? Those who live with taqwa will have Gardens with their Rabb under which rivers flow, to stay there forever, and pure spouses, along with Allah’s pleasure.” And Allah is All-Seeing of servants, who pray, “Our Rabb! We have believed, so forgive our sins and protect us from the torment of the Fire.”

ai.m: Those who / the ones who — a plural relative pronoun (masculine) introducing a description: 'those (people) who …'.
ai.g: A relative pronoun, masculine plural, meaning 'those who / the ones who'. It refers back to a group already in view and introduces a clause describing them. Its form is fixed and does not change for case.
ai.r: — (relative pronoun; no triliteral root)

ai.m: 'They say / they keep saying' — a present-tense verb of speaking: to say, utter, or assert in words.
ai.g: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), from a hollow (middle-vowel) root. The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are saying.'
ai.r: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — speech; saying, uttering, asserting

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: 'Indeed we …' — an emphatic opener that combines a particle of strong affirmation ('truly, certainly') with the pronoun 'we', stressing and confirming the statement that follows about the speakers.
ai.g: The emphatic particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with the attached pronoun '-nā' ('we'). 'Inna' introduces a sentence and lends it certainty and emphasis, while '-nā' is its subject, identifying the speakers as 'we'. This is the fuller, uncontracted form (innanā) of the commonly contracted innā; the extra nūn belongs to the longer pronominal base used to keep the doubled nūn of 'inna' and the nūn of the pronoun distinct rather than merged.
ai.r: — (particle of emphasis; no triliteral root)

ai.m: We have believed; we have come to faith and trust — to affirm belief, give one's trust, and feel secure in that conviction, stated by a group about themselves.
ai.g: A past-tense verb on the form-IV pattern (āmana, 'to believe / to have faith'). The ending -nā (a single morpheme, نَا) attached to a past verb marks the subject as 'we'. The doubled 'n' heard in 'āmannā' comes from the verb stem's final 'n' meeting the 'n' that begins the -nā ending.
ai.r: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

ai.m: 'So forgive!' — a command to pardon and cover over wrongdoing, to wipe away faults; when addressed to Allah it is a plea, 'forgive us'. The opening 'so/then' links it to a preceding reason.
ai.g: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single person, prefixed by 'fa-' ('so, then'), which connects it to something previously stated as its cause. The verb's bare, vowel-less ending (-ir, with no added vowel) is the form a direct order takes. To 'forgive' here carries the root sense of covering over and concealing a fault.
ai.r: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — covering over, pardoning, forgiveness

ai.m: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
ai.g: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

ai.m: Our sins — wrongdoings or offences attributed to 'us'; the plural 'sins/faults' joined to the speakers.
ai.g: A masculine plural noun ('sins') with the attached possessive pronoun '-nā' ('our'). The -a ending before the pronoun is accusative, the case typically used for the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon — e.g. that which is forgiven or removed).
ai.r: ذ-ن-ب (dh-n-b) — sin, offence, fault

ai.m: 'And guard us / shield us' — a connector 'and' plus a command to protect, preserve, and ward off harm; when addressed to Allah, a plea to be kept safe from something.
ai.g: A command (imperative) verb 'guard/protect', preceded by the connector 'wa' ('and') and followed by the object pronoun '-nā' ('us'). The verb comes from a root whose weak letters are dropped in the command, leaving the very short 'qi'. It governs 'us' as the one being protected.
ai.r: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — guarding, shielding, protection

ai.m: Torment, punishment, or chastisement — severe, painful suffering imposed as a penalty.
ai.g: A singular noun. The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case, the form used for a direct object of a verb, or for the first noun of a possessive pair ('the punishment of …') when that whole phrase is itself an object.
ai.r: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to torment, punish

ai.m: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
ai.g: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').
ai.r: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — fire, blaze, burning

title: Grant me pure offspring
situation: Seeing the miraculous provision God gave Maryam in the sanctuary, the aged Zakariya was moved to ask God for a righteous child.
arabic: هُنَالِكَ دَعَا زَكَرِيَّا رَبَّهٗ​ ​ۚ قَالَ رَبِّ هَبۡ لِىۡ مِنۡ لَّدُنۡكَ ذُرِّيَّةً طَيِّبَةً​ ​ ۚ اِنَّكَ سَمِيۡعُ الدُّعَآءِ‏
translation: Then and there Zachariah prayed to his Lord, saying, “My Lord! Grant me—by your grace—righteous offspring. You are certainly the Hearer of ˹all˺ prayers.”
ai_translation: Then and there Zachariah prayed to his Rabb, saying, “My Rabb! Grant me—by your grace—righteous offspring. You are certainly the Hearer of prayers.”

ai.m: An adverb meaning 'there' or 'at that point' — pointing to a distant place, and by extension to a particular moment or set of circumstances ('right then and there').
ai.g: A demonstrative adverb of place built from hunā ('there') plus the suffix -lika that signals farness, giving 'over there / yonder'. It is a fixed (indeclinable) word with no changing case ending, and can point to a time or situation as well as a place.
ai.r: — (demonstrative adverb)

ai.m: A past-tense verb meaning 'he called upon' or 'he prayed / invoked' — to appeal to someone, to summon, or to make supplication.
ai.g: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he called / invoked'. This root ends in a weak letter, so the final root letter appears as the long -ā vowel; it marks a completed action by a single male subject.
ai.r: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — calling, summoning, supplicating

ai.m: Zakariyyā — the proper name of the Prophet Zachariah; a personal name and so without a derived meaning.
ai.g: A proper name (of a person). It ends in a fixed long -ā and does not change its ending for grammatical case; its role is understood from context.

ai.m: The noun 'Lord' joined to a 'his' pronoun — 'his Lord'. Rabb conveys the Master and Sustainer who owns, nurtures, and brings a thing to its full development; far richer than 'lord' alone.
ai.g: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun -hu ('his'). The -a ending is accusative, the case used when the noun is an object of a verb or otherwise governed into that case; -hu means it belongs to 'him'.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, ownership, nurturing and sustaining to completion

ai.m: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
ai.g: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
ai.r: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
ai.g: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: A command meaning 'grant!' or 'bestow!' — a request to give or confer something as a gift, typically addressed to Allah in supplication.
ai.g: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a single person: 'grant!'. The verb's weak first root letter drops in the command form, leaving the short, vowel-less ending — the standard shape of a direct request to one addressee.
ai.r: و-ه-ب (w-h-b) — giving freely, bestowing a gift

ai.m: 'to Me' or 'for Me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the first-person pronoun, expressing direction, benefit, or belonging toward the speaker.
ai.g: A preposition ('to/for') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me'). Together they express benefit, direction, or attribution toward the first person.

ai.m: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
ai.g: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
ai.r: — (preposition)

ai.m: From Yourself; from Your presence. The base word ladun means 'the presence of', 'the side of', or 'directly from' — pointing to something issuing straight from a source. Here it is preceded by the preposition min ('from'), whose final n assimilates into the following l so that the l is doubled. With the attached pronoun the whole conveys 'from Your own presence', stressing that what is given comes directly from the giver.

p.en: from (preposition; its n merges into the following l)
presence / nearness / 'from with' (doubled l from the merged n)

ai.g: An adverb of place/source ('at, by, in the presence of') joined to the attached pronoun -ka, 'your/you' for a single masculine addressee, together conveying 'from Your presence'. The initial l is written with a shadda (doubled): this gemination results from the preceding preposition min, whose final n assimilates into the l. The word implies immediacy of source — something coming directly from the one referred to.
ai.r: — (an adverbial particle of place; no triliteral verbal root)

ai.m: Offspring, progeny, descendants — the children and seed of a person, a line of descent. It is a collective noun covering one's posterity.
ai.g: A collective/feminine noun ending in the rounded tā' marbūṭa. When the case ending is voiced, the tā' marbūṭa is pronounced as 't', so the ending sounds '-tan': the -t- of the feminine marker plus -an (tanwīn-fatḥ). The -an marks it indefinite and accusative — 'a progeny / offspring' as a direct object or complement; the doubled-n (tanwīn) signals indefiniteness ('a/some').
ai.r: ذ-ر-ر (dh-r-r) — to scatter/multiply; hence scattered seed, progeny

ai.m: An adjective meaning 'good', 'pure', or 'wholesome' (describing a feminine noun) — that which is fine, sound, agreeable, and untainted, whether in substance, character, or speech.
ai.g: A feminine singular adjective ('good / pure'). The final -tan ending combines the feminine marker with 'tanwīn' (the -n sound marking an indefinite noun, 'a …') in the accusative case, which typically marks it as a direct object or describes such a noun.
ai.r: ط-ي-ب (ṭ-y-b) — goodness, purity, wholesomeness

ai.m: 'Indeed you' — an emphasis particle meaning 'truly / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'you', used to open a statement with certainty and stress about the person addressed.
ai.g: The emphasis particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with an attached pronoun. 'inna' adds strong assertion to a sentence and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The suffix '-ka' means 'you' (masculine singular) as its subject.

ai.m: An intensive descriptive noun meaning 'All-Hearing' or 'ever-hearing' — one who hears fully, constantly, and perfectly; as a divine attribute, the One who hears every sound and supplication.
ai.g: An intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, conveying constant, abundant hearing. The final -u vowel is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate that describes the subject ('… is all-hearing').
ai.r: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — hearing, listening

ai.m: A noun meaning 'the calling', 'the supplication', or 'the prayer of request' — the act of calling upon Allah, appealing, or invoking.
ai.g: A definite verbal noun ('the supplication'), marked by the prefix al- ('the'). The final -i vowel is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF supplication') or follows a preposition.
ai.r: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — calling, supplicating

title: Write us among the witnesses
situation: Declaring their belief in the revelation and in following the messenger, they asked to be recorded among those who bear witness to the truth.
arabic: رَبَّنَاۤ اٰمَنَّا بِمَاۤ اَنۡزَلۡتَ وَاتَّبَعۡنَا الرَّسُوۡلَ فَاكۡتُبۡنَا مَعَ الشّٰهِدِيۡنَ‏
translation: ˹They prayed to Allah,˺ “Our Lord! We believe in Your revelations and follow the messenger, so count us among those who bear witness.”
ai_translation: “Our Rabb! We believe in Your revelations and follow the messenger, so count us among those who bear witness.”

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: We have believed; we have come to faith and trust — to affirm belief, give one's trust, and feel secure in that conviction, stated by a group about themselves.
ai.g: A past-tense verb on the form-IV pattern (āmana, 'to believe / to have faith'). The ending -nā (a single morpheme, نَا) attached to a past verb marks the subject as 'we'. The doubled 'n' heard in 'āmannā' comes from the verb stem's final 'n' meeting the 'n' that begins the -nā ending.
ai.r: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

ai.m: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
ai.g: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.
ai.r: — (particle + relative pronoun)

ai.m: 'You sent down / You revealed' — to cause something to descend from a higher place to a lower one; used especially of Allah sending down revelation, addressed to a single 'You'.
ai.g: A completed-action (past-tense) verb on the 'afʿala' pattern, which carries a causative sense ('to make come down'). The ending -ta marks the second-person masculine singular doer ('you' — one male) who completed the act: 'You sent down'.
ai.r: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, to come/send down

ai.m: 'And we followed / and we follow' — to go after, pursue, and conform to someone or something, taking it as a guide or example.
ai.g: wa- is 'and'. The stem is a completed-action (past-tense) verb on the 'iftaʿala' pattern, which adds a sense of doing something for oneself or diligently ('to follow closely, to adopt as a guide'). The ending -nā marks 'we' as the doer: 'and we followed'.
ai.r: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, to come after, to pursue

ai.m: The messenger, envoy, or emissary: one who is sent with a message; in the Qur'an typically a prophet sent by Allah bearing revelation to a people.
ai.g: A noun on the form faʿūl (an intensive/agent pattern, 'one sent'), prefixed with al- ('the'). The final -a ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb ('… the messenger') or the subject of certain particles. The 'l' of al- assimilates into the following 'r' (a 'sun letter'), pronounced ar-rasūl.
ai.r: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching a message

ai.m: 'So write us / so record us / so enroll us' — a plea that the speakers be registered or inscribed (e.g., among a named group).
ai.g: fa- is a connector 'so/then', often drawing a consequence. The stem is a command (imperative) verb addressed to a single person ('you write/record'), the bare unsuffixed form marking the singular addressee. The final -nā is the object pronoun 'us': 'so record us'.
ai.r: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write, to inscribe, to ordain/record

ai.m: With, together with, alongside — indicating company, accompaniment, or being in the same place or time as another.
ai.g: A preposition of accompaniment ('with, alongside'); grammatically it is an adverbial of place/time (ẓarf) that governs the genitive. It is placed before a following noun to put one thing in the company of another, and that following noun stands in the genitive. The -a is its fixed ending.

ai.m: 'The witnesses / those who testify' — people who observe and bear testimony, affirming the truth of something.
ai.g: al- is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following 'sh', heard as ash-shā…). The active participle shāhid ('one who witnesses') takes the sound masculine plural ending -īna, which makes it plural and marks the accusative/genitive case — typically the object of a verb, or the object of a preposition, or part of a possessive phrase.
ai.r: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, to testify, to be present

title: Forgive our excesses and make us firm
who: The devoted men who fought alongside earlier prophets
situation: In the face of battle their only words were a prayer for forgiveness of their sins and excesses, for firm footing, and for victory over the disbelievers.
arabic: وَمَا كَانَ قَوۡلَهُمۡ اِلَّاۤ اَنۡ قَالُوۡا رَبَّنَا اغۡفِرۡ لَنَا ذُنُوۡبَنَا وَاِسۡرَافَنَا فِىۡۤ اَمۡرِنَا وَ ثَبِّتۡ اَقۡدَامَنَا وَانۡصُرۡنَا عَلَى الۡقَوۡمِ الۡكٰفِرِيۡنَ‏
translation: And all they said was, “Our Lord! Forgive our sins and excesses, make our steps firm, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people.”
ai_translation: And all they said was, “Our Rabb! Forgive our sins and excesses, make our steps firm, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people.”

ai.m: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
ai.g: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
ai.r: — (relative pronoun / particle)

ai.m: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

p.en: to be, was, used to be

ai.g: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.
ai.r: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence; to be

ai.m: Their saying or speech — the words they uttered. It names a particular statement or utterance belonging to a group.
ai.g: A noun ('saying') carrying the -a ending, which is the accusative case — typically marking the direct object of a verb ('… the saying') or the subject of certain particles. The attached -hum means 'their', so it reads 'their saying'.
ai.r: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

ai.m: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
ai.g: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
ai.r: — (particle)

ai.m: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
ai.g: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
ai.r: — (particle; no root)

ai.m: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
ai.g: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.
ai.r: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, utterance

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: Forgive! — a plea or command to pardon, to cover over and blot out wrongdoing. It carries the sense of veiling a fault so it is no longer held against the offender.
ai.g: A command (imperative) addressed to a single person: 'forgive!'. The vowelless final -r reflects the imperative form. It is commonly followed by 'us' or 'for me' to specify whom to pardon.
ai.r: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, conceal, and pardon; mercy that blots out sin

ai.m: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
ai.g: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

ai.m: Our sins — wrongdoings or offences attributed to 'us'; the plural 'sins/faults' joined to the speakers.
ai.g: A masculine plural noun ('sins') with the attached possessive pronoun '-nā' ('our'). The -a ending before the pronoun is accusative, the case typically used for the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon — e.g. that which is forgiven or removed).
ai.r: ذ-ن-ب (dh-n-b) — sin, offence, fault

ai.m: And our going to excess — our overstepping of due limits, immoderation, or squandering. 'Isrāf' is exceeding the bounds of what is right or measured.
ai.g: A verbal noun ('going to excess') with the -a ending marking the accusative case — typically the direct object of a verb ('… our excess'). The attached -nā means 'our', and the leading wa- means 'and'.
ai.r: س-ر-ف (s-r-f) — to exceed proper limits, to be extravagant or wasteful

ai.m: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
ai.g: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
ai.r: — (particle)

ai.m: Our affair, matter, command, or concern — that which we are dealing with or commanded to do. 'Amr' spans both a 'matter/situation' and a 'command/order'.
ai.g: A noun ('affair') with the -i ending, the genitive case — which typically links it to a preceding noun or follows a preposition ('… of our affair' / 'in our affair'). The attached -nā means 'our'.
ai.r: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command; also 'matter, affair, situation'

ai.m: And make firm! / make steady! — a plea or command to plant something firmly, to keep it steadfast and unshaken. Used of steadying feet, hearts, or resolve.
ai.g: A command (imperative) to a single person in the intensive 'fa''ala' pattern (to fix firmly), 'make firm / keep steadfast!'. The vowelless ending -t marks the imperative. The leading wa- means 'and'.
ai.r: ث-ب-ت (th-b-t) — to be firm, fixed, steadfast, established

ai.m: 'Our feet' — the plural of qadam (foot), made possessive by an attached 'our'. By extension 'making the feet firm' is an idiom for granting steadfastness and stability.
ai.g: A broken (irregular) plural noun + the possessive suffix '-nā' ('our'). The '-a' before the suffix is the accusative ending, which here marks the noun as the direct object — the thing being acted upon — while '-nā' shows it belongs to 'us'.
ai.r: ق-د-م (q-d-m) — to precede/advance; foot, step

ai.m: 'And help us! / give us victory! / aid us!' — a command to come to someone's aid and grant them support and triumph, with 'us' as the one helped.
ai.g: Connective 'wa-' ('and') + a command verb addressed to a single male ('you, help!') + the object pronoun '-nā' ('us'). The initial alif is a prosthetic helping vowel (hamzat al-waṣl), added to begin this form I command whose stem starts with a vowel-less consonant; it drops in pronunciation when joined to a preceding word. The stem vowel is left vowel-less (jussive) as is normal for an order, and '-nā' is the one receiving the help.
ai.r: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, aid, grant victory

ai.m: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
ai.g: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
ai.r: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

ai.m: 'The people / the folk' — a collective noun for a community, nation, or group of people regarded as a body. Often it carries the nuance of one's own people or a particular group sharing a trait.
ai.g: A collective noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-i' is the genitive ending, which typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship.
ai.r: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand/rise; a people, community

ai.m: The disbelievers / the ungrateful — those who reject faith and cover over the truth; the word also carries the sense of covering up or being ungrateful for what one has been given.
ai.g: 'al-' is 'the'. The stem is an active participle ('one who disbelieves/is ungrateful') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the accusative/genitive form of the sound masculine plural: it marks the word as an object of a verb or as governed by a preposition, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
ai.r: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; ingratitude, disbelief

title: You did not create this in vain
situation: Those who remember God standing, sitting, and lying down, and who reflect on the creation of the heavens and earth until it moves them to this long, humble prayer.
arabic: الَّذِيۡنَ يَذۡكُرُوۡنَ اللّٰهَ قِيَامًا وَّقُعُوۡدًا وَّعَلٰى جُنُوۡبِهِمۡ وَيَتَفَكَّرُوۡنَ فِىۡ خَلۡقِ السَّمٰوٰتِ وَالۡاَرۡضِ​ۚ رَبَّنَا مَا خَلَقۡتَ هٰذَا بَاطِلًا ۚ سُبۡحٰنَكَ فَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ‏  رَبَّنَاۤ اِنَّكَ مَنۡ تُدۡخِلِ النَّارَ فَقَدۡ اَخۡزَيۡتَهٗ ​ؕ وَمَا لِلظّٰلِمِيۡنَ مِنۡ اَنۡصَارٍ‏  رَبَّنَاۤ اِنَّنَا سَمِعۡنَا مُنَادِيًا يُّنَادِىۡ لِلۡاِيۡمَانِ اَنۡ اٰمِنُوۡا بِرَبِّكُمۡ فَاٰمَنَّا  ۖ رَبَّنَا فَاغۡفِرۡ لَنَا ذُنُوۡبَنَا وَكَفِّرۡ عَنَّا سَيِّاٰتِنَا وَتَوَفَّنَا مَعَ الۡاَبۡرَارِ​ۚ‏  رَبَّنَا وَاٰتِنَا مَا وَعَدتَّنَا عَلٰى رُسُلِكَ وَلَا تُخۡزِنَا يَوۡمَ الۡقِيٰمَةِ ​ؕ اِنَّكَ لَا تُخۡلِفُ الۡمِيۡعَادَ‏
translation: (191) ˹They are˺ those who remember Allah while standing, sitting, and lying on their sides, and reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth ˹and pray˺, “Our Lord! You have not created ˹all of˺ this without purpose. Glory be to You! Protect us from the torment of the Fire. (192) Our Lord! Indeed, those You commit to the Fire will be ˹completely˺ disgraced! And the wrongdoers will have no helpers. (193) Our Lord! We have heard the caller to ˹true˺ belief, ˹proclaiming,˺ ‘Believe in your Lord ˹alone˺,’ so we believed. Our Lord! Forgive our sins, absolve us of our misdeeds, and allow us ˹each˺ to die as one of the virtuous. (194) Our Lord! Grant us what You have promised us through Your messengers and do not put us to shame on Judgment Day—for certainly You never fail in Your promise.”
ai_translation: (191) Those who remember Allah while standing, sitting, and lying on their sides, and reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth, “Our Rabb! You have not created this without purpose. Glory be to You! Protect us from the torment of the Fire. (192) Our Rabb! Indeed, those You commit to the Fire will be disgraced! And the wrongdoers will have no helpers. (193) Our Rabb! We have heard the caller to belief, ‘Believe in your Rabb,’ so we believed. Our Rabb! Forgive our sins, absolve us of our misdeeds, and allow us to die as one of the virtuous. (194) Our Rabb! Grant us what You have promised us through Your messengers and do not put us to shame on Judgment Day—for certainly You never fail in Your promise.”

ai.m: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
ai.g: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

ai.m: 'They remember / make mention of,' i.e., to call to mind, invoke, or mention — both inward recollection and outward utterance, often of Allah.
ai.g: A present-tense verb. The -ūna ending marks a plural masculine subject ('they') and signals the ordinary (indicative) present tense — an ongoing or habitual remembering and mentioning.
ai.r: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind

ai.m: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
ai.g: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
ai.r: — (proper name)

ai.m: 'Standing / standing upright' — the verbal noun of standing, here describing a state ('while standing'). It can also carry the sense of being upright or steadfast.
ai.g: A singular verbal noun (maṣdar) — the action-noun of standing — used here to describe a state. The -an ending is accusative and indefinite, functioning to describe the manner or circumstance in which something is done ('while standing'). It answers 'how?' or 'in what state?'
ai.r: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, be upright

ai.m: 'And sitting / seated' — the verbal noun of sitting, here describing a state ('while sitting'). The leading 'wa-' means 'and.'
ai.g: A singular verbal noun (maṣdar) — the action-noun of sitting — preceded by wa- ('and'), used here to describe a state. The -an ending is accusative and indefinite, functioning to describe the manner or circumstance ('while sitting'). It answers 'how?' or 'in what state?'
ai.r: ق-ع-د (q-ʿ-d) — to sit, be seated, remain

ai.m: 'And upon / on,' a combination of 'and' with the preposition meaning 'on, upon, over' — indicating resting on a surface, or an obligation/duty laid upon someone.
ai.g: The connector wa- ('and') joined to the preposition ʿalā ('on/upon'). As a preposition, it places whatever noun follows it into the genitive case and conveys position upon, or a duty resting on, something.
ai.r: — (preposition; no triliteral root)

ai.m: 'Their sides / flanks' — the parts of the body along which a person lies down. With the attached pronoun it means 'their sides.'
ai.g: A masculine broken (irregular) plural noun with the attached pronoun -him ('their'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, here because the word follows a preposition and is also possessed ('… of their sides' / 'their sides'). The attached -him marks a plural possessor, 'their.'
ai.r: ج-ن-ب (j-n-b) — side, flank; to be beside

ai.m: 'And they ponder / reflect deeply,' i.e., to think over something attentively, turning it about in the mind to draw out meaning. The leading 'wa-' means 'and.'
ai.g: A present-tense verb (form V, which adds the sense of doing something to/for oneself — here sustained inner thought) preceded by wa- ('and'). The -ūna ending marks a plural masculine subject ('they') and signals the ordinary (indicative) present tense — ongoing or habitual reflection.
ai.r: ف-ك-ر (f-k-r) — to think, ponder, reflect

ai.m: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
ai.g: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
ai.r: — (particle)

ai.m: Creation / the act of creating — the bringing of things into existence, or the created order that results; also denotes how something is fashioned or formed.
ai.g: A verbal noun ('creating / creation'). The final -i is the genitive case ending: it typically links the word to a following noun ('the creation OF …') or follows a preposition.
ai.r: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — creating, originating, fashioning

ai.m: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
ai.g: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.
ai.r: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, sky

ai.m: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
ai.g: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.
ai.r: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
ai.g: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

ai.m: 'You created / brought into being.' The verb means to create, to originate and shape something out of nothing, addressed to a single 'you.'
ai.g: A past-tense verb. The -ta ending marks the subject as 'you' (masculine singular) — the one addressed performed the act. It describes a completed act of creating.
ai.r: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — to create, originate, fashion

ai.m: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
ai.g: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

ai.m: 'In vain, falsely, without purpose' — that which is futile, baseless, or empty of truth; the opposite of what is true and well-founded.
ai.g: An active participle/noun meaning 'something false or futile.' The -an ending is accusative and indefinite, here typically describing the manner or purpose of an action ('in vain, for nothing'). It answers 'how?' or 'to what end?'
ai.r: ب-ط-ل (b-ṭ-l) — to be false, vain, void, futile

ai.m: 'Glory be to You / how far above all flaw You are' — a set exclamation declaring Allah utterly free of any imperfection, partner, or unworthy attribute, paired with 'You.'
ai.g: A verbal noun, subḥān ('glorification, utter freedom from imperfection'), bound to the attached pronoun -ka, 'You/Your' (one masculine addressee). It stands in the accusative (-a ending) as the exclamatory object of an understood verb ('I declare Your absolute glory') — a fixed formula of praise.
ai.r: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — glorifying, declaring (Allah) free of all imperfection

ai.m: An appeal: 'so guard us / protect us, shield us.' The verb is a plea to be safeguarded from harm. The leading 'fa-' adds 'so/then,' and 'us' is the object of protection.
ai.g: A command (imperative) verb from a root with a weak letter, reduced to a short form, with the prefixed fa- ('so/then'). It is a direct request — when addressed to Allah it carries the force of supplication ('protect us'). The attached -nā means 'us' as the ones to be guarded.
ai.r: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, protect, shield (the root of taqwā)

ai.m: Torment, punishment, or chastisement — severe, painful suffering imposed as a penalty.
ai.g: A singular noun. The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case, the form used for a direct object of a verb, or for the first noun of a possessive pair ('the punishment of …') when that whole phrase is itself an object.
ai.r: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to torment, punish

ai.m: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
ai.g: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').
ai.r: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — fire, blaze, burning

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: 'Indeed you' — an emphasis particle meaning 'truly / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'you', used to open a statement with certainty and stress about the person addressed.
ai.g: The emphasis particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with an attached pronoun. 'inna' adds strong assertion to a sentence and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The suffix '-ka' means 'you' (masculine singular) as its subject.

ai.m: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
ai.g: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.
ai.r: — (pronoun)

ai.m: 'You admit / cause to enter, bring in.' The verb means to make something or someone go into a place. This is the causative sense, addressed to a single 'you.'

p.en: you cause to enter (present tense, form IV, 'you')

ai.g: A present-tense causative verb (form IV) addressed to 'you' (masculine singular), here in the shortened (jussive) mood, which for a sound verb ends in a silent sukūn (تُدۡخِلۡ, no case vowel). The final short -i is not part of the verb's mood: it is a helping kasra inserted only to break the awkward consonant cluster that forms when this silent ending meets a following word beginning with a connective hamza. It is purely a smoothing vowel of pronunciation. The verb means 'to cause to enter / admit.'
ai.r: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — to enter, go in

ai.m: 'The Fire' — fire as a blazing element, and by extension the well-known fire of punishment. The definite article makes it 'the Fire,' a specific, recognized fire rather than fire in general.
ai.g: A definite noun ('the' + 'fire'), feminine. The article's lām assimilates into the following 'n' (shown by the doubling on nār). The final -a is the accusative case ending, which typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon) or the object of certain particles.
ai.r: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — to give light, shine, illuminate (the noun nār, 'fire,' derives from this sense of light/blaze)

ai.m: A two-part connector: fa- means 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking what follows as a result or consequence; qad before a past-tense verb intensifies it, conveying 'certainly', 'indeed', or 'already' — stressing that the action has truly and definitely occurred.
ai.g: fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so' or 'then', often marking a result. qad is a particle of emphasis; placed before a completed (past-tense) verb it affirms that the action has definitely or already happened. Neither part takes a case ending.

ai.m: 'You have disgraced him / put him to shame, humiliated him.' The verb means to bring disgrace, abasement, or ignominy upon someone, with 'him' as the object.
ai.g: A past-tense causative verb (form IV) from a root with a weak letter. The -ta ending marks the subject as 'you' (masculine singular), and the attached -hu means 'him' as the one disgraced. It describes a completed act of shaming or humiliating.
ai.r: خ-ز-ي (kh-z-y) — to be disgraced, humiliated, put to shame

ai.m: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
ai.g: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
ai.r: — (relative pronoun / particle)

ai.m: A prepositional phrase, 'for/to the wrongdoers' — al-ẓālimūn being those who do wrong or injustice, who put things out of their rightful place; in religious usage especially those who wrong their own souls through disbelief or transgression.
ai.g: A definite active participle (a 'doer' noun, 'those who wrong') in the masculine plural, governed by the preposition li- ('for, to'). The plural ending -īna is the genitive/accusative plural form, required here after the preposition. The single written lām after li- is the definite article 'the', its own letter merged into the preposition.
ai.r: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to do wrong, oppress; injustice

ai.m: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
ai.g: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
ai.r: — (preposition)

ai.m: Helpers, supporters, defenders — those who come to one's aid and rally to one's side, particularly in a cause.
ai.g: A broken (internally restructured) plural noun, 'helpers'. The ending -in is the indefinite genitive marker (tanwīn). The genitive typically follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun ('... of ...'); the doubled-n sound ('nunation') signals that it is indefinite ('helpers / any helpers').
ai.r: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, aid, give victory

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: 'Indeed we …' — an emphatic opener that combines a particle of strong affirmation ('truly, certainly') with the pronoun 'we', stressing and confirming the statement that follows about the speakers.
ai.g: The emphatic particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with the attached pronoun '-nā' ('we'). 'Inna' introduces a sentence and lends it certainty and emphasis, while '-nā' is its subject, identifying the speakers as 'we'. This is the fuller, uncontracted form (innanā) of the commonly contracted innā; the extra nūn belongs to the longer pronominal base used to keep the doubled nūn of 'inna' and the nūn of the pronoun distinct rather than merged.
ai.r: — (particle of emphasis; no triliteral root)

ai.m: A past-tense verb meaning 'we heard / we listened' — the act of perceiving sound or a message, often carrying the further nuance of heeding or taking in what was said.
ai.g: A completed (past-tense) verb. The attached ending -nā marks the subject as 'we', so the action is something a group did and finished: 'we heard'.
ai.r: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — hearing, listening

ai.m: An active participle meaning 'one who calls out, an announcer, a herald' — a person who proclaims or summons others with a raised voice.

p.en: accusative ('-an') ending, with tanwīn marking it indefinite

ai.g: An active participle (the doer of the action) from Form III. The final -an is the accusative case with tanwīn ('a/an'): it marks the word as an indefinite object of a verb, or as a state/circumstance describing someone.
ai.r: ن-د-و / ن-د-ي (n-d-w/y) — to call out, summon, proclaim

ai.m: A present-tense verb meaning 'he calls out, he summons, he proclaims' — the act of calling to someone, often from a distance or with announcement.
ai.g: An imperfect (present/future) verb in Form III. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). The final -ī is the verb's weak third root letter (from ن-د-و/ي), which is fully retained here; that retention is the mark of the indicative mood, since the subjunctive adds a vowel to it (يُنَادِيَ) and the jussive drops it entirely (يُنَادِ).
ai.r: ن-د-و / ن-د-ي (n-d-w/y) — to call out, summon, proclaim

ai.m: To / toward faith — 'īmān' is inner belief and trusting acceptance: to affirm and have faith in Allah, His messengers, and His revelation, with the heart's security and commitment.
ai.g: A verbal noun (Form IV, the act/state of believing) with two prefixes: 'li-' ('to/for') and the article 'al-' ('the'), giving 'to the faith.' The '-i' ending is genitive, as required after the preposition 'li-.'
ai.r: ا-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust, safety, to believe

ai.m: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
ai.g: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
ai.r: — (particle; no root)

ai.m: 'Believe!' — a command to a group: have faith, trust, and affirm. Built on the verb meaning to attain security and to believe, it calls people to embrace faith.
ai.g: A command (imperative) verb on the causative (Form IV) pattern, from the verb meaning 'to believe / to have faith'. The -ū ending directs the command to a second-person masculine plural audience, 'you all — believe!'.
ai.r: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, safety, trust, faith

ai.m: 'By/in your Lord' — combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the noun 'Lord' (the Master, Sustainer, and Nurturer who owns, provides for, and brings to maturity) with the pronoun 'your (plural)'.
ai.g: A preposition attached to a noun carrying a possessive pronoun. The preposition bi- ('with/by/in') puts the noun into the genitive case, reflected in the -i vowel of rabbi. The suffix -kum means 'your' addressing a plural group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord, master, to nurture and sustain

ai.m: 'So we believed / we had faith' — the act of coming to faith, trusting, and affirming the truth, attributed to a 'we' subject, introduced by a connective 'so/then'.

p.en: so / then (connective showing result or sequence)

ai.g: A prefixed connective fa- ('so/then') on a Form IV perfect (completed-action) verb. The suffix -nā marks the subject as 'we' and the perfect form indicates a completed act ('we believed / have believed').
ai.r: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be safe, secure; to trust, believe

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: 'So forgive!' — a command to pardon and cover over wrongdoing, to wipe away faults; when addressed to Allah it is a plea, 'forgive us'. The opening 'so/then' links it to a preceding reason.
ai.g: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single person, prefixed by 'fa-' ('so, then'), which connects it to something previously stated as its cause. The verb's bare, vowel-less ending (-ir, with no added vowel) is the form a direct order takes. To 'forgive' here carries the root sense of covering over and concealing a fault.
ai.r: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — covering over, pardoning, forgiveness

ai.m: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
ai.g: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

ai.m: Our sins — wrongdoings or offences attributed to 'us'; the plural 'sins/faults' joined to the speakers.
ai.g: A masculine plural noun ('sins') with the attached possessive pronoun '-nā' ('our'). The -a ending before the pronoun is accusative, the case typically used for the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon — e.g. that which is forgiven or removed).
ai.r: ذ-ن-ب (dh-n-b) — sin, offence, fault

ai.m: 'And efface / blot out / remove' — a command to wipe away or cover over (sins, faults), removing their trace and consequence. The verb conveys both forgiving and erasing.

p.en: efface, blot out, expiate (Form II command)

ai.g: A connective wa ('and') on a Form II imperative (a command). The stem is intensive/causative in meaning ('cause to be covered/wiped away'); the silent (sukūn) ending on the final consonant is typical of a singular command addressed to one person ('you, do this!').
ai.r: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; (Form II) to cover over / expiate

ai.m: 'From us / away from us' — the preposition 'from, away from, off of' joined to the pronoun 'us', indicating removal or separation away from the speakers.
ai.g: A preposition with an attached pronoun. ʿan means 'away from / off of' (motion or removal away from something), and the suffix -nā is the object 'us'.
ai.r: — (particle; no triliteral root)

ai.m: 'Our evil deeds / misdeeds / bad acts' — the plural of a word for an evil or harmful action, a fault or wrongdoing, joined to 'our'.
ai.g: A sound feminine plural noun with a possessive pronoun. The -i vowel before -nā is the genitive ending, which here links the noun to the possessor ('… OF us', i.e. 'our'). The suffix -nā means 'our'.
ai.r: س-و-أ (s-w-ʾ) — to be bad, evil, to do harm

ai.m: 'And take us in full / cause us to pass away' — a command from the verb meaning to take something completely; applied to a soul it means to receive it fully at death, hence 'cause us to die' (as a gathering-back, not loss).

p.en: take fully, gather back (Form V stem)

ai.g: A connective wa ('and') on a Form V imperative (command) with an attached object. Form V here means 'to take/receive in full'. The final weak letter is dropped in the command form, and -nā is the object 'us' ('take us fully').
ai.r: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — to be complete, to fulfil; (Form V) to take in full / gather back

ai.m: With, together with, alongside — indicating company, accompaniment, or being in the same place or time as another.
ai.g: A preposition of accompaniment ('with, alongside'); grammatically it is an adverbial of place/time (ẓarf) that governs the genitive. It is placed before a following noun to put one thing in the company of another, and that following noun stands in the genitive. The -a is its fixed ending.

ai.m: 'The truly righteous / the devoutly good / the pious' — the plural of a noun for those abundant in goodness, dutiful obedience, and sincere virtue, with the definite article 'the'.
ai.g: A definite plural noun. The final -i is the genitive case: it typically appears when the word follows a preposition or is linked to a preceding noun ('… OF the righteous'). The plural pattern denotes those who abound in goodness.
ai.r: ب-ر-ر (b-r-r) — to be dutiful, pious, abundantly good

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: 'And give us / grant us / bring to us' — a command to give or bestow, joined to 'us' as the recipient, with a connective 'and'.
ai.g: A connective wa ('and') on a Form IV imperative (command) from a weak-ending verb, with an attached pronoun. The final weak vowel of the command is reflected before the object -nā ('us'), the one receiving the giving.
ai.r: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (Form IV) to bring, give, bestow

ai.m: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
ai.g: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

ai.m: 'You promised us' — a completed-action verb meaning 'to promise, pledge, undertake', with 'you (singular)' as the one promising and 'us' as those to whom the promise is made.

p.en: you (masculine singular subject); the root's final d assimilates into this t, doubling it

ai.g: A perfect (completed-action) Form I verb. The suffix written with a doubled tā' (-tta) marks the subject as 'you' (masculine singular): the root's final d has assimilated into the subject's t, producing the geminate. The further suffix -nā is the object 'us'. So: a completed promising done by 'you' toward 'us'.
ai.r: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise, pledge, give one's word

ai.m: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
ai.g: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

ai.m: 'Your messengers / your envoys' — the plural of a word for one sent with a message (a messenger, apostle, emissary), joined to 'your (singular)'.

p.en: your (masculine singular), with genitive linking vowel

ai.g: A plural noun with a possessive pronoun. The -i vowel before -ka is the genitive ending, which here links the noun to its owner ('messengers OF you' = 'your messengers'). The suffix -ka means 'your', addressing one male.
ai.r: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; (noun) one who is sent, a messenger

ai.m: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
ai.g: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

ai.m: 'You disgrace / humiliate / put to shame us' — a verb meaning to bring shame, disgrace, or humiliation upon someone, with 'you' as subject and 'us' as object.
ai.g: An imperfect (present/future) Form IV verb. The tu- prefix marks a second-person singular subject ('you'). This is a weak-ending verb whose final yā' is dropped by regular phonological elision before the attached object -nā; this happens in the ordinary indicative and is not a jussive or subjunctive shortening. The suffix -nā is the object 'us' ('you put us to shame').
ai.r: خ-ز-ي (kh-z-y) — to be disgraced, humiliated, put to shame

ai.m: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
ai.g: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
ai.r: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

ai.m: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
ai.g: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.
ai.r: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise

ai.m: 'Indeed you' — an emphasis particle meaning 'truly / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'you', used to open a statement with certainty and stress about the person addressed.
ai.g: The emphasis particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with an attached pronoun. 'inna' adds strong assertion to a sentence and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The suffix '-ka' means 'you' (masculine singular) as its subject.

ai.m: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
ai.g: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

ai.m: 'You break / fail to keep / go back on' — a present-tense verb meaning to break a promise, default on a pledge, or fail to fulfil what was undertaken.
ai.g: An imperfect (present/future) Form IV verb. The tu- prefix marks a second-person singular subject ('you'). The final -u is the indicative mood, marking a plain statement or ongoing fact ('you break / do break').
ai.r: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to come after, succeed; (Form IV) to break a promise, default

ai.m: 'The appointed promise / the tryst / the pledged appointment' — a noun for a fixed promise or an appointed time and place agreed upon, with the definite article 'the'.
ai.g: A definite noun. The final -a is the accusative case, which commonly marks the noun as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). The pattern denotes a fixed appointment or settled promise.
ai.r: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise, appoint a time

title: Rescue us from this town
who: The oppressed believers — men, women, and children
situation: The weak and persecuted in Mecca cried out to be delivered from a town whose people were unjust, and for a protector and helper from God.
arabic: وَمَا لَـكُمۡ لَا تُقَاتِلُوۡنَ فِىۡ سَبِيۡلِ اللّٰهِ وَالۡمُسۡتَضۡعَفِيۡنَ مِنَ الرِّجَالِ وَالنِّسَآءِ وَالۡوِلۡدَانِ الَّذِيۡنَ يَقُوۡلُوۡنَ رَبَّنَاۤ اَخۡرِجۡنَا مِنۡ هٰذِهِ الۡـقَرۡيَةِ الظَّالِمِ اَهۡلُهَا​ ۚ وَاجۡعَلْ لَّـنَا مِنۡ لَّدُنۡكَ وَلِيًّا ۙۚ وَّاجۡعَلْ لَّـنَا مِنۡ لَّدُنۡكَ نَصِيۡرًا ؕ‏
translation: And what is it with you? You do not fight in the cause of Allah and for oppressed men, women, and children who cry out, “Our Lord! Deliver us from this land of oppressors! Appoint for us a saviour; appoint for us a helper—all by Your grace.”
ai_translation: And what is it with you? You do not fight in the cause of Allah and for oppressed men, women, and children who cry out, “Our Rabb! Deliver us from this land of oppressors! Appoint for us a saviour; appoint for us a helper—all by Your grace.”

ai.m: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
ai.g: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
ai.r: — (relative pronoun / particle)

ai.m: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
ai.g: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

ai.m: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
ai.g: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

ai.m: A verb meaning 'you (all) fight / do battle.' The 'mutual' verb pattern conveys fighting against an opponent, mutual combat, addressed to a group.
ai.g: A present-tense verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The prefix 'tu-' marks the addressee ('you') and the suffix '-ūna' marks masculine plural with the indicative mood (a plain statement, 'you are fighting / you fight'). The qātala pattern signals mutual or sustained combat.
ai.r: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — killing, fighting, combat

ai.m: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
ai.g: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
ai.r: — (particle)

ai.m: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
ai.g: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.
ai.r: س-ب-ل (s-b-l) — way, path, road

ai.m: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
ai.g: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

ai.m: A noun/adjective in the plural, 'the oppressed / those deemed weak / the downtrodden,' joined by 'and' (wa-). It refers to people treated as weak and made helpless — held to be of no account and rendered powerless by others, rather than weak merely by nature.
ai.g: A definite masculine sound plural, prefixed with 'wa-' ('and'). It is a passive participle of the 'seeking/deeming' (istafʿala) pattern — literally 'those who are counted weak / made weak,' i.e. the oppressed. The '-īna' ending marks masculine plural in the accusative/genitive form (used for objects, or after prepositions and links). 'Wa-' simply joins it to what precedes.
ai.r: ض-ع-ف (ḍ-ʿ-f) — weakness, feebleness, being made weak

ai.m: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
ai.g: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

ai.m: A noun meaning 'the men / the menfolk' — adult human males. By extension the root conveys manliness and the standing on one's feet, but the plain sense of this plural is 'men.'
ai.g: A definite masculine plural noun ('the men'). The '-i' ending is genitive: the case a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun as '…of…' (as in 'of the men / among the men'). The 'r' is doubled in pronunciation because the 'l' of 'al-' (the) assimilates into it.
ai.r: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — man, manliness, going on foot

ai.m: A noun meaning 'the women / womenfolk' — adult human females, joined by 'and' (wa-). It is the plural used for women collectively.
ai.g: A definite plural noun for women, prefixed with 'wa-' ('and'). The '-i' ending is genitive: the case used after a preposition or in an '…of…' linkage ('of the women / among the women'). The 'n' is doubled in pronunciation because the 'l' of 'al-' (the) assimilates into it. 'Nisā'' is a plural that has no singular from the same form (its singular is 'imra'a,' woman).
ai.r: ن-س-و / ن-س-ء (n-s-w / n-s-ʾ) — women, womankind

ai.m: A noun meaning 'the children / the young ones / offspring,' joined by 'and' (wa-). It is the plural denoting the newly born and the young — those still in childhood.
ai.g: A definite masculine plural noun ('the children'), prefixed with 'wa-' ('and'). The '-i' ending is genitive: the case taken after a preposition or in an '…of…' linkage ('of the children / among the children'). 'Wildān' is a plural of 'walīd / walad' (a child, one born).
ai.r: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — giving birth, begetting, child, offspring

ai.m: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
ai.g: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

ai.m: 'They say / they keep saying' — a present-tense verb of speaking: to say, utter, or assert in words.
ai.g: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), from a hollow (middle-vowel) root. The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are saying.'
ai.r: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — speech; saying, uttering, asserting

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: A command/plea meaning 'bring us out' or 'take us out' — to cause us to exit or emerge from something. It is a request directed to a single addressee asking that 'we' be removed from a place or situation.
ai.g: A command (imperative) verb in the causative pattern (af'ala), so it means 'cause to go out' rather than simply 'go out'. The bare imperative form addresses a single 'you'. The attached -nā is the object pronoun 'us', the ones to be brought out.
ai.r: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — going out, exiting, emerging

ai.m: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
ai.g: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
ai.r: — (preposition)

ai.m: This (feminine) — a pointing word ('this one here') used for a single nearby thing that is grammatically feminine.
ai.g: A demonstrative pronoun ('this') for a single feminine thing close at hand. It is fixed in form and does not change for case; it commonly precedes the noun it points to.
