ai.m: A settled place where people live — a town, village, or populated locality. It denotes a community gathered in one inhabited place.
ai.g: A feminine singular noun marked with 'the'. The final -i is the genitive case: it typically marks the word as linked to a preceding preposition or oath particle, or as the second term of a possessive phrase ('… of …').
ai.r: ق-ر-ي (q-r-y) — gathering, bringing together (people in a settlement)

ai.m: One who does wrong or commits injustice — an oppressor or wrongdoer. The active participle describes a person characterized by ẓulm: putting things out of their rightful place, acting unjustly or tyrannically.
ai.g: An active participle (the 'one who does X' form) on the pattern fā'il, here meaning 'the one who wrongs/oppresses'. It carries 'the'. The final -i is genitive: it typically marks linkage to a preceding preposition or oath, or possession ('… of …').
ai.r: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, oppression

ai.m: 'Its people' — the inhabitants, family, or folk belonging to something. Ahl denotes the people who belong to a place, household, or affiliation; with the attached pronoun it means the people of 'it' (a feminine referent).
ai.g: A noun followed by the possessive pronoun -hā ('its/her', referring to a feminine or non-human thing). The -u ending on the noun is the nominative case, which typically marks the word as the doer/subject or the thing being identified.
ai.r: أ-ه-ل ('-h-l) — belonging, family, people of a place

ai.m: A command meaning 'make', 'set', 'appoint', or 'render' — to bring something into a state or assign it a role. Ja'ala is a versatile verb of making/placing/turning-into. With the joining 'and', it links to a preceding statement.
ai.g: 'And' joined to a command (imperative) verb addressed to a single 'you'. The bare imperative form (with no ending vowel) issues a direct request or order to one person. The verb often takes two objects ('make X into Y').
ai.r: ج-ع-ل (j-'-l) — making, placing, rendering, appointing

ai.m: 'For us / to us' — indicating that something is directed toward, or belongs to, the speaker's group.
ai.g: The preposition li- ('for / to') with the attached pronoun -nā ('us'). When this pronoun is added, the preposition's vowel becomes 'la-'. The whole expresses benefit or direction toward 'us' — what is done for, or owed to, the speaker's group.
ai.r: — (li- is a particle/preposition; -nā is a pronoun)

ai.m: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
ai.g: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
ai.r: — (preposition)

ai.m: From Yourself; from Your presence. The base word ladun means 'the presence of', 'the side of', or 'directly from' — pointing to something issuing straight from a source. Here it is preceded by the preposition min ('from'), whose final n assimilates into the following l so that the l is doubled. With the attached pronoun the whole conveys 'from Your own presence', stressing that what is given comes directly from the giver.

p.en: from (preposition; its n merges into the following l)
presence / nearness / 'from with' (doubled l from the merged n)

ai.g: An adverb of place/source ('at, by, in the presence of') joined to the attached pronoun -ka, 'your/you' for a single masculine addressee, together conveying 'from Your presence'. The initial l is written with a shadda (doubled): this gemination results from the preceding preposition min, whose final n assimilates into the l. The word implies immediacy of source — something coming directly from the one referred to.
ai.r: — (an adverbial particle of place; no triliteral verbal root)

ai.m: A guardian, protector, ally, or close supporter — one who is near and takes charge of another's affairs. Waliyy carries the sense of nearness combined with care, authority, and friendship.
ai.g: An indefinite noun ('a protector'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the accusative case: it commonly marks the word as a direct object of a verb, or as a predicate/complement after certain verbs of 'making' or 'becoming'.
ai.r: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, guardianship, alliance, friendship

ai.m: A command meaning 'make', 'set', 'appoint', or 'render' — identical in sense to id 920. Ja'ala is a versatile verb of making/placing/turning-into; with the joining 'and' it links to a preceding statement.
ai.g: 'And' joined to a command (imperative) verb addressed to a single 'you'. The bare imperative form (with no ending vowel) issues a direct request or order to one person. The verb often takes two objects ('make X into Y').
ai.r: ج-ع-ل (j-'-l) — making, placing, rendering, appointing

ai.m: 'For us / to us' — indicating that something is directed toward, or belongs to, the speaker's group.
ai.g: The preposition li- ('for / to') with the attached pronoun -nā ('us'). When this pronoun is added, the preposition's vowel becomes 'la-'. The whole expresses benefit or direction toward 'us' — what is done for, or owed to, the speaker's group.
ai.r: — (li- is a particle/preposition; -nā is a pronoun)

ai.m: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
ai.g: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
ai.r: — (preposition)

ai.m: From Yourself; from Your presence. The base word ladun means 'the presence of', 'the side of', or 'directly from' — pointing to something issuing straight from a source. Here it is preceded by the preposition min ('from'), whose final n assimilates into the following l so that the l is doubled. With the attached pronoun the whole conveys 'from Your own presence', stressing that what is given comes directly from the giver.

p.en: from (preposition; its n merges into the following l)
presence / nearness / 'from with' (doubled l from the merged n)

ai.g: An adverb of place/source ('at, by, in the presence of') joined to the attached pronoun -ka, 'your/you' for a single masculine addressee, together conveying 'from Your presence'. The initial l is written with a shadda (doubled): this gemination results from the preceding preposition min, whose final n assimilates into the l. The word implies immediacy of source — something coming directly from the one referred to.
ai.r: — (an adverbial particle of place; no triliteral verbal root)

ai.m: 'A helper, supporter, one who gives aid and victory' — an intensive form stressing reliable, effective help.
ai.g: An indefinite noun on an intensive pattern (faʿīl) that conveys a strong or constant doer — 'a true helper'. The -an ending marks the accusative and indefiniteness, commonly used here as a specifier naming the capacity ('as a helper').
ai.r: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, to aid, to give victory

title: We believe, so record us
who: Sincere Christians who recognised the truth
situation: When they heard the Qur'an their eyes overflowed with tears; they asked God to write them down among those who testify to it.
arabic: وَاِذَا سَمِعُوۡا مَاۤ اُنۡزِلَ اِلَى الرَّسُوۡلِ تَرٰٓى اَعۡيُنَهُمۡ تَفِيۡضُ مِنَ الدَّمۡعِ مِمَّا عَرَفُوۡا مِنَ الۡحَـقِّ​ۚ يَقُوۡلُوۡنَ رَبَّنَاۤ اٰمَنَّا فَاكۡتُبۡنَا مَعَ الشّٰهِدِيۡنَ‏
translation: When they listen to what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears for recognizing the truth. They say, “Our Lord! We believe, so count us among the witnesses.
ai_translation: When they listen to what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears for recognizing the truth. They say, “Our Rabb! We believe, so count us among the witnesses.

ai.m: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
ai.g: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

ai.m: A past-tense verb meaning 'they heard / they listened' — to perceive by ear, and by extension to give ear and pay heed.
ai.g: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The silent alif written after the wāw (-ū) is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.
ai.r: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — hearing, listening, heeding

ai.m: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
ai.g: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

ai.m: 'It was sent down / revealed': the act of being caused to descend, used especially of revelation brought down from Allah. The passive form puts the focus on the thing sent down rather than on the sender.
ai.g: A past-tense passive verb in Form IV (anzala 'to send down' → unzila 'was sent down'). The prefix is only the u- vowel carried on the connecting hamza; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ز-ل), not part of the prefix. The internal vowel pattern u–i marks it as passive ('was/were sent down'), with no named doer. The final -a marks the subject as 'he/it', a single masculine thing, and signals completed action.
ai.r: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (Form IV) to send down

ai.m: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
ai.g: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

ai.m: the Messenger — one sent with a message; specifically an envoy commissioned by Allah to convey His revelation. 'Rasūl' is a faʿūl-pattern noun denoting the one who is sent.
ai.g: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') is assimilated into the 'sun letter' r (so it sounds ar-r). The ending -i marks the genitive case, the form a word typically takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of …').
ai.r: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a message, an envoy

ai.m: A present-tense verb meaning 'you see, you behold, you perceive (with the eye)' — and by extension, to come to know or regard something as being a certain way.
ai.g: A present-tense verb addressed to a single 'you' (the ta- prefix marks second-person masculine singular). It comes from a weak root whose final letter appears as the long -ā vowel. Standing without a following negative or subjunctive particle, it reads as a plain present-tense statement.
ai.r: ر-أ-ي (r-ʼ-y) — seeing, perceiving, forming a view

ai.m: A construction meaning 'their eyes' — the organs of sight, here belonging to a group ('them').
ai.g: A plural noun (aʿyun, a broken plural of ʿayn, 'eye') with the attached possessive pronoun -hum ('their'). The -a vowel before the pronoun marks the accusative case, which typically signals that the noun is the object of a verb.
ai.r: ع-ي-ن (ʿ-y-n) — eye; also spring/source

ai.m: A present-tense verb meaning 'it overflows, brims over, pours out (in abundance)' — said of a vessel or eye filling until it spills.
ai.g: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix here marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('it/she …'), agreeing with a feminine or plural noun. The final -u vowel signals the indicative mood, used for a plain statement of ongoing action.
ai.r: ف-ي-ض (f-y-ḍ) — overflowing, brimming, pouring forth abundantly

ai.m: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
ai.g: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

ai.m: A construction meaning 'the tears' or 'the tear-water' — the moisture wept from the eyes.
ai.g: The definite article al- ('the'), whose 'l' assimilates into the following 'd', prefixed to the noun damʿ ('tears'). The final -i ending is genitive: it typically marks the noun as the object of a preposition, or links it to a preceding noun ('… OF …').
ai.r: د-م-ع (d-m-ʿ) — tears, weeping

ai.m: From what / from that which — a fusion of the preposition 'from' with the relative 'what/which', introducing the thing or situation being referred to.
ai.g: A merger of 'min' ('from') and 'mā' ('what/that which'); the 'n' of 'min' assimilates into the 'm' of 'mā', doubling it. The combination means 'from what ...' and typically introduces a following clause describing the thing referred to. Being particles, neither part takes a case ending.

ai.m: To know by recognition, to identify something already familiar — to perceive and acknowledge what one has come to know. It implies recognizing a truth or person one is acquainted with.
ai.g: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine plural — the -ū ending means 'they' did the action. It denotes a completed act of recognizing or coming to know something familiar.
ai.r: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, recognize; recognition

ai.m: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
ai.g: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

ai.m: 'The truth', 'the right', 'what is rightfully due' — that which is real, correct, and justly owed; the opposite of falsehood and wrongdoing.
ai.g: A definite masculine noun (the al- prefix means 'the'). The -i ending is genitive, the case typically taken after a preposition or when the word links to a preceding noun ('… of the truth / by right').
ai.r: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, rightness, that which is established and due

ai.m: 'They say / they keep saying' — a present-tense verb of speaking: to say, utter, or assert in words.
ai.g: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), from a hollow (middle-vowel) root. The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are saying.'
ai.r: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — speech; saying, uttering, asserting

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: We have believed; we have come to faith and trust — to affirm belief, give one's trust, and feel secure in that conviction, stated by a group about themselves.
ai.g: A past-tense verb on the form-IV pattern (āmana, 'to believe / to have faith'). The ending -nā (a single morpheme, نَا) attached to a past verb marks the subject as 'we'. The doubled 'n' heard in 'āmannā' comes from the verb stem's final 'n' meeting the 'n' that begins the -nā ending.
ai.r: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

ai.m: 'So write us / so record us / so enroll us' — a plea that the speakers be registered or inscribed (e.g., among a named group).
ai.g: fa- is a connector 'so/then', often drawing a consequence. The stem is a command (imperative) verb addressed to a single person ('you write/record'), the bare unsuffixed form marking the singular addressee. The final -nā is the object pronoun 'us': 'so record us'.
ai.r: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write, to inscribe, to ordain/record

ai.m: With, together with, alongside — indicating company, accompaniment, or being in the same place or time as another.
ai.g: A preposition of accompaniment ('with, alongside'); grammatically it is an adverbial of place/time (ẓarf) that governs the genitive. It is placed before a following noun to put one thing in the company of another, and that following noun stands in the genitive. The -a is its fixed ending.

ai.m: 'The witnesses / those who testify' — people who observe and bear testimony, affirming the truth of something.
ai.g: al- is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following 'sh', heard as ash-shā…). The active participle shāhid ('one who witnesses') takes the sound masculine plural ending -īna, which makes it plural and marks the accusative/genitive case — typically the object of a verb, or the object of a preposition, or part of a possessive phrase.
ai.r: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, to testify, to be present

title: Send down a table spread
situation: At the request of his disciples for a sign, Isa asked God to send down a table of food from heaven that would be a festival and a proof for them.
arabic: قَالَ عِيۡسَى ابۡنُ مَرۡيَمَ اللّٰهُمَّ رَبَّنَاۤ اَنۡزِلۡ عَلَيۡنَا مَآٮِٕدَةً مِّنَ السَّمَآءِ تَكُوۡنُ لَـنَا عِيۡدًا لِّاَوَّلِنَا وَاٰخِرِنَا وَاٰيَةً مِّنۡكَ​ۚ وَارۡزُقۡنَا وَاَنۡتَ خَيۡرُ الرّٰزِقِيۡنَ‏
translation: Jesus, son of Mary, prayed, “O Allah, our Lord! Send us from heaven a table spread with food as a feast for us—the first and last of us—and as a sign from You. Provide for us! You are indeed the Best Provider.”
ai_translation: Jesus, son of Mary, prayed, “O Allah, our Rabb! Send us from heaven a table spread with food as a feast for us—the first and last of us—and as a sign from You. Provide for us! You are indeed the Best Provider.”

ai.m: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
ai.g: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
ai.r: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

ai.m: "Isa" — the personal name of the prophet Jesus, son of Mary.
ai.g: A proper name (a foreign/non-Arabic name). It is fully indeclinable: its ending does not change for case, so it stays the same as subject, object, or after a preposition.

ai.m: 'Son' — a male child or descendant. It expresses the relationship of being the son of someone.
ai.g: A noun. The -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject or for a noun in apposition (a word that renames or further identifies another). The initial alif is a connecting hamza, normally elided after a preceding word, so it is read as 'bnu'. It is typically followed by the name of the father or parent ('son OF …').
ai.r: ب-ن-و / ب-ن-ي (b-n-w/y) — son; to build (offspring as that which is built up)

ai.m: "Maryam" — the personal name Mary, the mother of the prophet Jesus.
ai.g: A proper name (feminine, foreign origin). It is diptote: it takes no -n (nunation), and in the genitive and accusative it ends in -a rather than -i, so the -a ending shown serves for both object and "of" positions.

ai.m: O Allah — a vocative address to Allah. It is the divine name Allah with an added ending standing in place of the call-word 'O', so the whole word means 'O Allah' — an invocation calling directly upon Allah.
ai.g: The proper name Allah used in direct address (vocative), with the suffixed -umma serving the function of the vocative 'O' that normally precedes a called noun. The word is fixed in this form for calling upon Allah ('O Allah').

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: Send down! / Bring down! — a command to cause something to descend, especially to send down from above as a bestowal.
ai.g: A command (imperative) verb of the causative (Form IV) pattern, addressed to a single masculine 'you'. The pattern turns 'come down' into 'cause to come down, send down'. It ends in a vowelless final letter (sukūn), the typical shape of a direct order.
ai.r: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — descending, coming/sending down

ai.m: 'Upon us' / 'over us' / 'against us' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, upon') with an attached 'us'. It conveys something resting on, incumbent upon, or bearing against the group.
ai.g: A preposition (ʿalā, 'upon/over') with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'us'). When a pronoun is attached, ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay-. Such prepositional phrases put their pronoun in the object/genitive role.

ai.m: A table spread (with food) / a laden feast — a set dinner-table, especially one bearing provisions.
ai.g: A feminine singular noun. The final -tan (nunation on the feminine -t) marks it as indefinite ('a table-spread') and in the accusative case — the form used for the object of a verb.
ai.r: م-ي-د (m-y-d) — swaying; providing a laden table

ai.m: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
ai.g: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

ai.m: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
ai.g: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').
ai.r: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, loftiness; sky, heaven

ai.m: It is / it will be / so as to be — a verb of 'being', expressing existence or a state of being.
ai.g: Present-tense verb, third-person feminine singular ('it', e.g. a feminine thing). The ta- prefix here marks a feminine 'it' as the subject. The final -u ending is the indicative mood, marking a plain statement of being. From a hollow root whose middle و appears as the long ū.
ai.r: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, coming to be

ai.m: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
ai.g: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

ai.m: A festival / recurring feast-day — an appointed occasion of celebration that returns again and again; an ʿīd.
ai.g: A masculine singular noun. The final -an (nunation, written with the extra alif) marks it as indefinite ('a festival') and in the accusative case — the form used for the object of a verb or a predicate of 'to be'.
ai.r: ع-و-د (ʿ-w-d) — returning, recurring

ai.m: For the first of us — directed to the earliest among a group ('our first ones'), with 'for/to' marking the beneficiary.
ai.g: A noun ('first') governed by the preposition li- ('for/to'), with the attached possessive 'our'. The preposition normally calls for the genitive ending; the attached -nā ('us/our') stands in its place.
ai.r: أ-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — being first, primacy, beginning

ai.m: And the last of us / the later ones among us — those who come afterward or at the end ('our last ones').
ai.g: A noun ('last/latter') with the attached possessive 'our', joined by wa- ('and'). It stands in the genitive position (paired with the earlier 'for the first of us'); the attached -nā ('us/our') occupies the place of the case ending.
ai.r: أ-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — coming after, being last/later

ai.m: And a sign / token / miraculous proof — something set up to point beyond itself, a mark or evidence that signifies a deeper truth; also a verse of revelation.
ai.g: A feminine singular noun. The final -tan (nunation on the feminine -t) marks it as indefinite ('a sign') and in the accusative case — the form used for the object of a verb. Joined by wa- ('and').
ai.r: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — sign, mark, token

ai.m: From You — origin or source traced back to a single addressee ('You'), as in a gift or sending that comes 'from You'.
ai.g: The preposition min ('from') with an attached pronoun 'you' (masculine singular). Attached pronouns after a preposition are the object of that preposition; here it conveys 'from you'.

ai.m: A command/request meaning 'and provide us; and grant us sustenance / our daily provision' — to bestow on someone the food, livelihood, and means of life one needs.
ai.g: A command (imperative) verb. The bare imperative stem addresses a single 'you', and the attached -nā is the object pronoun 'us', so the whole means 'provide for us'. Often used as a petition directed to Allah.
ai.r: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — to provide sustenance, livelihood, provision

ai.m: 'And You' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'you' (addressing a single male). The independent pronoun stresses the subject, as in 'and You [Yourself] …'.
ai.g: A connective 'and' plus a detached subject pronoun. 'anta' is the masculine-singular 'you'; as a standalone pronoun it adds emphasis or introduces a statement about the addressee ('You are …').

ai.m: 'Best / the best (of)' — superior to all others in goodness, excellence, or worth; the finest in its class.
ai.g: khayr functions as a comparative/superlative noun ('better / best'). The -u ending marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject or predicate of a sentence and also opens a possessive phrase ('the best OF …').
ai.r: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — goodness, that which is good or best

ai.m: 'The providers / the sustainers' — those who supply provision and the means of life; a plural describing the doers of the act of providing.
ai.g: A definite active participle in the masculine sound plural. The pattern fāʿil ('rāziq') names the one performing the act; the '-īna' ending marks a masculine plural in the object/genitive state (the form used after prepositions, as a non-subject, or after certain particles).
ai.r: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — to provide sustenance, livelihood, provision

title: We have wronged ourselves
who: Prophet Adam and his wife Hawwa
situation: After eating from the forbidden tree, in deep remorse, they turned to God with the first prayer of repentance — admitting their wrong and begging mercy.
arabic: قَالَا رَبَّنَا ظَلَمۡنَاۤ اَنۡفُسَنَا وَاِنۡ لَّمۡ تَغۡفِرۡ لَـنَا وَتَرۡحَمۡنَا لَـنَكُوۡنَنَّ مِنَ الۡخٰسِرِيۡنَ‏
translation: They replied, “Our Lord! We have wronged ourselves. If You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will certainly be losers.”
ai_translation: They replied, “Our Rabb! We have wronged ourselves. If You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will certainly be losers.”

ai.m: The two of them said — to speak or utter words, with two subjects voicing the speech together. This form introduces what two people said.
ai.g: A past-tense (perfect) verb with the dual subject ending -ā ('the two of them did'). This -ā specifically marks exactly two doers acting together.
ai.r: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: We wronged / we did injustice — to wrong, oppress, or act unjustly, including against oneself; placing something where it does not belong. The form has a first-person plural 'we' subject.
ai.g: A past-tense (perfect) verb with the first-person plural subject ending -nā ('we did'). This -nā marks the doers as 'we / us.'
ai.r: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, oppress, do injustice; to put a thing out of its rightful place

ai.m: Ourselves / our own souls — 'nafs' means the self, soul, or inner person; in the plural with 'our,' it denotes one's own selves as the object of an action.
ai.g: A plural noun ('selves') joined to the possessive pronoun -nā ('our'). The -a ending on the noun is accusative, the case typically used when the word is the object of a verb (the thing acted upon).
ai.r: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, inner person; the living breath of a being

ai.m: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
ai.g: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

ai.m: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
ai.g: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

ai.m: To cover over, pardon, and forgive — especially sins, blotting them out and shielding the wrongdoer from their consequences. The form is a present-tense verb addressed to a single male: 'you forgive / you cover over (sins).'
ai.g: A present/imperfect verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person singular masculine subject ('you'). The bare -ir ending with no added vowel reflects a jussive/conditional or otherwise unmarked mood (as after a conditional particle), rather than the plain indicative which would end in -u.
ai.r: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, pardon, forgive

ai.m: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
ai.g: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

ai.m: And You have mercy on us / and that You may have mercy on us — to show mercy, compassion, and tender care. The form expresses a 'You' subject acting mercifully toward 'us.'
ai.g: A present/imperfect-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('You'). The final consonant carries a silent (sukūn) ending, showing a cut-off (jussive/subjunctive-style) state caused by a preceding governing particle. The -nā is an object pronoun ('us').
ai.r: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion, tender loving care

ai.m: We shall most certainly be — an emphatic assertion that a group will indeed come to be in some state. Carries a built-in stress: 'we will surely, definitely be'.
ai.g: Verb 'to be' carrying strong emphasis at both ends: the prefixed la- ('surely') and the suffixed -nna (the heavy emphatic ending, 'most certainly'). The na- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we').
ai.r: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to become

ai.m: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
ai.g: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

ai.m: "The losers / those who lose" — an active participle for those who suffer loss, who lose out or come to ruin, especially the ultimate loss of one's own soul.
ai.g: An active participle in the masculine sound plural with the definite article 'the'. The -īna ending marks the accusative or genitive case — the form used when such a plural is a direct object, a predicate of 'to be', or follows a preposition (as opposed to the -ūna subject form).
ai.r: خ-س-ر (kh-s-r) — to lose / suffer loss / be ruined

title: Do not place us with the wrongdoers
situation: Standing on the heights between Paradise and Hell, they pray not to be cast among the wrongdoing people.
arabic: وَاِذَا صُرِفَتۡ اَبۡصَارُهُمۡ تِلۡقَآءَ اَصۡحٰبِ النَّارِۙ قَالُوۡا رَبَّنَا لَا تَجۡعَلۡنَا مَعَ الۡقَوۡمِ الظّٰلِمِيۡنَ‏
translation: When their eyes will turn towards the residents of Hell, they will pray, “Our Lord! Do not join us with the wrongdoing people.”
ai_translation: When their eyes will turn towards the residents of Hell, they will pray, “Our Rabb! Do not join us with the wrongdoing people.”

ai.m: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
ai.g: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

ai.m: It was turned / diverted: a completed-action passive verb meaning something was redirected, averted, or made to face another way — the doer is unnamed and the focus is on the thing turned.
ai.g: A past-tense passive verb (the u-i vowel pattern, ṣurifa, signals the passive — 'was turned'). The -at ending marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she/it'), agreeing with a feminine noun.
ai.r: ص-ر-ف (ṣ-r-f) — to turn away, divert, redirect

ai.m: Their eyes / their sights: the organs of sight, or by extension acts of seeing and glances. The plural noun denotes eyes belonging to a group.
ai.g: A plural noun (plural of baṣar, 'sight/eye') with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u is the nominative ending, marking it typically as the subject; the suffix -hum means 'their' (masculine plural).
ai.r: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r) — sight, vision, perception

ai.m: Toward / in the direction of: a word denoting the facing-place or direction opposite something — the side one turns to face. It functions as 'toward' or 'in front of.'
ai.g: A noun used adverbially to mean 'toward, facing.' The final -a is the accusative ending, which here functions adverbially to express direction ('toward …'); it typically links to a following noun in the genitive.
ai.r: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to meet, encounter, face

ai.m: Companions, associates, fellows; those who keep company with or belong to a thing — people closely bound to something (often 'people/inhabitants of …').
ai.g: A broken (irregular) plural of ṣāḥib ('companion'). The final -i is the genitive ending, which typically links the word to a following noun ('companions OF …') or follows a preposition. As a plural it denotes a group, here in a possessive/linking relationship.
ai.r: ص-ح-ب (ṣ-ḥ-b) — companionship, to accompany, keep company

ai.m: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
ai.g: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').
ai.r: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — fire, blaze, burning

ai.m: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
ai.g: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.
ai.r: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, utterance

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
ai.g: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

ai.m: You place us / make us: a present-tense verb of putting, setting, or rendering something into a state, with an attached pronoun 'us' as its object.
ai.g: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix with no plural ending marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'). The bare (vowelless) ending shows the jussive mood, the form used after particles of command or prohibition. The attached -nā is the object pronoun 'us.'
ai.r: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, render, appoint

ai.m: With, together with, alongside — indicating company, accompaniment, or being in the same place or time as another.
ai.g: A preposition of accompaniment ('with, alongside'); grammatically it is an adverbial of place/time (ẓarf) that governs the genitive. It is placed before a following noun to put one thing in the company of another, and that following noun stands in the genitive. The -a is its fixed ending.

ai.m: 'The people / the folk' — a collective noun for a community, nation, or group of people regarded as a body. Often it carries the nuance of one's own people or a particular group sharing a trait.
ai.g: A collective noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-i' is the genitive ending, which typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship.
ai.r: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand/rise; a people, community

ai.m: The wrongdoers; those who commit injustice, oppression, or place things outside their right setting. Ẓulm is putting something where it does not belong and so transgressing against truth or against others.
ai.g: An active participle ('the ones who do X') with the definite article 'al-' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', a sun letter). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative or genitive — the form used as an object or after a preposition.
ai.r: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — injustice, wrongdoing, placing a thing wrongly

title: Decide between us in truth
situation: When his people threatened to drive him and the believers out, he placed his trust in God and asked Him to judge between them justly.
arabic: قَدِ افۡتَرَيۡنَا عَلَى اللّٰهِ كَذِبًا اِنۡ عُدۡنَا فِىۡ مِلَّتِكُمۡ بَعۡدَ اِذۡ نَجّٰٮنَا اللّٰهُ مِنۡهَا​ ؕ وَمَا يَكُوۡنُ لَـنَاۤ اَنۡ نَّعُوۡدَ فِيۡهَاۤ اِلَّاۤ اَنۡ يَّشَآءَ اللّٰهُ رَبُّنَا​ ؕ وَسِعَ رَبُّنَا كُلَّ شَىۡءٍ عِلۡمًا​ؕ عَلَى اللّٰهِ تَوَكَّلۡنَا​ ؕ رَبَّنَا افۡتَحۡ بَيۡنَنَا وَبَيۡنَ قَوۡمِنَا بِالۡحَـقِّ وَاَنۡتَ خَيۡرُ الۡفٰتِحِيۡنَ‏
translation: We would surely be fabricating a lie against Allah if we were to return to your faith after Allah has saved us from it. It does not befit us to return to it unless it is the Will of Allah, our Lord. Our Lord has encompassed everything in ˹His˺ knowledge. In Allah we trust. Our Lord! Judge between us and our people with truth. You are the best of those who judge.”
ai_translation: We would surely be fabricating a lie against Allah if we were to return to your faith after Allah has saved us from it. It does not befit us to return to it unless it is the Will of Allah, our Rabb. Our Rabb has encompassed everything in knowledge. In Allah we trust. Our Rabb! Judge between us and our people with truth. You are the best of those who judge.”

ai.m: A particle meaning 'indeed' or 'certainly' when placed before a past-tense verb — it affirms and emphasizes that the action has truly and definitely taken place.
ai.g: An emphatic particle. Before a past-tense verb it stresses that the act is completed and verified ('has indeed done'). The final -i is not a case ending but a connecting vowel added to prevent two unvowelled consonants from meeting when the next word begins with a cluster.

ai.m: 'We have invented / fabricated / forged (a falsehood).' The root means to fabricate, to concoct a lie, to invent something falsely and attribute it where it does not belong. The subject is 'we.'
ai.g: A past-tense verb in a reflexive/intensive pattern ('to fabricate, forge'). The suffix -nā marks the subject 'we' who performed the act ('we fabricated').
ai.r: ف-ر-ي (f-r-y) — to fabricate, forge, invent a lie

ai.m: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
ai.g: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
ai.r: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

ai.m: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
ai.g: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

ai.m: A noun meaning 'a lie / falsehood' — a deliberately false statement, an untruth fabricated against the truth.
ai.g: An indefinite noun ('a lie') with the accusative -an ending (tanwīn). The accusative commonly marks the object of a verb (e.g. fabricating a lie); the -an tanwīn shows it is indefinite.
ai.r: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie, to declare false

ai.m: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
ai.g: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

ai.m: 'We returned, went back, reverted.' The root means to come back, to return to a place or to a former state, way, or practice. The subject is 'we.'
ai.g: A past-tense verb (a hollow root whose middle weak letter contracts in this form). The suffix -nā marks the subject 'we' ('we returned / went back').
ai.r: ع-و-د (ʿ-w-d) — to return, come back, revert

ai.m: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
ai.g: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
ai.r: — (particle)

ai.m: 'Your way / creed / religious path,' addressed to a group. The base word denotes a defined body of belief and practice — a community's followed religious way.
ai.g: A feminine noun, 'creed' (base form milla, ending in ta marbuta). With a possessor attached, the ta marbuta surfaces as a pronounced -t- and takes a linking -i — the construct (iḍāfa) realization of the feminine ending, not a separate case morpheme — followed by -kum ('your,' addressing several people): 'your creed / your way.'
ai.r: م-ل-ل (m-l-l) — a followed creed or religious community

ai.m: After; following in time or order — the point or moment subsequent to something.
ai.g: An adverb of time functioning much like a preposition ('after'). It is fixed in the accusative form ending in -a, and is normally followed by a noun in the 'of' relationship, giving 'after (the) …'.
ai.r: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, that which comes later; distance/remoteness

ai.m: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
ai.g: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

ai.m: 'He delivered / rescued / saved us.' The root means to bring to safety, to deliver from danger or harm. In this intensive pattern it stresses a thorough rescue. The object is 'us.'
ai.g: A past-tense verb in the intensive (doubled-middle) pattern, conveying 'to rescue thoroughly,' with a third-person masculine 'he' as the implied subject. The attached -nā here is the object, 'us' — 'he saved us.'
ai.r: ن-ج-و (n-j-w) — to be safe, escape; (causative) to rescue, deliver

ai.m: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
ai.g: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
ai.r: — (proper divine name)

ai.m: A two-part word: the preposition 'min' ('from / out of / some of') joined to the pronoun 'it' (feminine). Together: 'from it / out of it / of it,' indicating a source or a portion taken from a feminine thing.
ai.g: A preposition 'min' with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it/her'), referring to a feminine noun. 'Min' indicates origin, source, or a part taken from a whole; the attached pronoun is in the object form required after a preposition.

ai.m: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
ai.g: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
ai.r: — (relative pronoun / particle)

ai.m: 'It is / it comes to be' — the present-tense verb of being and becoming (from kāna). It expresses that something is the case, exists, or comes about.
ai.g: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he/it is, becomes'. The ya- prefix means 'he/it', and the final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain factual statement (as opposed to a command or a negated/subjunctive form).
ai.r: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

ai.m: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
ai.g: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

ai.m: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
ai.g: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
ai.r: — (particle; no root)

ai.m: '(That) we return / go back / revert.' The root means to come back, to return to a place or to a former state, way, or practice. The subject is 'we.'
ai.g: A present-tense verb meaning 'we return,' built on the na- ('we') prefix, in the subjunctive (final -a vowel, used after a 'that / so that' particle). The doubled nūn (shadda) is not the prefix alone: the preceding subjunctive particle 'an' ('that') loses its own nūn into the verb's na- prefix, and the two merge into one geminated nūn — so the cluster carries both 'that' and 'we' ('that we may return').
ai.r: ع-و-د (ʿ-w-d) — to return, come back, revert

ai.m: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
ai.g: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.
ai.r: — (particle plus pronoun; no root)

ai.m: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
ai.g: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
ai.r: — (particle)

ai.m: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
ai.g: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
ai.r: — (particle; no root)

ai.m: '(that) he wills / wishes' — to will, intend, or so desire that a thing comes about.
ai.g: A present-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('he wills'). The final -a is the subjunctive ending, which typically appears after particles meaning 'that/so that/until,' giving the sense 'that he should will.'
ai.r: ش-و-ء (sh-w-ʾ) — to will, wish, want

ai.m: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
ai.g: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
ai.r: — (proper divine name)

ai.m: 'Our Lord' — 'Rabb' (Lord, Master, Sustainer who creates, owns, nurtures and governs) joined to 'our'. A weighty term for Allah as the One who brings up and sustains all that exists.
ai.g: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun '-nā' ('our'). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case, used when the word is the subject or predicate of a sentence ('[He] is our Lord').
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship

ai.m: '(it) extended / encompassed / was vast enough for' — to be wide, spacious, or ample; to take in or embrace something fully within one's capacity. It conveys all-embracing breadth.
ai.g: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it encompassed'). The final -a marks the completed action of a single masculine subject ('he/it did encompass / extend over').
ai.r: و-س-ع (w-s-ʿ) — to be wide, spacious, to encompass

ai.m: 'Our Lord' — 'Rabb' (Lord, Master, Sustainer who creates, owns, nurtures and governs) joined to 'our'. A weighty term for Allah as the One who brings up and sustains all that exists.
ai.g: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun '-nā' ('our'). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case, used when the word is the subject or predicate of a sentence ('[He] is our Lord').
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship

ai.m: All, every, the whole of — totality. When followed by a singular it means 'every (one)'; when followed by a definite plural or whole it means 'all of.'
ai.g: A noun of totality, almost always joined to a following noun in the genitive ('every … / all of …'). The final -a is the accusative case, the form used when the word functions as an object of a verb.
ai.r: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — wholeness, totality

ai.m: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
ai.g: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
ai.r: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

ai.m: Knowledge — that which is known; firm, certain awareness and understanding.
ai.g: An abstract noun, 'knowledge.' The final -an is the accusative with indefinite 'nunation,' commonly marking the noun as a direct object, or as a specification ('in respect of knowledge').
ai.r: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know, knowledge

ai.m: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
ai.g: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
ai.r: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

ai.m: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
ai.g: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

ai.m: 'We have placed our trust, relied wholly (upon someone).' The root means to entrust an affair, to depend on and commit oneself; this pattern expresses fully delegating one's reliance. The subject is 'we.'
ai.g: A past-tense verb in a reflexive pattern ('to commit one's reliance, put one's trust'). The suffix -nā marks the subject 'we' ('we put our trust').
ai.r: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — to entrust, rely upon, commit an affair

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: An imperative addressed to one person: 'judge / decide / open (a matter) with a verdict.' The root means to open; by extension it means to render a decisive judgment that settles a dispute, and to grant victory or relief.
ai.g: A command verb addressed to a single 'you,' with no ending added beyond the bare command form. It calls for an act of deciding or opening — settling a matter with a definitive judgment.
ai.r: ف-ت-ح (f-t-ḥ) — to open; to judge decisively, grant victory

ai.m: 'Between us' — the spatial or relational word for 'between/among', with 'us' attached: the space, relation, or matter standing between ourselves.
ai.g: An adverb of place 'between', fixed in the -a form, with the attached pronoun -na ('us'). Together they mean 'between us / among us', marking a relation linking two or more parties.
ai.r: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

ai.m: 'And between'. A connective word meaning 'and between / and amid', used to mark the space, relationship, or distinction lying among two or more parties.
ai.g: The word bayna ('between') with 'and' in front. It is an adverb of place that always leads into what follows, so it ends in a fixed -a and is normally paired with a following noun or pronoun ('between … and …').
ai.r: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinctness, 'between'

ai.m: 'Our people / folk / community,' joined to a 'we/our' possessor. The base word denotes a people bound together — a nation, tribe, or community of kin and kind.
ai.g: A masculine noun meaning 'people.' It takes a linking -i before the attached possessor (here the genitive case, since the word follows a preposition / sits in a possessive link), then -nā ('our'): 'our people.'
ai.r: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a people who stand together

ai.m: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
ai.g: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
ai.r: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

ai.m: 'And You' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'you' (addressing a single male). The independent pronoun stresses the subject, as in 'and You [Yourself] …'.
ai.g: A connective 'and' plus a detached subject pronoun. 'anta' is the masculine-singular 'you'; as a standalone pronoun it adds emphasis or introduces a statement about the addressee ('You are …').

ai.m: 'Best / the best (of)' — superior to all others in goodness, excellence, or worth; the finest in its class.
ai.g: khayr functions as a comparative/superlative noun ('better / best'). The -u ending marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject or predicate of a sentence and also opens a possessive phrase ('the best OF …').
ai.r: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — goodness, that which is good or best

ai.m: 'Those who open / decide' — the ones who render decisive judgments, settle matters, and grant relief or victory. As an active participle it names the doers of such opening.
ai.g: A definite sound masculine plural active participle ('those who decide'). The -īna ending marks the accusative/genitive plural — the case used for an object or after a preposition or in a possessive link ('of those who decide').
ai.r: ف-ت-ح (f-t-ḥ) — to open; to judge decisively, grant victory

title: Let us die as Muslims
who: Pharaoh's magicians, after they believed in Musa
situation: When Pharaoh threatened to torture and execute them for their new faith, they asked God only for patience and to take their souls in submission to Him.
arabic: وَمَا تَـنۡقِمُ مِنَّاۤ اِلَّاۤ اَنۡ اٰمَنَّا بِاٰيٰتِ رَبِّنَا لَمَّا جَآءَتۡنَا​ ؕ رَبَّنَاۤ اَفۡرِغۡ عَلَيۡنَا صَبۡرًا وَّتَوَفَّنَا مُسۡلِمِيۡنَ‏
translation: Your rage towards us is only because we believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us. Our Lord! Shower us with perseverance, and let us die while submitting ˹to You˺.”
ai_translation: Your rage towards us is only because we believed in the signs of our Rabb when they came to us. Our Rabb! Shower us with perseverance, and let us die while submitting.”

ai.m: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
ai.g: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
ai.r: — (relative pronoun / particle)

ai.m: 'You hold a grievance against / take vengeance on / disapprove of'; a verb expressing resentment or punishing retribution for something one finds objectionable.
ai.g: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'). The final -u is the indicative mood ending, the default form used for an ongoing or general statement ('you take vengeance').
ai.r: ن-ق-م (n-q-m) — to resent, avenge, punish for a wrong

ai.m: "from us" — the preposition 'from' (indicating origin, source, or starting point) fused with the attached pronoun 'us'. It can also carry a partitive sense, 'some of us / a part of us'.
ai.g: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The base 'min' normally takes a vowelless final consonant, but before the pronoun '-nā' the nūn is doubled (assimilation), giving 'minnā'. The suffix '-nā' is the first-person plural object/possessive pronoun meaning 'us' or 'our'.
ai.r: — (preposition; the pronoun has no triliteral root)

ai.m: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
ai.g: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
ai.r: — (particle)

ai.m: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
ai.g: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
ai.r: — (particle; no root)

ai.m: We have believed; we have come to faith and trust — to affirm belief, give one's trust, and feel secure in that conviction, stated by a group about themselves.
ai.g: A past-tense verb on the form-IV pattern (āmana, 'to believe / to have faith'). The ending -nā (a single morpheme, نَا) attached to a past verb marks the subject as 'we'. The doubled 'n' heard in 'āmannā' comes from the verb stem's final 'n' meeting the 'n' that begins the -nā ending.
ai.r: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

ai.m: 'With/in the signs of…' — the preposition bi- joined to a plural noun meaning 'signs', 'tokens', or 'verses': evidences that point to a truth beyond themselves.
ai.g: bi- is a preposition meaning 'with/in' and always takes the genitive. āyāt is a sound feminine plural; its -i ending here is genitive, the case required after the preposition, and it typically also links to a following noun ('signs OF …').
ai.r: ء-ي-ي / ء-و-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token

ai.m: Our Lord, Master, and Sustainer: the One who owns, governs, nurtures, and brings to completion. Rabb combines ownership, authority, and loving cultivation of what He sustains; the '-our' joins the speakers to Him as those under His care.
ai.g: The noun rabb ('Lord, Master, Sustainer') with the attached possessive pronoun -nā ('our'). The -i before the pronoun is the genitive case, used after a preposition, after a calling/oath, or to link the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, own

ai.m: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the point that' something occurred — pointing to the moment a past event took place and often implying that one thing happened upon the completion of another. In other uses it can carry the sense of 'not yet'.
ai.g: A particle (a small connecting word), not a noun or verb, so it has no case or tense ending. It introduces a clause and links it in time to another event — most often 'when / as soon as' a past action happened.

ai.m: 'It/she came to us'; a past-tense verb of coming or arriving, with a grammatically feminine subject (such as a 'sign' or 'proof') reaching the speaker's group.
ai.g: A past-tense verb. The -at ending marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she/it'). The attached -nā is the object pronoun 'us', so the whole means 'it/she came to us'.
ai.r: ج-ي-أ (j-y-ʾ) — to come, arrive

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: 'Pour out! / Pour down!' — a command to make a liquid flow abundantly, and figuratively to bestow or shower something (such as strength or patience) lavishly and completely.
ai.g: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single male ('you, pour!'), from the causative (form IV) verb 'afragha' ('to pour out, to make flow'). The initial alif here is hamzat al-qaṭʿ — the permanent causative prefix that is built into every form IV verb and is always pronounced (never dropped); it is not a prosthetic helping vowel. The final consonant is left vowel-less (jussive), as is normal for an order.
ai.r: ف-ر-غ (f-r-gh) — to be empty; to pour out/empty

ai.m: 'Upon us' / 'over us' / 'against us' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, upon') with an attached 'us'. It conveys something resting on, incumbent upon, or bearing against the group.
ai.g: A preposition (ʿalā, 'upon/over') with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'us'). When a pronoun is attached, ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay-. Such prepositional phrases put their pronoun in the object/genitive role.

ai.m: Patience, steadfast endurance, self-restraint — the inner strength to bear hardship calmly, persevere, and hold oneself firm without complaint. A rich virtue: composure under trial and constancy in obedience.
ai.g: A masculine verbal noun, indefinite. The '-an' ending (written with a following alif) is the indefinite accusative, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb — the thing being given, poured, or brought about.
ai.r: ص-ب-ر (ṣ-b-r) — to be patient, endure, restrain oneself

ai.m: 'And take us fully / cause us to die (as believers)'; a request that Allah receive one's soul in full at death, the verb meaning to take something completely or in its entirety.

p.en: take in full / cause to die (Form V imperative stem)

ai.g: A command (imperative, Form V 'to take in full, receive a soul at death') addressed to a single masculine 'you', here a plea to Allah. The stem ends in a fixed fatha intrinsic to the imperative of this weak-final verb (تَوَفَّ). The attached -nā is the object 'us', giving 'take us fully / cause us to die'.
ai.r: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — to fulfil, complete, take in full

ai.m: A plural description meaning 'ones who submit (to Allah), Muslims'; an active participle for those who surrender themselves wholly to Allah in peace and obedience.
ai.g: An active participle (Form IV, pattern مُفۡعِل → مُسۡلِم, 'one who submits, surrenders to Allah'). The single-letter prefix mu- carries a damma; the consonants س-ل-م are the root. The -īna ending is the masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive case, used for objects, after prepositions, or to describe a state ('as ones who submit').
ai.r: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — peace, safety, wholehearted submission

title: Forgive me and my brother
situation: On returning to find his people worshipping the calf, after his anger with Harun, he prayed for forgiveness for himself and his brother and for God's mercy.
arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ اغۡفِرۡ لِىۡ وَلِاَخِىۡ وَ اَدۡخِلۡنَا فِىۡ رَحۡمَتِكَ ​ۖ  وَاَنۡتَ اَرۡحَمُ الرّٰحِمِيۡنَ‏
translation: Moses prayed, “My Lord! Forgive me and my brother! And admit us into Your mercy. You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.”
ai_translation: Moses prayed, “My Rabb! Forgive me and my brother! And admit us into Your mercy. You are the the Rahim of the merciful.”

ai.m: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
ai.g: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
ai.r: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
ai.g: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: Forgive! — a plea or command to pardon, to cover over and blot out wrongdoing. It carries the sense of veiling a fault so it is no longer held against the offender.
ai.g: A command (imperative) addressed to a single person: 'forgive!'. The vowelless final -r reflects the imperative form. It is commonly followed by 'us' or 'for me' to specify whom to pardon.
ai.r: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, conceal, and pardon; mercy that blots out sin

ai.m: 'to Me' or 'for Me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the first-person pronoun, expressing direction, benefit, or belonging toward the speaker.
ai.g: A preposition ('to/for') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me'). Together they express benefit, direction, or attribution toward the first person.

ai.m: And for / to my brother; the kinsman 'brother,' joined to 'and' and a preposition meaning 'for / belonging to,' with 'my' attached.
ai.g: The noun 'brother' carries the conjunction wa- ('and') and the preposition li- ('for / to'). The final -ī is the attached possessive pronoun 'my.' After a preposition the noun stands in the genitive, here absorbed into the possessive ending.
ai.r: أ-خ-و (ʾ-kh-w) — brotherhood, a brother

ai.m: And admit us / cause us to enter; to bring a group inside or into a state or place.
ai.g: A Form IV causative imperative (a command, amr: 'make/let enter'), prefixed with wa- ('and'). The opening hamza (a-) is the imperative hamza of Form IV, not a present-tense prefix — the corresponding present tense would instead begin with tu- (tudkhilu). The command addresses a single 'you' as the doer, and -nā ('us') is the object being admitted.
ai.r: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — to enter; (form IV) to bring/make enter

ai.m: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
ai.g: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
ai.r: — (particle)

ai.m: Your mercy / Your compassion — mercy understood as active tenderness, care, and the will to relieve and forgive, here possessed by the One addressed.
ai.g: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -i is the genitive ending (seen on the t before the suffix), the case used after a preposition or when a noun is possessed. The final -ka is 'your,' addressing a single male.
ai.r: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion, womb-like tenderness

ai.m: 'And You' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'you' (addressing a single male). The independent pronoun stresses the subject, as in 'and You [Yourself] …'.
ai.g: A connective 'and' plus a detached subject pronoun. 'anta' is the masculine-singular 'you'; as a standalone pronoun it adds emphasis or introduces a statement about the addressee ('You are …').

ai.m: Most merciful / more merciful — the superlative or comparative of 'merciful': the one whose mercy surpasses all others'.
ai.g: A comparative/superlative adjective on the pattern afʿal ('most/more …'). The final -u (ḍamma) is the nominative ending, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a word standing as a predicate.
ai.r: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion

ai.m: The merciful ones / those who show mercy — people characterized by compassion and tenderness toward others.
ai.g: A definite active participle (pattern fāʿil) in the masculine plural ('the merciful ones'). The ending -īna is the plural form used in the genitive or accusative case — typically when the word follows a preposition, is possessed ('… OF the merciful'), or is a direct object.
ai.r: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion

title: Allah is sufficient for us
who: Taught as the response of the contented believer
situation: Set against those who were displeased with how charity was distributed, the Qur'an teaches the believer's reply: contentment with God's decree and trust in His bounty.
arabic: وَلَوۡ اَنَّهُمۡ رَضُوۡا مَاۤ اٰتٰٮهُمُ اللّٰهُ وَرَسُوۡلُهٗۙ وَقَالُوۡا حَسۡبُنَا اللّٰهُ سَيُؤۡتِيۡنَا اللّٰهُ مِنۡ فَضۡلِهٖ وَ رَسُوۡلُهٗۙ اِنَّاۤ اِلَى اللّٰهِ رٰغِبُوۡنَ‏
translation: If only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger had given them and said, “Allah is sufficient for us! Allah will grant us out of His bounty, and so will His Messenger. To Allah ˹alone˺ we turn with hope.”
ai_translation: If only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger had given them and said, “Allah is sufficient for us! Allah will grant us out of His bounty, and so will His Messenger. To Allah we turn with hope.”

ai.m: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
ai.g: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').
ai.r: — (particles; no triliteral root)

ai.m: 'That they…' — an emphatic connector 'anna' ('that, indeed') fused with the pronoun 'they,' used to introduce an affirmed clause as the content of a thought or statement.
ai.g: Built on the particle 'anna' ('that…, indeed'), which introduces and affirms a following clause (often after verbs of knowing, thinking, or saying) and puts its noun into the accusative. The attached '-hum' is the pronoun 'they/them' for a male-inclusive group.

ai.m: They became content, satisfied, or pleased — to be well-pleased with what one has, to accept it gladly.
ai.g: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). It states a completed action: they came to be pleased.
ai.r: ر-ض-و (r-ḍ-w) — to be pleased, satisfied, content

ai.m: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
ai.g: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

ai.m: He gave / granted / bestowed upon them — to bring, hand over, or confer (a gift or favour) to someone.
ai.g: A past-tense (perfect) verb in Form IV ('to give/bestow'). With no subject suffix, it is third-person masculine singular ('he did'). The attached object pronoun 'them' (here voweled '-humu' to connect to the next word) gives 'he bestowed upon them.'
ai.r: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (Form IV) to bring, give, bestow

ai.m: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
ai.g: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
ai.r: — (proper divine name)

ai.m: "And His Messenger," the one sent with a message; "rasūl" denotes an envoy or apostle commissioned to deliver something, here belonging to "Him."
ai.g: The "wa-" prefix means "and." The base "rasūl" is a noun of the faʿūl pattern meaning "one who is sent." The suffix "-hu" is the attached possessive pronoun "his," placing the noun in a possessive "messenger of Him" relationship; the pronoun occupies the genitive slot.
