ai.r: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a message or the one sent with it

ai.m: And they said — to utter or declare in speech, with the action presented as completed by a group.
ai.g: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. 'qāla' is the past-tense verb 'to say'; the '-ū' suffix marks a completed action done by 'they' (a masculine or mixed group). The stem shown here ('qālu') carries only the stem vowel before the suffix, with the plural '-ū' supplied by the separate ending. Past tense, so the speaking is presented as already finished.
ai.r: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak

ai.m: Means 'enough for us / our sufficiency'. The base word 'ḥasb' denotes that which suffices and satisfies — a sufficiency that makes anything more unnecessary; with the attached pronoun, 'sufficient for us / all we need'.
ai.g: A noun functioning as a predicate ('[is] enough'), carrying the nominative -u ending typical of the thing being asserted. The attached -nā means 'us / for us / our', so the phrase reads 'our sufficiency' or 'enough for us'.
ai.r: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — to reckon, count; to suffice, be enough

ai.m: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
ai.g: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
ai.r: — (proper divine name)

ai.m: He will soon give us — combining the near-future sense 'soon/shortly' with the act of giving, bringing, or bestowing upon us.
ai.g: A present-tense verb turned into the future by the prefix sa- ('will, shortly'). The ya-…-ī shape marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The attached -nā is the object pronoun 'us'.
ai.r: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to give, bring

ai.m: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
ai.g: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
ai.r: — (proper divine name)

ai.m: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
ai.g: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
ai.r: — (preposition)

ai.m: 'His bounty / grace / favor' — faḍl is overflowing generosity, an extra goodness given beyond what is owed; with the attached pronoun it means the bounty belonging to Him (Allah).
ai.g: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-hi' ('his/His'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, which typically appears after a preposition or links the noun to what follows in an 'of' relationship; here it carries through to the possessor.
ai.r: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — excess, surplus; hence bounty, grace, superiority

ai.m: "And His Messenger," the one sent with a message; "rasūl" denotes an envoy or apostle commissioned to deliver something, here belonging to "Him."
ai.g: The "wa-" prefix means "and." The base "rasūl" is a noun of the faʿūl pattern meaning "one who is sent." The suffix "-hu" is the attached possessive pronoun "his," placing the noun in a possessive "messenger of Him" relationship; the pronoun occupies the genitive slot.
ai.r: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a message or the one sent with it

ai.m: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
ai.g: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

ai.m: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
ai.g: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

ai.m: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
ai.g: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

ai.m: Ones who earnestly desire, yearn, or set their hopes (toward something) — eager, longing seekers.
ai.g: An active participle (a doer-noun, 'ones who desire') in the masculine plural. The -ūna ending marks the plural in the nominative case — the form a noun takes as the subject or as a predicate describing 'they'.
ai.r: ر-غ-ب (r-gh-b) — to desire, long for, aspire to

title: Do not make us a trial for the oppressors
situation: Few dared follow Musa for fear of Pharaoh; those who did declared their reliance on God and asked not to be made a test in the hands of the wrongdoers.
arabic: فَقَالُوۡا عَلَى اللّٰهِ تَوَكَّلۡنَا​ ۚ رَبَّنَا لَا تَجۡعَلۡنَا فِتۡنَةً لِّـلۡقَوۡمِ الظّٰلِمِيۡنَۙ‏  وَنَجِّنَا بِرَحۡمَتِكَ مِنَ الۡقَوۡمِ الۡكٰفِرِيۡنَ‏
translation: (85) They replied, “In Allah we trust. Our Lord! Do not subject us to the persecution of the oppressive people, (86) and deliver us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people.”
ai_translation: (85) They replied, “In Allah we trust. Our Rabb! Do not subject us to the persecution of the oppressive people,. (86) and deliver us by Your mercy from the rejecting the truth people.”

ai.m: '…so / then they said.' Combines the connector 'so/then' (showing result or sequence) with a past-tense verb of speaking, third person plural — a completed act of saying by a group.
ai.g: A completed-action (past) verb prefixed with 'fa-' ('so/then'), which links it to what precedes as a result or next step. The '-ū' ending (with silent trailing alif) marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural).
ai.r: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

ai.m: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
ai.g: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
ai.r: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

ai.m: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
ai.g: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

ai.m: 'We have placed our trust, relied wholly (upon someone).' The root means to entrust an affair, to depend on and commit oneself; this pattern expresses fully delegating one's reliance. The subject is 'we.'
ai.g: A past-tense verb in a reflexive pattern ('to commit one's reliance, put one's trust'). The suffix -nā marks the subject 'we' ('we put our trust').
ai.r: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — to entrust, rely upon, commit an affair

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
ai.g: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

ai.m: You place us / make us: a present-tense verb of putting, setting, or rendering something into a state, with an attached pronoun 'us' as its object.
ai.g: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix with no plural ending marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'). The bare (vowelless) ending shows the jussive mood, the form used after particles of command or prohibition. The attached -nā is the object pronoun 'us.'
ai.r: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, render, appoint

ai.m: A trial, test, temptation, affliction, or sedition. Fitna is a weighty term: originally the smelting of metal to test its purity, it comes to mean any testing or tribulation — persecution, civil strife, seductive enticement, or a probing ordeal that reveals what is within.
ai.g: An indefinite feminine noun. The ending -an (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a trial') and in the accusative case — typically the case of a direct object or of a noun functioning as the predicate after certain verbs.
ai.r: ف-ت-ن (f-t-n) — to test by fire, to try, to tempt, to afflict

ai.m: 'For the people / folk' — a community or nation of people, preceded by the preposition 'for / to'.
ai.g: A preposition 'li-' ('for / to') joined to the definite noun 'the people'. The -i ending is genitive, the case required after the preposition 'li-'. The combination 'li-' + 'al-' merges in writing and is pronounced 'lil-'.
ai.r: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — standing, rising; a group who stand together as a people

ai.m: The wrongdoers — those who do wrong or injustice; literally those who put things out of their rightful place, transgressing limits and harming themselves or others. The root sense is darkness.
ai.g: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', doubling it). The stem is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the object/genitive form of the sound masculine plural, marking the word as an object of a verb or governed by a preposition.
ai.r: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — darkness; wrongdoing, injustice

ai.m: 'And save / deliver us!' — a command (or plea) to rescue and bring to safety, with 'us' as the object. The 'wa-' is the connective 'and'.
ai.g: A connective 'wa-' ('and') with an intensive command verb (doubled middle letter, meaning 'rescue thoroughly'). It is addressed to a single 'you', with -nā ('us') attached as the object. As a command it expresses a request or plea ('do save us').
ai.r: ن-ج-و / ن-ج-ي (n-j-w/y) — deliverance, rescue, escape to safety

ai.m: 'By / with Your mercy' — mercy understood as tender compassion and active kindness, here preceded by 'by/with' (indicating means) and possessed by 'You'.
ai.g: A preposition 'bi-' ('by / with', often indicating the means) attached to the noun 'mercy', which carries the possessive -ka ('Your', addressing one male). The -i vowel reflects the genitive case required after 'bi-'. The final 't' sound is the feminine noun-ending heard when a possessor follows.
ai.r: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion, womb-like tenderness

ai.m: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
ai.g: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

ai.m: 'The people / the folk' — a collective noun for a community, nation, or group of people regarded as a body. Often it carries the nuance of one's own people or a particular group sharing a trait.
ai.g: A collective noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-i' is the genitive ending, which typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship.
ai.r: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand/rise; a people, community

ai.m: The disbelievers / the ungrateful — those who reject faith and cover over the truth; the word also carries the sense of covering up or being ungrateful for what one has been given.
ai.g: 'al-' is 'the'. The stem is an active participle ('one who disbelieves/is ungrateful') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the accusative/genitive form of the sound masculine plural: it marks the word as an object of a verb or as governed by a preposition, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
ai.r: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; ingratitude, disbelief

title: I seek refuge from asking in ignorance
situation: After he pleaded for his drowning son and was gently corrected, Nuh sought refuge in God from ever again asking for something of which he had no knowledge.
arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ اِنِّىۡۤ اَعُوۡذُ بِكَ اَنۡ اَسۡــَٔلَكَ مَا لَـيۡسَ لِىۡ بِهٖ عِلۡمٌ​ؕ وَاِلَّا تَغۡفِرۡ لِىۡ وَتَرۡحَمۡنِىۡۤ اَكُنۡ مِّنَ الۡخٰسِرِيۡنَ‏
translation: Noah pleaded, “My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking You about what I have no knowledge of, and unless You forgive me and have mercy on me, I will be one of the losers.”
ai_translation: Noah pleaded, “My Rabb, I seek refuge in You from asking You about what I have no knowledge of, and unless You forgive me and have mercy on me, I will be one of the losers.”

ai.m: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
ai.g: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
ai.r: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
ai.g: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
ai.g: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

ai.m: 'I seek refuge / protection' — to take shelter in and appeal to someone (Allah) for safety against an evil or danger. Conveys turning to a protector for guarding.

p.en: seek refuge / take shelter (stem, ending in the indicative vowel -u)

ai.g: A present-tense verb 'to seek refuge'. The opening alif (a-) marks the subject as 'I'. The stem ends in the third root letter ذ, which carries the final short vowel -u; this -u is the indicative ending, signalling a real, ongoing action — a plain statement ('I seek refuge') rather than a command or a 'that…' form.
ai.r: ع-و-ذ (ʿ-w-dh) — to seek refuge, take shelter, protect oneself

ai.m: With You / in You — the preposition 'with/by/in' joined to the pronoun 'You' (addressing a single person), expressing reliance upon or recourse to that person.
ai.g: The preposition bi- ('with/in/by') with the attached pronoun -ka ('you', addressing one male). Pronouns following a preposition take this object form.

ai.m: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
ai.g: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
ai.r: — (particle; no root)

ai.m: I ask, request, or question you — to put a request or a question to someone.
ai.g: A present-tense verb with the a- prefix marking a first-person singular ('I') subject. The -a ending is the subjunctive mood, used after particles meaning 'that / so that / lest', expressing a purpose or a hypothetical rather than a plain fact. The attached -ka ('you') is the object.
ai.r: س-ا-ل (s-ʾ-l) — to ask, question, request

ai.m: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
ai.g: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

ai.m: A special negating verb meaning 'is not / are not'. Unlike a simple particle, it behaves like a verb (frozen in the past-tense form) and serves to deny that something is the case, cancelling an assertion of being.
ai.g: A defective verb fixed in the 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it is not'). The final -a is its frozen ending; it does not conjugate for tense like other verbs. Grammatically it raises its subject to the nominative and puts its predicate in the accusative, functioning to negate a state of being.
ai.r: ل-ي-س (l-y-s) — negation, not-being

ai.m: 'to Me' or 'for Me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the first-person pronoun, expressing direction, benefit, or belonging toward the speaker.
ai.g: A preposition ('to/for') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me'). Together they express benefit, direction, or attribution toward the first person.

ai.m: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
ai.g: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

ai.m: A noun meaning 'knowledge' — sure, established knowing; awareness of facts based on evidence, the opposite of ignorance or guesswork.
ai.g: A singular noun. The -un ending is the indefinite nominative: the 'n' sound (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('some knowledge', not 'the knowledge'), and the nominative case typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing whose existence is being affirmed.
ai.r: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; knowledge

ai.m: And if not / and unless — a compound joining 'and' with a conditional 'if not', introducing the alternative outcome should something not happen.
ai.g: A particle cluster: the conjunction wa- ('and') joined to the conditional in ('if') merged with the negative lā ('not'), together meaning 'and if … not' or 'and unless'. Particles do not take case endings.

ai.m: To cover over, pardon, and forgive — especially sins, blotting them out and shielding the wrongdoer from their consequences. The form is a present-tense verb addressed to a single male: 'you forgive / you cover over (sins).'
ai.g: A present/imperfect verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person singular masculine subject ('you'). The bare -ir ending with no added vowel reflects a jussive/conditional or otherwise unmarked mood (as after a conditional particle), rather than the plain indicative which would end in -u.
ai.r: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, pardon, forgive

ai.m: 'to Me' or 'for Me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the first-person pronoun, expressing direction, benefit, or belonging toward the speaker.
ai.g: A preposition ('to/for') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me'). Together they express benefit, direction, or attribution toward the first person.

t.en: and You have mercy on me

ai.m: And you show mercy, compassion, or tender forgiveness to me — to treat with kindness and spare from harm.
ai.g: A present-tense verb with the prefixed wa- ('and') and the ta- prefix marking a second-person ('you') subject. The form lacks a final case vowel because it stands in the jussive/subjunctive mood used after conditional or purpose particles. The object 'me' is built from two morphemes: the 'protective nūn' (nūn al-wiqāya) -ni, which guards the verb ending, followed by the first-person pronoun -ī ('me').
ai.r: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion, tenderness

ai.m: A verb meaning 'I am / I happen to be,' here in a shortened (jussive) form. It is the core verb of being/existing used to link a subject to a state or description. In a shortened form like this it is typically tied to a negation or condition, yielding a sense such as 'I was (not)' or 'should I be.'
ai.g: A present-tense verb 'to be,' first-person singular ('I'), in the shortened jussive mood marked by the bare final consonant with a silent stop (sukūn) instead of a vowel. This clipped ending is what a particle of negation or condition produces, so the verb commonly carries a past-negative ('I was not') or conditional ('were I to be') sense rather than a plain present.
ai.r: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

ai.m: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
ai.g: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

ai.m: "The losers / those who lose" — an active participle for those who suffer loss, who lose out or come to ruin, especially the ultimate loss of one's own soul.
ai.g: An active participle in the masculine sound plural with the definite article 'the'. The -īna ending marks the accusative or genitive case — the form used when such a plural is a direct object, a predicate of 'to be', or follows a preposition (as opposed to the -ūna subject form).
ai.r: خ-س-ر (kh-s-r) — to lose / suffer loss / be ruined

title: Let me die in submission to You
situation: Raised to power in Egypt and reunited with his family, at the height of his blessings he thanked God and asked to die a Muslim and be joined with the righteous.
arabic: رَبِّ قَدۡ اٰتَيۡتَنِىۡ مِنَ الۡمُلۡكِ وَ عَلَّمۡتَنِىۡ مِنۡ تَاۡوِيۡلِ الۡاَحَادِيۡثِ​ ۚ فَاطِرَ السَّمٰوٰتِ وَالۡاَرۡضِ اَنۡتَ وَلِىّٖ فِى الدُّنۡيَا وَالۡاٰخِرَةِ​ ۚ تَوَفَّنِىۡ مُسۡلِمًا وَّاَلۡحِقۡنِىۡ بِالصّٰلِحِيۡنَ‏
translation: “My Lord! You have surely granted me authority and taught me the interpretation of dreams. ˹O˺ Originator of the heavens and the earth! You are my Guardian in this world and the Hereafter. Allow me to die as one who submits and join me with the righteous.”
ai_translation: “My Rabb! You have surely granted me authority and taught me the interpretation of dreams. O Originator of the heavens and the earth! You are my Guardian in this dunya — this temporary worldly life and the Akhirah. Allow me to die as one who submits and join me with the righteous.”

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
ai.g: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
ai.g: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.
ai.r: — (no triliteral root; an emphasizing particle)

ai.m: Means "you gave me" — the act of granting, bestowing, or handing over something, completed in the past, done by "you" to "me."
ai.g: A completed (past-tense) verb. The -ta ending marks a masculine singular "you" as the doer; the attached -nī ("me") is the object receiving the action, with the -n- buffering the verb before the pronoun.
ai.r: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to bring, give, bestow

ai.m: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
ai.g: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

ai.m: The dominion, kingship, sovereign power — al-mulk is rule and possession on the grandest scale: the authority of a king, the realm ruled, and the very power to command and dispose. It denotes sovereignty itself.
ai.g: A masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case, typically marking it as the second term of a possessive phrase ('… OF the dominion') or as governed by a preceding preposition.
ai.r: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — ownership, dominion, sovereignty

ai.m: Means "and you taught me" — the act of instructing or imparting knowledge, completed in the past, done by "you" to "me," prefixed with "and."
ai.g: The prefix wa- means "and." The verb is a completed (past-tense) intensive (form II, doubled middle root) meaning "to teach." The -ta ending marks a masculine singular "you" as the doer; the attached -nī ("me") is the object, with the -n- buffering the verb before the pronoun.
ai.r: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge, knowing

ai.m: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
ai.g: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
ai.r: — (preposition)

ai.m: 'Interpretation / explanation / outcome' — the verbal noun for tracing something back to its origin, meaning, or final result; especially the proper interpretation of dreams, statements, or events.
ai.g: A Form II (tafʿīl) verbal noun. The final -i is genitive: it typically links this word to a following noun in an 'interpretation OF …' relationship, or marks it as the object of a preposition.
ai.r: أ-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — to return/trace back to an origin or end

ai.m: 'Reports / accounts / sayings' — the plural of a word for a piece of speech, narrative, or item of news; that which is related or told.
ai.g: A broken (irregular) plural with the definite article 'al-'. The final -i is genitive, the case used when the word follows a preposition or is possessed by / attached to a preceding noun ('of the reports / accounts').
ai.r: ح-د-ث (ḥ-d-th) — to happen anew; to relate, report

ai.m: Means "Originator, Maker who brings into being" — one who splits non-existence open to fashion something entirely new, the One who creates from nothing.
ai.g: An active participle on the fāʿil pattern, naming the one who performs the act ("the one who originates"). The -a ending marks the accusative case, the case required by the word's own role in the sentence. It also commonly serves as the first term of a possessive ("… of …") construction, but in that role it still simply carries whatever case its function calls for.
ai.r: ف-ط-ر (f-ṭ-r) — to split open, originate, bring into being

ai.m: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
ai.g: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.
ai.r: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, sky

ai.m: Means "and the earth" — the ground, land, or world we stand on, prefixed with "and" and carrying "the."
ai.g: The prefix wa- means "and" and l- is "the." The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun in a possessive ("… of …") relationship or follows a preposition.
ai.r: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land, ground

ai.m: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
ai.g: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

ai.m: Means "my guardian, protector, patron" — a close ally and caretaker who stands near, takes charge of one's affairs, and gives protection and support; joined to the marker for "my."
ai.g: A noun on the intensive faʿīl pattern bearing the attached pronoun -ī, "my," which marks the protector as belonging to the speaker. The -ī suffix is the first-person singular possessive ending.
ai.r: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, guardianship, allegiance

ai.m: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
ai.g: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
ai.r: — (particle)

ai.m: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
ai.g: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
ai.r: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

ai.m: And the Hereafter / the final, lasting life — the world to come after death, contrasted with the present worldly life.
ai.g: The prefix wa- means 'and' and al- means 'the'. The stem is a feminine adjective used as a noun, 'the Last (abode/life)', i.e. the Hereafter. The final -i is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun or follows a preposition or oath particle.
ai.r: أ-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — being last, coming after, the end

ai.m: Means "take me in full, cause me to pass away" — a command to receive someone completely (especially to take a soul at death), addressed to "you" and directed at "me."
ai.g: A command (imperative, form V) directed at a single "you." Its core sense is to take a thing in full measure, commonly used of taking a soul at death. The attached -nī ("me") is the object, with the -n- buffering the verb before the pronoun.
ai.r: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — fullness, completion, paying in full

ai.m: Means "as one who submits" — a person wholly surrendered and committed in obedience (a Muslim in the root sense of one who yields himself).
ai.g: An active participle (form IV) naming "one who submits/surrenders." The -an ending (accusative with tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and often signals a descriptive state ("as a …") or a verb's object.
ai.r: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — soundness, peace; (form IV) to surrender, submit

ai.m: Means "and join me, attach me" — a command to make someone reach and be joined to a group or thing, addressed to "you" and directed at "me," prefixed with "and."
ai.g: The prefix wa- means "and." The verb is a command (imperative, form IV) directed at a single "you," meaning to cause something to catch up with and be joined to another. The attached -nī ("me") is the object, with the -n- buffering the verb before the pronoun.
ai.r: ل-ح-ق (l-ḥ-q) — to catch up, follow, join, attach

ai.m: Means "with the righteous" — the upright, morally sound people whose deeds and character are good and in order; prefixed with "with/among."
ai.g: The prefix bi- means "with/by" and l- is "the." This is a sound masculine plural active participle ("those who are righteous"). Its ending -īna is a single, inseparable unit marking the oblique (genitive/accusative) plural, used here after the preposition; it replaces the nominative plural ending -ūna.
ai.r: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — soundness, righteousness, setting things right

title: Make this city safe
situation: Settling his family in the barren valley of Mecca, he prayed for the city's security, for his descendants to keep up prayer, and for forgiveness for himself, his parents, and all believers.
arabic: وَاِذۡ قَالَ اِبۡرٰهِيۡمُ رَبِّ اجۡعَلۡ هٰذَا الۡبَلَدَ اٰمِنًا وَّاجۡنُبۡنِىۡ وَبَنِىَّ اَنۡ نَّـعۡبُدَ الۡاَصۡنَامَؕ‏  رَبِّ اِنَّهُنَّ اَضۡلَلۡنَ كَثِيۡرًا مِّنَ النَّاسِ​ۚ فَمَنۡ تَبِعَنِىۡ فَاِنَّهٗ مِنِّىۡ​ۚ وَمَنۡ عَصَانِىۡ فَاِنَّكَ غَفُوۡرٌ رَّحِيۡمٌ‏  رَبَّنَاۤ اِنِّىۡۤ اَسۡكَنۡتُ مِنۡ ذُرِّيَّتِىۡ بِوَادٍ غَيۡرِ ذِىۡ زَرۡعٍ عِنۡدَ بَيۡتِكَ الۡمُحَرَّمِۙ رَبَّنَا لِيُقِيۡمُوۡا الصَّلٰوةَ فَاجۡعَلۡ اَ فۡـٮِٕدَةً مِّنَ النَّاسِ تَهۡوِىۡۤ اِلَيۡهِمۡ وَارۡزُقۡهُمۡ مِّنَ الثَّمَرٰتِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَشۡكُرُوۡنَ‏  رَبَّنَاۤ اِنَّكَ تَعۡلَمُ مَا نُخۡفِىۡ وَمَا نُعۡلِنُ​ ؕ وَمَا يَخۡفٰى عَلَى اللّٰهِ مِنۡ شَىۡءٍ فِى الۡاَرۡضِ وَلَا فِى السَّمَآءِ‏  اَلۡحَمۡدُ لِلّٰهِ الَّذِىۡ وَهَبَ لِىۡ عَلَى الۡـكِبَرِ اِسۡمٰعِيۡلَ وَاِسۡحٰقَ​ؕ اِنَّ رَبِّىۡ لَسَمِيۡعُ الدُّعَآءِ‏  رَبِّ اجۡعَلۡنِىۡ مُقِيۡمَ الصَّلٰوةِ وَمِنۡ ذُرِّيَّتِىۡ​​ ۖ  رَبَّنَا وَتَقَبَّلۡ دُعَآءِ‏  رَبَّنَا اغۡفِرۡ لِىۡ وَلـِوَالِدَىَّ وَلِلۡمُؤۡمِنِيۡنَ يَوۡمَ يَقُوۡمُ الۡحِسَابُ‏ ﻿﻿
translation: (35) ˹Remember˺ when Abraham prayed, “My Lord! Make this city ˹of Mecca˺ secure, and keep me and my children away from the worship of idols. (36) My Lord! They have caused many people to go astray. So whoever follows me is with me, and whoever disobeys me—then surely You are ˹still˺ All-Forgiving, Most Merciful. (37) Our Lord! I have settled some of my offspring in a barren valley, near Your Sacred House, our Lord, so that they may establish prayer. So make the hearts of ˹believing˺ people incline towards them and provide them with fruits, so perhaps they will be thankful. (38) Our Lord! You certainly know what we conceal and what we reveal. Nothing on earth or in heaven is hidden from Allah. (39) All praise is for Allah who has blessed me with Ishmael and Isaac in my old age. My Lord is indeed the Hearer of ˹all˺ prayers. (40) My Lord! Make me and those ˹believers˺ of my descendants keep up prayer. Our Lord! Accept my prayers. (41) Our Lord! Forgive me, my parents, and the believers on the Day when the judgment will come to pass.”
ai_translation: (35) Recall when Abraham prayed: "My Rabb, make this city secure, and keep me and my children away from worship of idols. (36) My Rabb, they have led many astray. Whoever follows me is with me; whoever disobeys me—You are still All-Forgiving, the Rahim whose special mercy awaits believers in the Akhirah. (37) Our Rabb, I settled part of my offspring in an uncultivated valley near Your Sacred House, so they may establish salah. Turn the hearts of believing people toward them and provide them fruits, so they may be grateful. (38) Our Rabb, You know what we conceal and reveal. Nothing on earth or in heaven is hidden from Allah. (39) All praise belongs to Allah who blessed me with Ishmael and Isaac in my old age. My Rabb is the Hearer of prayers. (40) My Rabb, make me and those of my descendants who believe keep up salah. Our Rabb, accept my prayer. (41) Our Rabb, forgive me, my parents, and the believers on the Day judgment arrives."

ai.m: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
ai.g: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

ai.m: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
ai.g: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
ai.r: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

ai.m: A proper noun: Abraham (Ibrāhīm), the patriarch and prophet, exalted as an upright monotheist and 'friend of Allah'.
ai.g: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence. Because it is a foreign proper name, it is 'diptote' — it does not take the indefinite 'n' sound (tanwīn) that ordinary nouns would.

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
ai.g: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: Make! / Render! — a command to bring something into a state or to appoint/turn one thing into another. The verb jaʿala can mean to make, set, place, or designate.
ai.g: A second-person masculine singular imperative ('you, make!'). The opening 'i-' is a helping vowel that lets the consonant cluster be pronounced, and the silent (jussive) ending with no final vowel is characteristic of the command form addressed to one male.
ai.r: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, set, place, appoint, render

ai.m: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
ai.g: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

ai.m: A town, settled place, or land — a defined inhabited locality, as opposed to open wilderness. It denotes a place of human dwelling and community.
ai.g: A definite singular noun ('the town'). The final -a ending is accusative, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb or as the focus of certain particles.
ai.r: ب-ل-د (b-l-d) — land, territory, settled locality

ai.m: Āmin — safe and secure; a place or person free from fear and danger, enjoying peace and protection.
ai.g: An indefinite active participle ('safe / secure'). The -an ending is accusative with nunation, commonly marking a descriptive word (modifying an accusative noun) or a predicate; the nunation signals it is indefinite. It describes the quality of being secure and free from fear.
ai.r: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be safe, secure, free from fear

ai.m: 'And keep me away (from)' / 'remove me far from' — a command addressed to Allah asking to be distanced and shielded from something. It combines a connecting 'and' with a request for protective separation.
ai.g: A command verb (imperative) with an attached object pronoun. The imperative form directs someone to perform the action; the suffix -nī means 'me' as the one acted upon. The opening wa- links it to a preceding statement.
ai.r: ج-ن-ب (j-n-b) — side, to set aside, to keep at a distance

ai.m: 'And my sons' / 'and my children' — the male offspring, here joined to a possessor by 'my'. It refers to one's own descendants as a group.
ai.g: A plural noun ('sons') with the attached possessive 'my'. With the first-person 'my' suffix, the case ending is absorbed, so the same form can serve as subject, object, or object of a preposition; context supplies the role. The opening wa- means 'and'.
ai.r: ب-ن-و / ب-ن-ي (b-n-w / b-n-y) — son, offspring, to build

ai.m: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
ai.g: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
ai.r: — (particle; no root)

ai.m: We worship / we serve and devote ourselves (to). It expresses the act of rendering humble worship, obedience, and submission to a deity, performed by a group ('we').
ai.g: A present/imperfect verb in the first-person plural ('we'), signaled by the n- prefix; the prefix carries a shadda (a doubled/geminated nūn, nna-) because it assimilates a preceding particle. The final -a ending marks the subjunctive mood, which typically appears after particles meaning 'that', 'so that', or 'in order to', giving a sense of '(that) we worship'.
ai.r: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, serve, submit

ai.m: The idols — carved images or statues set up and worshipped besides Allah. The word denotes physical objects of false worship.
ai.g: A definite broken (irregular) plural of ṣanam, 'idol'. The final -a ending is accusative, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb.
ai.r: ص-ن-م (ṣ-n-m) — idol, carved image

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
ai.g: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: 'Indeed they (feminine plural)' — an emphasis particle 'inna' (truly, certainly) fused with the pronoun 'they' referring to a group of feminine or non-rational things. It opens a statement with stress and certainty.
ai.g: The emphasizing particle inna ('indeed, certainly') with an attached subject pronoun. Inna adds strong affirmation to the sentence it begins; the suffix -hunna means 'they' for a feminine or non-rational plural group.

ai.m: 'They (feminine) led astray' / 'caused to go wrong' — a completed action of making others lose the right way, performed by a feminine or non-rational plural subject. The verb is causative: not merely going astray, but leading others into error.
ai.g: A past-tense (completed) causative verb. The -na suffix marks a third-person feminine plural subject ('they' for women or non-rational things) acting in the past. The aF-pattern (form IV) gives it the sense of causing the action in others.
ai.r: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, lose the way

ai.m: An adjective/noun meaning 'many', 'much', or 'numerous' — a large quantity or great number of something.
ai.g: Adjective/noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the final -an (nunation with fatḥa). The accusative typically marks a verb's object or an indefinite quantity, and the doubled-n sound shows the word is indefinite ('many').
ai.r: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, abundant

ai.m: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
ai.g: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

ai.m: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
ai.g: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
ai.r: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

ai.m: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
ai.g: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

ai.m: '(Whoever) follows me' / 'has followed me' — a completed act of following, accompanying, or imitating, with 'me' as the one followed. It implies taking someone as a leader or example.
ai.g: A past-tense (completed) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he followed'), with the attached object pronoun -nī, 'me'. The bare past form ends in -a, which marks 'he/it' as the doer; this fatha belongs to the verb stem, not to the pronoun.
ai.r: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

ai.m: A cluster of three elements: a connective 'so/then', the emphasis particle 'inna' that strongly affirms a statement ('indeed, truly'), and 'he/it'. Together: 'so indeed he / then truly it'.
ai.g: 'fa-' is a connecting particle showing sequence or consequence ('so, then'). 'inna' is an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the sentence that follows and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The attached 'hu' is that pronoun, 'he/it', here serving as the subject being emphasized.

ai.m: From me; indicating origin, belonging, or association with the speaker — 'coming from me' or 'of my side'.
ai.g: The preposition min ('from/of') with the attached pronoun -ī ('me'). An extra n is inserted (giving the doubled 'nn') to join the preposition smoothly to the pronoun. The -ī is the first-person singular pronoun 'me/my'.
ai.r: — (particle/preposition; no root)

ai.m: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
ai.g: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.
ai.r: — (pronoun/particle; no triliteral root)

ai.m: '(Whoever) disobeys me' / 'has disobeyed me' — a completed act of rebelling against or refusing to obey, with 'me' as the one defied. It denotes resistance to a command or authority.
ai.g: A past-tense (completed) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he disobeyed'), with the attached object pronoun -nī, 'me'. The bare form with no added subject ending marks 'he/it' as the doer. The root's final weak letter appears as the long ā before the pronoun.
ai.r: ع-ص-ي (ʿ-ṣ-y) — to disobey, rebel, resist

ai.m: A two-part opener meaning roughly 'then/so, truly You …': a connecting 'then/so' joined to an emphatic particle that asserts what follows with certainty, plus an attached 'You.' The emphatic particle (inna) strongly affirms the statement, like saying 'indeed' or 'it is certainly the case that.'
ai.g: A particle cluster, not a verb. fa- is a connector ('then, so, and thus'). inna is an emphatic/affirming particle that places the following noun or pronoun in the accusative; here that pronoun is the attached -ka ('you,' one male), the topic being emphasized. There is no tense or case ending of its own.
ai.r: — (particles; no root)

ai.m: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'much-forgiving, ever-ready to forgive, one who veils and pardons faults again and again'. The form stresses abundance, so it conveys forgiveness as a constant, far-reaching quality.
ai.g: An intensive adjective (the ghafūr 'doer-in-abundance' pattern), used as a divine attribute of Allah. The -un ending is nunation in the nominative case: it marks the word as indefinite and in the nominative, the case typically used for the subject or for a predicate that describes the subject.
ai.r: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, veil, forgive

ai.m: Most merciful, ever-merciful; one whose mercy is constant and abundant. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's enduring, all-embracing compassion toward His creation.
ai.g: An intensive adjective on the form faʿīl ('abundantly/constantly merciful'). The ending -un (tanwīn) is the nominative case with indefiniteness, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it ('[He] is most merciful').
ai.r: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion, womb-like tenderness

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
ai.g: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

ai.m: 'I settled / caused to dwell' — a completed action of placing someone in a dwelling so they may reside there, done by 'I'. It is causative: making another take up residence in a place.
ai.g: A past-tense (completed) causative verb. The suffix -tu marks 'I' as the doer in the past. The aF-pattern (form IV) gives the sense of causing someone else to dwell or settle.
ai.r: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — to be still, to dwell, to reside

ai.m: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
ai.g: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
ai.r: — (preposition)

ai.m: My offspring, descendants, or progeny. 'Dhurriyya' is one's children and their line of descent; the attached pronoun makes it 'my.'
ai.g: A noun with the first-person singular possessive ending -ī ('my'). The original feminine ending of the noun appears as -t before this pronoun. The attached -ī ('my') is the same form whether the noun is subject, object, or possessor.
ai.r: ذ-ر-ر / ذ-ر-ا (dh-r-r / dh-r-ʾ) — to scatter, multiply, produce offspring

ai.m: 'In a valley' — a low course or hollow between mountains or high ground, often a watercourse. The leading 'bi' marks location: within or at such a place.
ai.g: The preposition bi- ('in, at, with') attached to an indefinite noun. The -in ending is the indefinite genitive ('a valley'), the case regularly required after a preposition.
ai.r: و-د-ي (w-d-y) — valley, watercourse

ai.m: Other than / different from. A noun used to negate or exclude — it points to something that is not the thing mentioned, marking difference or absence.
ai.g: A noun of exception/negation meaning 'something other than'. The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition. So it sets up the sense 'other than [the following thing]'.
ai.r: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, change

ai.m: Possessor of / the one having — a relational word meaning 'owner of' or 'endowed with,' used to attach a quality or relationship to the noun it describes.
ai.g: A relational noun meaning 'owner/possessor of,' which must be followed by another noun ('possessor OF …'). It declines for case: dhū (nominative), dhī (genitive), dhā (accusative). The form dhī (ending -ī) is its genitive, used when it follows a preposition or describes a preceding genitive noun. It never stands alone; it always governs a following noun.
ai.r: — (a relational noun meaning 'possessor of'; no verbal root)

ai.m: Sown crops, cultivated growth, or tillage — plants grown by sowing seed, and by extension the act or produce of cultivation. It evokes vegetation that people raise for food.
ai.g: An indefinite singular noun. The -in ending is the indefinite genitive ('of crops' or 'a crop'), the case typically used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun in a possessive ('… of …') relation.
ai.r: ز-ر-ع (z-r-ʿ) — to sow, to cultivate, to grow plants

ai.m: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
ai.g: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').
ai.r: — (adverb of place)

ai.m: Your house, home, or dwelling; the place where one resides and spends the night. The root is tied to spending the night and settling in a place of abode.
ai.g: A noun carrying the -i genitive ending, which typically follows a preposition or marks the word as joined to a possessor in a chain ('… OF …'). The suffix -ka means 'your' (one male), so 'your house'.
ai.r: ب-ي-ت (b-y-t) — to spend the night, lodge; hence a house or dwelling.

ai.m: 'The sacred / forbidden one' — that which has been made inviolable and set apart, so that violating it is prohibited. Applied to a place, it marks a sanctuary whose sanctity must not be transgressed.
ai.g: A definite passive participle (pattern muFaʿʿaL) meaning 'something that has been made sacred/inviolable.' The -i ending is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition.
ai.r: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — to forbid, to make sacred or inviolable

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: 'So that they may establish / perform' — purpose ('in order that') joined to the act of setting something up firmly and keeping it upright, done by 'they'. Of worship, it means to perform it properly and steadfastly.
ai.g: The purpose particle li- ('so that') before a present/future causative verb, putting it in the subjunctive mood (expressing intended result). The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'; the subjunctive drops the final -n that the indicative would have.
ai.r: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise, to set up and keep upright

ai.m: The ritual prayer (ṣalāh): the prescribed formal worship of standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah at appointed times. As a verbal noun it also carries the underlying sense of calling upon, supplicating, and blessing.
ai.g: A definite feminine noun. The -a ending is accusative: it generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. that which is established or performed), or the object of certain particles.
ai.r: ص-ل-و (ṣ-l-w) — prayer, worship, supplication

ai.m: 'So make / appoint / render' — a connecting 'so/then' joined to a command to bring something into a state, place it, or designate it. The verb can mean to make, to put, or to cause to become.
ai.g: A command verb (imperative), second-person masculine singular ('you make/put'), preceded by fa- ('so, then'), which links it to what came before as a consequence or sequel. The imperative directs the addressee to perform the action.
ai.r: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, to render, to place, to appoint

ai.m: Hearts — but specifically the inner faculty of feeling, longing, and devotion; the seat of the affections rather than merely the physical organ. It is a plural of fuʾād, denoting hearts that yearn and turn.
ai.g: A broken (irregular) plural of fuʾād, 'heart'. The -tan ending is indefinite accusative ('hearts'), which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb.
ai.r: ف-ء-د (f-ʾ-d) — the heart, the inner seat of feeling

ai.m: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
ai.g: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

ai.m: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
ai.g: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
ai.r: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

ai.m: '(That) incline / yearn toward' / 'tend longingly to' — to lean, fall, or be drawn toward something out of love and desire. It pictures hearts tilting eagerly in a direction.
ai.g: A present/future-tense verb, third-person feminine singular ('she/it inclines'), agreeing with a feminine or non-rational plural subject. The verb ends in the weak long -ī from its final-weak root.
ai.r: ه-و-ي (h-w-y) — to incline, to fall, to long for, to desire

ai.m: A particle-and-pronoun unit meaning 'toward them / to them' — indicating direction or the goal of a motion, attention, or address aimed at a group.
ai.g: The preposition ilā ('to / toward'), which shifts to the form ilay- when a pronoun attaches, plus the suffix -him ('them'). The pronoun is in the genitive/oblique form required after a preposition; the whole expresses direction toward a goal.
ai.r: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

ai.m: 'And provide them / sustain them' — a connecting 'and' joined to a command to grant provision (food, livelihood, all that sustains life), with 'them' as the recipients. It asks Allah to bestow sustenance.
ai.g: A command verb (imperative), second-person masculine singular ('you provide'), with the attached object pronoun -hum, 'them'. The opening wa- means 'and'. The imperative directs the addressee to grant provision.
ai.r: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — to provide, to bestow sustenance or livelihood

ai.m: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
ai.g: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

ai.m: 'the fruits,' 'the produce,' 'the crops' — the fruits and yields of plants and trees, taken collectively. By extension 'thamarāt' can mean the produce or beneficial outcomes that something brings forth.
ai.g: A definite sound feminine plural ('the fruits'). The '-āt' marks the feminine plural, and the final '-i' is the case-vowel that sound feminine plurals take for BOTH the genitive (after a preposition or in a possessive link) and the accusative (object) roles — they do not use a separate '-a.' 'Al-' makes it definite; the 'th' doubles because it is a 'sun letter' absorbing the 'l' of 'al-.'
ai.r: ث-م-ر (th-m-r) — to bear fruit; fruit, produce

ai.m: 'So that they may / perhaps they will.' A particle expressing hope, expectation, or purpose, fused with the pronoun 'them'; it introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome.

p.en: perhaps / so that / in hope that

ai.g: The particle laʿalla ('perhaps, in the hope that, so that') with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'), which serves as its subject. Laʿalla belongs to a family of particles that put a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; -hum is that fixed object form. It conveys hope or an intended purpose rather than certainty.
ai.r: — (particle with pronoun; no root)

ai.m: A verb meaning 'they give thanks / are grateful' — to acknowledge and show gratitude for good received, and to praise the giver.
ai.g: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks the doers as 'they' (masculine plural). The full -ūna ending is the indicative mood, the normal form for an ongoing or habitual action ('they give thanks / are grateful').
ai.r: ش-ك-ر (sh-k-r) — to thank, be grateful; gratitude

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: 'Indeed you' — an emphasis particle meaning 'truly / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'you', used to open a statement with certainty and stress about the person addressed.
ai.g: The emphasis particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with an attached pronoun. 'inna' adds strong assertion to a sentence and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The suffix '-ka' means 'you' (masculine singular) as its subject.

ai.m: You (masculine singular) know, are aware of, or have knowledge of something. A simple present-tense verb of knowing.
ai.g: A present/future-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'). The final -u ending is the indicative mood, used for a straightforward statement ('you know / you do know').
ai.r: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know, knowledge

ai.m: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
ai.g: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

ai.m: 'We conceal / hide' — to keep something hidden, secret, or out of sight, done by 'we'. It is the opposite of openly revealing.
ai.g: A present/future-tense causative verb (form IV). The nu- prefix marks a first-person plural subject, 'we'. It is indicative (a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual action), ending in the weak long -ī from its final-weak root.
ai.r: خ-ف-ي (kh-f-y) — to be hidden; (form IV) to conceal, to hide

ai.m: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
ai.g: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
ai.r: — (relative pronoun / particle)

ai.m: 'We make public / proclaim' — to bring something into the open, announce, or declare it openly, done by 'we'. It is the opposite of concealing.
ai.g: A present/future-tense causative verb (form IV). The nu- prefix marks a first-person plural subject, 'we'. The final -u ending is indicative, marking a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual action (as opposed to a command or a subjunctive 'that we …').
ai.r: ع-ل-ن (ʿ-l-n) — to be open/public; (form IV) to announce, to proclaim

ai.m: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
ai.g: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
ai.r: — (relative pronoun / particle)

ai.m: To be hidden, concealed, or unseen; to remain out of sight or knowledge. The verb describes something escaping notice or being kept from view.
ai.g: A present/imperfect verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he' or 'it'). The verb ends in a fixed final long vowel -ā (a 'weak' final-letter verb), and in this prefixed present form it conveys an ongoing or general action: 'is/remains hidden'.
ai.r: خ-ف-ي (kh-f-y) — to be hidden, concealed, unseen

ai.m: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
ai.g: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
ai.r: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

ai.m: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
ai.g: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

ai.m: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
ai.g: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
ai.r: — (preposition)

ai.m: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
ai.g: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
ai.r: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

ai.m: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
ai.g: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
ai.r: — (particle)

ai.m: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
ai.g: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').
ai.r: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land, ground

ai.m: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
ai.g: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

ai.m: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
ai.g: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
ai.r: — (particle)

ai.m: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
ai.g: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').
ai.r: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, loftiness; sky, heaven

ai.m: All praise, commendation, and grateful acknowledgement — the recognition that beauty, goodness, and perfection rightly belong to and are owed to the one being praised. As a definite noun with the article 'al-', it conveys that the totality of praise is encompassed.
ai.g: A definite noun (carrying the article 'al-', 'the'). The final '-u' ending is nominative: it marks the word as the subject or main topic of a statement — the thing being talked about or the doer of an action, rather than its object.
ai.r: ح-م-د (ḥ-m-d) — to praise, to commend, to give thanks

ai.m: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
ai.g: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

ai.m: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
ai.g: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

ai.m: 'He granted / bestowed (as a gift)' — a completed act of giving freely, with no expectation of return, as a pure gift. It denotes generous, gratuitous bestowal.
ai.g: A past-tense (completed) verb, third-person masculine singular. The bare stem ending in -a marks 'he/it' as the doer of the completed action ('he granted').
ai.r: و-ه-ب (w-h-b) — to give freely, to grant as a gift

ai.m: 'to Me' or 'for Me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the first-person pronoun, expressing direction, benefit, or belonging toward the speaker.
ai.g: A preposition ('to/for') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me'). Together they express benefit, direction, or attribution toward the first person.

ai.m: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
ai.g: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
ai.r: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

ai.m: Old age — the advanced stage of life, with its weakness and the passing of one's prime; also greatness or seniority in years. Here it carries the sense of being well advanced in age.
ai.g: A definite singular noun. The -i ending is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition.
ai.r: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — to be great, large; to grow old, advance in years

ai.m: Ishmael (Ismāʿīl) — the proper name of the prophet, son of Abraham. As a non-Arabic name it does not derive from an Arabic root.
ai.g: A proper name of foreign origin. Such names are diptotes: they take a single -a ending for both the accusative and genitive (they do not take the indefinite -un/-in 'nunation'). The -a here marks it as an object or as following a preposition.

ai.m: The proper name 'Isaac' (Isḥāq), the prophet, joined to the conjunction 'and.'
ai.g: Conjunction 'wa' (and) prefixed to a proper name. The final -a is the accusative/genitive ending; because this is a foreign (non-Arabic) name, it is grammatically 'diptote,' meaning it takes -a for both those cases and never takes nunation (the -n sound).
ai.r: — (proper name)

ai.m: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
ai.g: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

ai.m: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
ai.g: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

ai.m: 'Surely (is) all-hearing' — the emphatic 'la-' ('truly, surely') joined to the intensive name meaning 'One who hears all' — the perpetual, all-encompassing Hearer who hears every sound and prayer. The faʿīl pattern signals constancy and totality.
ai.g: The emphatic prefix la- ('surely, truly') on an intensive adjective/name (pattern faʿīl) meaning 'ever-hearing, all-hearing.' The final -u ending is nominative, which typically marks the word as a subject or predicate (the thing described). The la- adds strong affirmation.
ai.r: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — to hear, to listen

ai.m: A noun meaning 'the calling', 'the supplication', or 'the prayer of request' — the act of calling upon Allah, appealing, or invoking.
ai.g: A definite verbal noun ('the supplication'), marked by the prefix al- ('the'). The final -i vowel is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF supplication') or follows a preposition.
ai.r: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — calling, supplicating

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
ai.g: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: Place me, appoint me, set me (in a position or role). The command 'make/place', given to a single addressee, with an attached 'me' — a request to be put in charge of or assigned to something.
ai.g: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a single person, 'make/place/appoint'. The stem ends in a sukūn (no vowel) as commands of this verb do. The suffix -nī is the object 'me' (the -n- links the verb cleanly to the 'me' pronoun).
ai.r: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, set, render, appoint

ai.m: One who establishes, sets up, or keeps something firmly upright and ongoing; an active doer who causes a thing to stand and be maintained, often used of one who duly performs or upholds the ritual prayer (ṣalāh).
ai.g: An active participle (the 'one who does X' form) built on the causative Form IV pattern, so it carries the sense of 'one who makes (something) stand / keeps (it) up.' The final -a is the accusative ending, which generally marks a word as a direct object of a verb or as governing a following noun in a construct-like relationship.
ai.r: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, be upright

ai.m: The ritual Prayer — the formal worship of standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah at appointed times. More broadly the root conveys connection, supplication, and reaching out to the divine; it is the central act of Islamic devotion.
