ai.g: A definite feminine noun ('the prayer'). The article al- means 'the.' The -i ending (on the feminine tā') is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a preceding preposition or to another noun in an 'of' relationship (e.g. 'of the prayer / to the prayer').
ai.r: ص-ل-و (ṣ-l-w) — prayer, worship, connection, supplication

ai.m: 'And from / and out of / and among.' A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'from,' which marks origin, source, a starting point, or 'some of' a larger whole.
ai.g: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

ai.m: Offspring, progeny, descendants — the line of children and their children that issue from a person; collective in sense, covering one's seed and posterity.
ai.g: A feminine noun carrying a collective meaning ('descendants'). The attached -ī is the first-person possessive pronoun, 'my,' giving 'my offspring.' Before such a possessive, the noun takes the genitive vowel -i, the case that typically signals possession or links the word to what follows.
ai.r: ذ-ر-ر / ذ-ر-أ (dh-r-r / dh-r-ʾ) — to scatter, multiply, bring forth

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: To accept favorably and with approval; to receive (a deed, prayer, or repentance) graciously and grant it acceptance — more than mere taking, it implies welcoming with good pleasure.
ai.g: A command (imperative) verb on the intensive Form V pattern, which adds the nuance of accepting willingly and with favor. The bare, vowelless ending is the masculine singular imperative addressed to one person ('you, accept!'). The prefixed wa- means 'and,' joining it to what precedes.
ai.r: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to accept, receive, face toward

ai.m: A call, supplication, or invocation; the act of calling upon Allah in entreaty, prayer, or petition.
ai.g: A verbal noun (the name of the action 'calling / supplicating'). The final -i is the genitive ending, the case that usually marks possession, links the word to a following noun ('… of …'), or follows a preposition. Here the genitive is produced by a construct (iḍāfa) link to a following possessor; the -i is purely the case vowel and does not itself encode any pronoun. When a first-person possessor ('my') is understood, that meaning comes from a possessive yāʾ that has been elided, not from the genitive vowel.
ai.r: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invoke

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: Forgive! — a plea or command to pardon, to cover over and blot out wrongdoing. It carries the sense of veiling a fault so it is no longer held against the offender.
ai.g: A command (imperative) addressed to a single person: 'forgive!'. The vowelless final -r reflects the imperative form. It is commonly followed by 'us' or 'for me' to specify whom to pardon.
ai.r: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, conceal, and pardon; mercy that blots out sin

ai.m: 'to Me' or 'for Me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the first-person pronoun, expressing direction, benefit, or belonging toward the speaker.
ai.g: A preposition ('to/for') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me'). Together they express benefit, direction, or attribution toward the first person.

ai.m: Parents — the two who gave one birth, father and mother taken together as a pair.
ai.g: A dual noun ('the two parents') carrying the possessive 'my.' It follows the preposition li- ('for / to'). The dual ending appears in its genitive form -ay (rather than -ā), which is the shape duals take after a preposition or in a possession link; the attached -ya is 'my,' so the whole means 'and for my two parents.'
ai.r: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to beget, give birth

ai.m: Believers — those who have faith, who inwardly affirm and trust in Allah and give security through that faith; the ones characterized by true belief.
ai.g: A masculine sound plural active participle ('those who believe'), built on the causative Form IV pattern (faith that brings about inner security/affirmation). The plural ending -īna is the form used for the object of a verb or after a preposition; here it follows li- ('for'), and the prefixed al- ('the') makes it definite — 'and for the believers.'
ai.r: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, safety, faith, trust

ai.m: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
ai.g: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
ai.r: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

ai.m: He stands up, rises, or gets to his feet; also to undertake or attend to a matter. The core image is of coming to an upright, established position.
ai.g: A present/imperfect verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The final -u marks the indicative mood, signalling an ongoing or habitual action ('he stands / he is standing'); a change of that final vowel would signal a different mood.
ai.r: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, uphold

ai.m: The reckoning, the accounting, the settling of accounts; a careful computing and calling-to-account, as when deeds are tallied and judged.
ai.g: A verbal noun ('the act of reckoning / accounting'), made definite by al- ('the'). The final -u is the nominative ending, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing being described.
ai.r: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — to count, reckon, compute

title: Have mercy on my parents
situation: Alongside the command to be kind to one's parents in their old age, the Qur'an teaches this prayer of mercy for them, recalling how they raised us when we were small.
arabic: وَاخۡفِضۡ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ الذُّلِّ مِنَ الرَّحۡمَةِ وَقُلْ رَّبِّ ارۡحَمۡهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيٰنِىۡ صَغِيۡرًا ؕ‏
translation: And be humble with them out of mercy, and pray, “My Lord! Be merciful to them as they raised me when I was young.”
ai_translation: And be humble with them out of mercy, and pray, “My Rabb! Be merciful to them as they raised me when I was young.”

ai.m: And lower, let down, or bring down — and figuratively to be gentle and humble, to soften one's manner toward others.
ai.g: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single 'you', joined by wa- 'and'. Its vowelless ending is typical of the masculine-singular command form, directing one person to perform the act.
ai.r: خ-ف-ض (kh-f-ḍ) — to lower, let down, be gentle

ai.m: 'To them both / for the two of them' — a preposition meaning 'to / for' joined to a pronoun referring to exactly two people, indicating something directed toward or belonging to that pair.
ai.g: The preposition li- ('to / for,' often marking a recipient, beneficiary, or possessor) with its vowel shifting to 'a' before a pronoun, joined to the dual pronoun -humā ('the two of them'). The -humā ending specifically denotes two persons.

ai.m: Wing, side, or flank — literally a bird's wing, and by extension the side one lowers in tenderness; the image of 'lowering the wing' conveys gentle humility and protective care.
ai.g: A noun ('wing'). The final -a is the accusative case ending, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).
ai.r: ج-ن-ح (j-n-ḥ) — to incline, lean to one side; wing, flank

ai.m: Lowliness, humbleness, gentle submission — the state of making oneself low and meek out of tender care, the opposite of pride and harshness.
ai.g: A noun ('humility') carrying 'the' (al-, here the l assimilates into the following dh). The final -i is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a preceding noun in a '… OF …' possessive relationship, or follows a preposition.
ai.r: ذ-ل-ل (dh-l-l) — to be lowly, humble, submissive, abased

ai.m: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
ai.g: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

ai.m: Mercy — tender compassion joined with active kindness; the disposition that moves one to relieve, forgive, and show favor.
ai.g: A verbal noun ('mercy') with 'the'. The final -i is the genitive case ending, which typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.
ai.r: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion, womb-like tenderness

ai.m: And say — a command to one person to utter or speak words. The plain, central act of speaking aloud.
ai.g: A command (imperative) addressed to a single male, 'say!' from a hollow verb (middle root letter 'w' drops out in the command). The vowel-less ending is the standard singular masculine imperative. Prefixed wa- 'and' joins it to a preceding clause.
ai.r: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

ai.m: Lord and Master — the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and has full authority over a thing; a term combining ownership, care, and lordship that goes beyond any single English word.
ai.g: A noun with the -i (genitive) ending, which typically links the word to a following noun in an 'of / belonging to' relationship, or follows a preposition or oath particle. 'Rabb' denotes a master who owns, sustains, and nurtures what is under his charge.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, mastery and ownership

t.en: Have mercy on both of them

ai.m: An imperative plea meaning 'have mercy on the two of them' or 'show compassion to both.' It calls upon the one addressed (understood as Allah) to extend tender, active mercy toward two specific persons.

p.en: command form of 'have mercy' (with helping vowel)

ai.g: An imperative (command/request) verb. The helping vowel and dropped initial sound are typical of a command built on this root. The attached -huma is a dual object pronoun meaning 'the two of them,' so the whole word directs the requested mercy specifically toward two people.
ai.r: ر-ح-م (r-h-m) — mercy, compassion

ai.m: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
ai.g: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

ai.m: A past-tense verb meaning 'they two raised/nurtured me,' i.e. they reared, brought up, and cared for me from childhood. It carries the sense of patient upbringing and fostering.

p.en: protective nun + me (the nun shields the 'me' pronoun)

ai.g: A completed (past) action. The -a element marks a dual subject, 'the two of them did it.' The final element is the first-person object pronoun 'me' (the yaa), preceded by a connecting nun (nun al-wiqayah) that is inserted to protect and preserve that 'me' pronoun on the verb, so the word means 'the two of them brought me up.'
ai.r: ر-ب-و / ر-ب-ب (r-b-w / r-b-b) — to nurture, raise, foster growth

ai.m: Small, little, or minor — an adjective describing something of slight size, amount, or significance. It can also mean young in age. The -an ending leaves it indefinite ('a small …').
ai.g: An indefinite adjective on the faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative (tanwīn): it commonly marks the object of a verb, or works adverbially, and signals the word is indefinite ('a small one'). It pairs with kabīr ('large').
ai.r: ص-غ-ر (ṣ-gh-r) — smallness, being little or young

title: A truthful entrance and exit
situation: Often linked to the Hijra from Mecca to Medina, this prayer asks God for a sound, sincere entry and exit and for a supporting authority from Him.
arabic: وَقُلْ رَّبِّ اَدۡخِلۡنِىۡ مُدۡخَلَ صِدۡقٍ وَّ اَخۡرِجۡنِىۡ مُخۡرَجَ صِدۡقٍ وَّاجۡعَلْ لِّىۡ مِنۡ لَّدُنۡكَ سُلۡطٰنًا نَّصِيۡرًا‏
translation: And say, “My Lord! Grant me an honourable entrance and an honourable exit and give me a supporting authority from Yourself.”
ai_translation: Say: O my Rabb, grant me an entrance of truth and an exit of truth, and give me from Your presence a supporting authority.

ai.m: And say — a command to one person to utter or speak words. The plain, central act of speaking aloud.
ai.g: A command (imperative) addressed to a single male, 'say!' from a hollow verb (middle root letter 'w' drops out in the command). The vowel-less ending is the standard singular masculine imperative. Prefixed wa- 'and' joins it to a preceding clause.
ai.r: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

ai.m: Lord and Master — the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and has full authority over a thing; a term combining ownership, care, and lordship that goes beyond any single English word.
ai.g: A noun with the -i (genitive) ending, which typically links the word to a following noun in an 'of / belonging to' relationship, or follows a preposition or oath particle. 'Rabb' denotes a master who owns, sustains, and nurtures what is under his charge.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, mastery and ownership

ai.m: A command meaning 'cause me to enter / bring me in / admit me.' This is the causative form of 'to enter,' so the one addressed is asked to make the speaker go in.

p.en: inherent hamza of the causative (Form IV) verb pattern
cause to enter / admit (causative verb stem)

ai.g: An imperative (command) verb in the causative pattern (af'ala), meaning 'make/cause to enter' rather than simply 'enter.' The initial hamza (a-) belongs to the Form IV stem morphology, not to subject agreement. The addressee ('you,' singular) is encoded by the zero-suffix imperative form itself, not by any prefix. The attached -nī is the object 'me.' Being a command, it has no case ending; the request is for the listener to perform the action upon the speaker.
ai.r: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — to enter, go in

ai.m: A verbal noun / noun of place meaning 'an entering, a being-brought-in, a place or manner of entrance.' Tied to the causative sense, it conveys 'a bringing-in' or 'the entrance by which one is admitted.'

p.en: place/act of being made to enter; entrance

ai.g: A noun formed from the causative verb (pattern muf'al), denoting either the place of entering or the act of being made to enter. The final -a is the accusative ending, which typically marks the noun as an object — and often as a 'cognate' object reinforcing a related verb (entering with a true entering).
ai.r: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — to enter, go in

ai.m: Truthfulness, sincerity, genuineness — the quality of what is true and reliable. As the second word of a possessive phrase it lends the sense 'a true/sound/honourable ...'.
ai.g: A singular indefinite noun. The '-in' ending (doubled kasra, tanwīn) marks the genitive case for an indefinite noun — it typically shows that the word is linked to a preceding noun ('... OF truth') or follows a preposition.
ai.r: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness, sincerity

ai.m: 'And cause me to go out / bring me out / let me exit.' This pairs the connective 'and' with the causative command 'make me come out,' so the one addressed is asked to make the speaker leave or emerge.

p.en: inherent hamza of the causative (Form IV) verb pattern
cause to go out / bring out (causative verb stem)

ai.g: The prefix wa- means 'and,' joining this to what precedes. The core is an imperative (command) in the causative pattern (af'ala): 'make/cause to go out.' The initial hamza (a-) belongs to the Form IV stem morphology, not to subject agreement; the addressee ('you,' singular) is encoded by the zero-suffix imperative form itself. The attached -nī is the object 'me.' As a command it carries no case ending.
ai.r: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, come forth, exit

ai.m: A verbal noun / noun of place meaning 'a bringing-out, a being-made-to-exit, a place or manner of exit.' Linked to the causative sense, it conveys 'a leading-out' or 'the exit through which one is brought forth.'

p.en: place/act of being made to go out; exit

ai.g: A noun formed from the causative verb (pattern muf'al), denoting either the place of going out or the act of being made to go out. The final -a is the accusative ending, which typically marks the noun as an object, often as a 'cognate' object reinforcing a related verb.
ai.r: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, come forth, exit

ai.m: Truthfulness, sincerity, genuineness — the quality of what is true and reliable. As the second word of a possessive phrase it lends the sense 'a true/sound/honourable ...'.
ai.g: A singular indefinite noun. The '-in' ending (doubled kasra, tanwīn) marks the genitive case for an indefinite noun — it typically shows that the word is linked to a preceding noun ('... OF truth') or follows a preposition.
ai.r: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness, sincerity

ai.m: A command meaning 'make', 'set', 'appoint', or 'render' — identical in sense to id 920. Ja'ala is a versatile verb of making/placing/turning-into; with the joining 'and' it links to a preceding statement.
ai.g: 'And' joined to a command (imperative) verb addressed to a single 'you'. The bare imperative form (with no ending vowel) issues a direct request or order to one person. The verb often takes two objects ('make X into Y').
ai.r: ج-ع-ل (j-'-l) — making, placing, rendering, appointing

ai.m: For me / to me / mine — a preposition meaning 'to/for' fused with the first-person 'me', expressing possession, benefit, or attribution toward the speaker.
ai.g: The preposition li- ('to/for') joined to the attached pronoun -ī ('me'). Together they express that something belongs to, is owed to, or is for the benefit of the speaker.

ai.m: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
ai.g: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
ai.r: — (preposition)

ai.m: From Yourself; from Your presence. The base word ladun means 'the presence of', 'the side of', or 'directly from' — pointing to something issuing straight from a source. Here it is preceded by the preposition min ('from'), whose final n assimilates into the following l so that the l is doubled. With the attached pronoun the whole conveys 'from Your own presence', stressing that what is given comes directly from the giver.

p.en: from (preposition; its n merges into the following l)
presence / nearness / 'from with' (doubled l from the merged n)

ai.g: An adverb of place/source ('at, by, in the presence of') joined to the attached pronoun -ka, 'your/you' for a single masculine addressee, together conveying 'from Your presence'. The initial l is written with a shadda (doubled): this gemination results from the preceding preposition min, whose final n assimilates into the l. The word implies immediacy of source — something coming directly from the one referred to.
ai.r: — (an adverbial particle of place; no triliteral verbal root)

ai.m: Authority, sanction, or compelling proof — power or warrant given to back something up, whether kingly authority or a decisive argument. 'Sulṭān' is authorizing power or evidence.
ai.g: A single noun ('authority') carrying the accusative indefinite ending -an (tanwīn al-naṣb). This one ending does two things at once: the -a marks the accusative case (typically the direct object of a verb), and the final -n sound (nunation) shows the noun is indefinite ('an authority / any warrant'). The nunation is a diacritic on the case vowel, not a separable suffix, so the word stays one undivided token.
ai.r: س-ل-ط (s-l-ṭ) — power, dominance, authority

ai.m: A noun (intensive form) meaning 'a helper, a supporter, one who comes to another's aid.' The intensive pattern stresses reliability and strength in giving help — a steadfast defender or ally.
ai.g: A noun on the intensive pattern fa'īl ('one who reliably/strongly does'), here 'a constant helper.' The final -an is the accusative indefinite ending, which typically marks the word as an object of a verb or as a predicate after certain particles.
ai.r: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, aid, grant victory

title: Grant us mercy and guidance
who: The Youths of the Cave (Ashab al-Kahf)
situation: Fleeing a tyrant who would persecute their faith, the young believers took refuge in a cave and prayed for mercy and right guidance in their affair.
arabic: اِذۡ اَوَى الۡفِتۡيَةُ اِلَى الۡـكَهۡفِ فَقَالُوۡا رَبَّنَاۤ اٰتِنَا مِنۡ لَّدُنۡكَ رَحۡمَةً وَّهَيِّئۡ لَـنَا مِنۡ اَمۡرِنَا رَشَدًا‏  وَّرَبَطۡنَا عَلٰى قُلُوۡبِهِمۡ اِذۡ قَامُوۡا فَقَالُوۡا رَبُّنَا رَبُّ السَّمٰوٰتِ وَالۡاَرۡضِ لَنۡ نَّدۡعُوَا۫ مِنۡ دُوۡنِهٖۤ اِلٰهًـا​ لَّـقَدۡ قُلۡنَاۤ اِذًا شَطَطًا‏ ﻿﻿
translation: (10) ˹Remember˺ when those youths took refuge in the cave, and said, “Our Lord! Grant us mercy from Yourself and guide us rightly through our ordeal.” (14) And We strengthened their hearts when they stood up and declared, “Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. We will never call upon any god besides Him, or we would truly be uttering an outrageous lie.”
ai_translation: (10) When the young men took refuge in the cave and said: Our Rabb, grant us mercy from Yourself and guide us rightly through our ordeal. (14) And We strengthened their hearts when they stood up and declared, “Our Rabb is the Rabb of the heavens and the earth. We will never call upon anything besides Allah worthy of worship Him, or we would truly be uttering an outrageous lie.”

ai.m: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
ai.g: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

ai.m: He took refuge / he betook himself — to withdraw to a place for shelter and settle there, to retire to safe quarters. Past tense, masculine singular ('he').
ai.g: A past-tense verb (weak-lām root, ending in a long ā). With no added subject suffix, it is third-person masculine singular ('he'), so it states 'he took refuge / withdrew for shelter'.
ai.r: أ-و-ي (ʾ-w-y) — to take shelter, give refuge, withdraw to a place

ai.m: The young men / youths — young males in their prime of strength and vigor. A plural of 'youth', made definite by 'the'.
ai.g: A broken (irregular) plural noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final -u is the nominative case — the form a noun takes as the subject of a sentence (the ones who do the action), hence 'the youths' as a doer.
ai.r: ف-ت-ي (f-t-y) — youth, young manhood; vigor of the young

ai.m: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
ai.g: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

ai.m: The cave — a hollow opening or cavern in a mountain or rock, large enough to give shelter.
ai.g: A noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case — the form taken after a preposition or when joined to a preceding noun ('… OF …', e.g. 'companions OF the cave').
ai.r: ك-ه-ف (k-h-f) — cave, cavern; a place of refuge

ai.m: '…so / then they said.' Combines the connector 'so/then' (showing result or sequence) with a past-tense verb of speaking, third person plural — a completed act of saying by a group.
ai.g: A completed-action (past) verb prefixed with 'fa-' ('so/then'), which links it to what precedes as a result or next step. The '-ū' ending (with silent trailing alif) marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural).
ai.r: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: An imperative plea meaning 'give us / grant us / bring to us.' It is a request addressed to a single party (commonly Allah in supplication) asking that something be conferred upon 'us.'
ai.g: A command (imperative) verb from the form-IV verb 'to give/bring.' It is directed at a single addressee ('you give!'). The attached -nā is an object pronoun meaning 'us,' marking who receives the action.
ai.r: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to bring/give

ai.m: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
ai.g: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
ai.r: — (preposition)

ai.m: From Yourself; from Your presence. The base word ladun means 'the presence of', 'the side of', or 'directly from' — pointing to something issuing straight from a source. Here it is preceded by the preposition min ('from'), whose final n assimilates into the following l so that the l is doubled. With the attached pronoun the whole conveys 'from Your own presence', stressing that what is given comes directly from the giver.

p.en: from (preposition; its n merges into the following l)
presence / nearness / 'from with' (doubled l from the merged n)

ai.g: An adverb of place/source ('at, by, in the presence of') joined to the attached pronoun -ka, 'your/you' for a single masculine addressee, together conveying 'from Your presence'. The initial l is written with a shadda (doubled): this gemination results from the preceding preposition min, whose final n assimilates into the l. The word implies immediacy of source — something coming directly from the one referred to.
ai.r: — (an adverbial particle of place; no triliteral verbal root)

ai.m: Mercy: compassion that actively does good — tenderness joined with the will and power to relieve, forgive, and benefit. As a noun it names an instance or measure of such mercy.
ai.g: An indefinite noun with the -an (accusative) ending, marked by tanwīn (the doubled-n sound). The accusative generally signals the word is a direct object or otherwise governed; the tanwīn marks it as indefinite — 'a mercy', 'some mercy'.
ai.r: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion, womb-like tenderness

ai.m: A command meaning 'and make ready / prepare / arrange smoothly for.' The verb hayyaʾa conveys disposing something into a fitting, well-ordered state, removing obstacles so a matter falls into place; the opening element means 'and.'
ai.g: A command (imperative) addressed to a single male: 'arrange / make ready!' The verb is form II (the doubled middle root letter), which gives a sense of actively shaping or disposing something; the final consonant carries the silent/jussive ending typical of an imperative. The opening element is the connector 'and' (wa-); the doubled consonant (shaddah) on it reflects assimilation to the final sound of the preceding word.
ai.r: ه-ي-ء (h-y-ʾ) — to make ready, dispose, arrange into a fitting state

ai.m: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
ai.g: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

ai.m: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
ai.g: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
ai.r: — (preposition)

ai.m: Our affair, matter, command, or concern — that which we are dealing with or commanded to do. 'Amr' spans both a 'matter/situation' and a 'command/order'.
ai.g: A noun ('affair') with the -i ending, the genitive case — which typically links it to a preceding noun or follows a preposition ('… of our affair' / 'in our affair'). The attached -nā means 'our'.
ai.r: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command; also 'matter, affair, situation'

ai.m: Right guidance, sound direction, maturity of judgment — being on a straight and correct course, the opposite of error or folly.
ai.g: A masculine noun. The -an ending is the accusative with 'tanwīn' (the doubled-fatḥa nunation), which generally marks a word as an object of a verb, or as an adverbial/specifying complement ('... in the way of right guidance'). The tanwīn signals the noun is indefinite ('right guidance' in general).
ai.r: ر-ش-د (r-sh-d) — right guidance, sound judgment, maturity

ai.m: A past-tense statement meaning 'and We bound fast / fortified / made firm' — the verb rabaṭa is to tie or fasten securely, and figuratively to steady and strengthen (as in bracing the heart).
ai.g: A completed (past-tense) verb. The -nā ending is the attached subject pronoun 'we' (Allah's majestic plural). The opening element is the connector 'and' (wa-); the doubled consonant (shaddah) on it reflects assimilation to the final sound of the preceding word. The verb's core image is tying something tightly, hence 'to make steadfast.'
ai.r: ر-ب-ط (r-b-ṭ) — to tie, bind fast, fortify, brace

ai.m: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
ai.g: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

ai.m: 'Their hearts' — the plural of qalb ('heart'), joined to the pronoun 'their'. In Qur'anic usage the 'heart' (qalb) is the seat of understanding, intention, faith, and feeling, not merely the physical organ.
ai.g: Qulūb is the broken (irregular) plural of qalb, 'hearts'. The -i ending is genitive: here it appears because the noun follows a preposition and because it is possessed by an attached pronoun. The suffix -him means 'their' (a masculine plural group), and its -i- vowel matches the preceding genitive ending. So the whole means 'hearts belonging to them'.
ai.r: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, turn about, change

ai.m: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
ai.g: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

ai.m: A past-tense verb 'they stood up / they stood still / they arose'. The root covers standing, rising, and standing firm.
ai.g: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (males) did'; the written alif after it is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.
ai.r: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, stand firm

ai.m: '…so / then they said.' Combines the connector 'so/then' (showing result or sequence) with a past-tense verb of speaking, third person plural — a completed act of saying by a group.
ai.g: A completed-action (past) verb prefixed with 'fa-' ('so/then'), which links it to what precedes as a result or next step. The '-ū' ending (with silent trailing alif) marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural).
ai.r: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

ai.m: 'Our Lord' — 'Rabb' (Lord, Master, Sustainer who creates, owns, nurtures and governs) joined to 'our'. A weighty term for Allah as the One who brings up and sustains all that exists.
ai.g: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun '-nā' ('our'). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case, used when the word is the subject or predicate of a sentence ('[He] is our Lord').
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship

ai.m: The Lord of — owner, master and sustainer who creates, possesses and governs. Of Allah it names the One who brings up and maintains all that exists.
ai.g: The noun 'rabb' with the final -u marking the nominative case (subject or predicate: '… is the Lord'). Standing before a following noun it carries the sense 'Lord of …'. It combines ownership, authority and nurturing care.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, ownership, nurturing

ai.m: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
ai.g: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.
ai.r: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, sky

ai.m: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
ai.g: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.
ai.r: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land

ai.m: 'Never / will not' — a particle that negates a future action emphatically. Lan denies that something will ever happen, stronger and more absolute than a simple 'not'.
ai.g: A negating particle that applies to present-tense verbs to deny them in the future ('will never…'). Grammatically it also puts the following verb into the subjunctive mood, which clips that verb's ending to a short -a. Lan itself does not change.
ai.r: — (particle)

ai.m: A statement meaning 'we call upon / invoke / appeal to' — the verb daʿā is to call out to someone, to summon, or to worship by supplication.
ai.g: A present/future verb with the na- prefix meaning 'we.' The final -a (here written with a following alif) is the subjunctive ending, which appears after certain particles meaning 'that / so that / never will' and gives the sense of a hoped-for, intended, or negated future act rather than a plain statement of fact.
ai.r: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invoke, supplicate

ai.m: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
ai.g: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
ai.r: — (preposition)

ai.m: Other than Him / apart from Him / besides Him. A relational word expressing the idea of being below, short of, or to the exclusion of something or someone.

p.en: other than, apart from, besides, below

ai.g: A relational noun/quasi-preposition meaning 'apart from / instead of'. It is followed by a possessive pronoun -hi ('Him'), which puts it in the genitive 'of' relationship; the kasra written under the pronoun reflects this genitive linkage.
ai.r: — (no triliteral root; a relational particle/noun)

ai.m: 'A god / a deity, an object of worship' — the word in its indefinite form, naming a single divine being without specifying which.
ai.g: A singular indefinite noun. The -an ending combines two things: the accusative case (the form for a verb's object or, often, a noun described by a following adjective) and nunation, the -n sound that signals 'a/an,' i.e. indefiniteness.
ai.r: ء-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, that which is worshipped

ai.m: An emphatic opener meaning roughly 'indeed, certainly, assuredly' — a combination of an emphasis particle ('truly') with a particle that, on a past-tense verb, stresses that the act has definitely occurred.
ai.g: Two particles fused together. The la- is an emphatic prefix ('truly'); the doubled consonant (shaddah) on it reflects assimilation to the final sound of the preceding word. qad before a completed (past-tense) verb stresses that the action has really and already happened ('has indeed ...'). Together they form a strong assertion. Particles like these have no case endings.

ai.m: 'We said' — the act of speaking or uttering, completed in the past, with 'we' as the speakers (a plural, or the royal/majestic 'We').
ai.g: A past-tense verb 'to say' with the suffix '-nā' marking the doer as 'we' (first-person plural). This is a hollow verb (its middle root letter is a weak 'w'), which contracts before the suffix to leave 'qul-' before the ending.
ai.r: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak

ai.m: In that case / then — a response particle signaling that what follows is the consequence of a just-stated condition or supposition ('if so, then…').
ai.g: A response/consequence particle, not a noun or verb. The -an ending is a fixed part of the word (written with a final alif), not a live grammatical case. It introduces the result side of a hypothetical ('then you would…').

ai.m: Something wildly excessive and wrong — an outrageous overstepping, a gross deviation far beyond bounds; an enormity or blatant falsehood.
ai.g: A masculine noun. The -an ending is the accusative with tanwīn (doubled fatḥa), typically marking an object or a specifying complement ('... as an outrage / in excess'). The tanwīn marks it indefinite ('an enormity').
ai.r: ش-ط-ط (sh-ṭ-ṭ) — to go far beyond bounds, be grossly excessive

title: Expand my chest and ease my task
situation: Commanded to confront Pharaoh, he asked God to open his heart, make his mission easy, and loosen the knot in his tongue so people would understand him.
arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ اشۡرَحۡ لِىۡ صَدۡرِىْ ۙ‏  وَيَسِّرۡ لِىۡۤ اَمۡرِىْ ۙ‏  وَاحۡلُلۡ عُقۡدَةً مِّنۡ لِّسَانِیْ ۙ‏  يَفۡقَهُوۡا قَوۡلِیْ ‏
translation: (25) Moses prayed, “My Lord! Uplift my heart for me, (26) and make my task easy, (27) and remove the impediment from my tongue (28) so people may understand my speech,
ai_translation: (25) Moses said: My Rabb, expand my chest for me, ease my task for me, (26) and untie the knot from my tongue so they may understand my speech. (27) and remove the impediment from my tongue. (28) so people may understand my speech,.

ai.m: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
ai.g: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
ai.r: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
ai.g: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: Open up, expand, broaden, lay open. To widen something or make it spacious; figuratively, to make the heart receptive, relieved, and at ease.
ai.g: A command (imperative) addressed to one male. The initial i- is the connecting helper-vowel for the consonant cluster; the final vowelless -ḥ (sukūn) marks the masculine singular imperative.
ai.r: ش-ر-ح (sh-r-ḥ) — to open up, expand, explain

ai.m: 'to Me' or 'for Me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the first-person pronoun, expressing direction, benefit, or belonging toward the speaker.
ai.g: A preposition ('to/for') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me'). Together they express benefit, direction, or attribution toward the first person.

ai.m: My chest or breast; by extension the bosom as the seat of the heart, feelings, and inner self.
ai.g: A noun possessed by the speaker. The attached -ī means 'my', and a possessor pronoun puts the noun in the genitive (the -i base vowel), giving 'the chest OF me'.
ai.r: ص-د-ر (ṣ-d-r) — chest, front; to proceed/issue forth

ai.m: And make easy, smooth, or facilitate. To remove difficulty from a matter and render it manageable and effortless.
ai.g: A command (imperative) to one male, joined by wa- ('and'). It is form II (the doubled middle consonant -ss-), which here intensifies the simple root into 'to make easy, to facilitate'. The final vowelless -r (sukūn) is the masculine singular imperative ending.
ai.r: ي-س-ر (y-s-r) — ease, facility; to be easy

ai.m: 'to Me' or 'for Me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the first-person pronoun, expressing direction, benefit, or belonging toward the speaker.
ai.g: A preposition ('to/for') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me'). Together they express benefit, direction, or attribution toward the first person.

ai.m: My affair, matter, command, or task. A broad word covering a directive, a concern, a situation, or a piece of business that one is occupied with.
ai.g: A noun possessed by the speaker. The -ī suffix means 'my', and the possessor pronoun places the noun in the genitive (the -i base vowel): 'the affair OF me'.
ai.r: أ-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command; an affair/matter

ai.m: And loosen, untie, undo, or release. To unfasten a knot or set free what is bound.
ai.g: A command (imperative) to one male, joined by wa- ('and'). The connecting helper-vowel is pronounced u- here because the stem's interior vowel is u; the final vowelless -l (sukūn) marks the masculine singular imperative.
ai.r: ح-ل-ل (ḥ-l-l) — to untie, loosen, make lawful, alight

ai.m: A knot; a tied fastening, and figuratively a difficulty, complication, or impediment that ties something up.
ai.g: An indefinite feminine noun in the accusative case. The -an ending (nunation, here surfacing as -tan because the feminine -t is sounded before it) marks it as the object of a verb and as indefinite ('a knot'). The single-instance pattern (faʿla) names one knot.
ai.r: ع-ق-د (ʿ-q-d) — to tie, knot, contract, bind

ai.m: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
ai.g: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

ai.m: My tongue; by extension my speech, language, or manner of speaking.
ai.g: A noun possessed by the speaker. The -ī suffix means 'my', and a possessor pronoun puts the noun in the genitive (the -i base vowel): 'the tongue OF me'.
ai.r: ل-س-ن (l-s-n) — tongue, language, speech

ai.m: That they may understand, grasp, or comprehend deeply. Denotes perceiving the meaning and gaining real insight into something, not mere hearing.
ai.g: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'). The ya- prefix plus the -ū ending together mark 'they'; the normal -ūna has dropped its final -na, signalling the subjunctive mood that follows purpose words ('so that they may understand').
ai.r: ف-ق-ه (f-q-h) — to understand deeply, comprehend, gain insight

ai.m: My speech, saying, statement, or words; what one utters or says.
ai.g: A noun possessed by the speaker. The -ī suffix means 'my', and the possessor pronoun puts the noun in the genitive (the -i base vowel): 'the saying OF me'.
ai.r: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak; a saying/word

title: We fear he will transgress
who: Prophet Musa and his brother Harun
situation: Sent together to Pharaoh, they confided their fear that he would strike at them or rage against them — and God reassured them that He was with them, hearing and seeing.
arabic: قَالَا رَبَّنَاۤ اِنَّـنَا نَخَافُ اَنۡ يَّفۡرُطَ عَلَيۡنَاۤ اَوۡ اَنۡ يَّطۡغٰى‏ ﻿﻿
translation: They both pleaded, “Our Lord! We fear that he may be quick to harm us or act tyrannically.”
ai_translation: They both pleaded, “Our Rabb! We fear that he may be quick to harm us or act tyrannically.”

ai.m: The two of them said — to speak or utter words, with two subjects voicing the speech together. This form introduces what two people said.
ai.g: A past-tense (perfect) verb with the dual subject ending -ā ('the two of them did'). This -ā specifically marks exactly two doers acting together.
ai.r: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

p.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

ai.g: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: 'Indeed we …' — an emphatic opener that combines a particle of strong affirmation ('truly, certainly') with the pronoun 'we', stressing and confirming the statement that follows about the speakers.
ai.g: The emphatic particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with the attached pronoun '-nā' ('we'). 'Inna' introduces a sentence and lends it certainty and emphasis, while '-nā' is its subject, identifying the speakers as 'we'. This is the fuller, uncontracted form (innanā) of the commonly contracted innā; the extra nūn belongs to the longer pronominal base used to keep the doubled nūn of 'inna' and the nūn of the pronoun distinct rather than merged.
ai.r: — (particle of emphasis; no triliteral root)

ai.m: 'We fear' / 'we are afraid' — to feel fear or apprehension of harm. The verb expresses the dread of a possible bad outcome, with the subject being 'we.'
ai.g: A present-tense verb. The na- prefix means 'we.' The closing -u marks the indicative mood, the form used for a plain ongoing statement of fact ('we [do] fear'), as opposed to a wish or command.
ai.r: خ-و-ف (kh-w-f) — fear, fright

ai.m: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
ai.g: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
ai.r: — (particle; no root)

ai.m: 'He acts rashly / hastily oversteps / rushes to excess' — to be hasty and immoderate, to go too far in a sudden, headlong way. The verb pairs the idea of haste with overstepping due bounds.
ai.g: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person singular masculine subject ('he'). The final -a is the subjunctive mood, used after particles like 'that' or 'lest' to express a feared, purposed, or merely possible outcome rather than a flat statement.
ai.r: ف-ر-ط (f-r-ṭ) — going to excess, haste, neglecting bounds

ai.m: 'Upon us' / 'over us' / 'against us' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, upon') with an attached 'us'. It conveys something resting on, incumbent upon, or bearing against the group.
ai.g: A preposition (ʿalā, 'upon/over') with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'us'). When a pronoun is attached, ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay-. Such prepositional phrases put their pronoun in the object/genitive role.

ai.m: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
ai.g: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

ai.m: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
ai.g: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
ai.r: — (particle; no root)

ai.m: 'He transgresses / overflows all bounds / turns tyrant' — to exceed proper limits in arrogance and oppression, the imagery being a flood bursting its banks. The subject is a single male.
ai.g: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person singular masculine subject ('he'). The root ends in a weak letter, so the verb closes with a long -ā; in this form the ending can carry an ongoing sense or a subjunctive 'that he may transgress' after a purpose particle.
ai.r: ط-غ-ي (ṭ-gh-y) — exceeding limits, tyranny, rebellion

title: Increase me in knowledge
who: The Prophet Muhammad — and every seeker
situation: Taught directly to the Prophet, this is the one thing the Qur'an tells him to ask for more of: knowledge. It has become the seeker's prayer for learning.
arabic: فَتَعٰلَى اللّٰهُ الۡمَلِكُ الۡحَـقُّ​ ۚ وَلَا تَعۡجَلۡ بِالۡقُرۡاٰنِ مِنۡ قَبۡلِ اَنۡ يُّقۡضٰٓى اِلَيۡكَ وَحۡيُهٗ​ وَقُلْ رَّبِّ زِدۡنِىۡ عِلۡمًا‏
translation: Exalted is Allah, the True King! Do not rush to recite ˹a revelation of˺ the Quran ˹O Prophet˺ before it is ˹properly˺ conveyed to you, and pray, “My Lord! Increase me in knowledge.”
ai_translation: Exalted is Allah, the True King! Do not rush to recite a revelation of the Quran O Prophet before it is properly conveyed to you, and pray, “My Rabb! Increase me in knowledge.”

ai.m: 'So He is exalted high above (it)' or 'then He is far transcendent.' Built on a verb meaning to be lofty/elevated, this form expresses that someone is utterly high and above something — used of Allah being far beyond any deficiency or false association. The opening fa- links it to what precedes as a consequence.
ai.g: A 'he' verb expressing height and transcendence. The prefix fa- means 'so/then,' drawing a consequence. The verb pattern intensifies the sense of being elevated and removed far above something lower.
ai.r: ع-ل-و (ʿ-l-w) — to be high, lofty, exalted

ai.m: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
ai.g: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
ai.r: — (proper divine name)

ai.m: 'The king' — the sovereign ruler who holds dominion and authority over a realm and its people.
ai.g: A definite noun ('the king'). The final -u ending is the nominative case, the form a noun takes as the subject of a sentence or as a predicate.
ai.r: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, rule, hold dominion

ai.m: 'The truth / the reality; what is right, real, and rightfully due.' A weighty noun meaning that which is firmly true and real, as opposed to falsehood; it also carries the senses of a rightful claim, a duty owed, and justice. With the article it denotes 'the Truth' in a definite, absolute sense.
ai.g: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') plus the stem. The final -u ending is the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a word identifying what something is (as in 'X is the truth').
ai.r: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, reality, rightness; that which is established and rightfully due

ai.m: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
ai.g: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

ai.m: 'Do not be hasty / hurry / rush' — a verb about seeking something too quickly, acting before the proper time, or being impatient. It is the form used after a prohibition word ('do not…').
ai.g: The ta- prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'). The verb is present tense, and the bare, vowel-less final consonant (the jussive form) is the shape used after a prohibitive 'do not', giving a command not to do something ('do not hurry').
ai.r: ع-ج-ل (ʿ-j-l) — to hasten, hurry, be impatient

ai.m: With/by the Qur'an — al-Qur'ān, literally 'the Recitation' or 'the Reading,' the revealed Scripture meant to be recited aloud.
ai.g: A definite verbal noun governed by the preposition bi- ('with/by'). The final -i (kasra) is the genitive case ending, the case required after a preposition.
ai.r: ق-ر-أ (q-r-ʾ) — to read, to recite, to gather words in recitation

ai.m: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
ai.g: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
ai.r: — (preposition)

ai.m: A noun/adverb meaning 'before' — denoting that which precedes in time or order.
ai.g: An adverb/noun of time. The -i ending is genitive, which here arises because it follows a preposition (commonly 'min', 'from'); it characteristically links to a following noun ('before … OF …').
ai.r: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; the front or prior side

ai.m: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
ai.g: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
ai.r: — (particle; no root)

ai.m: It is decreed, decided, carried out, or brought to completion — to settle a matter fully and conclusively, finishing it off.
ai.g: A present-tense passive verb ('it is being decreed/completed'). The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject, and the passive vowelling shows the action is done to it rather than by it. The final long -ā belongs to this weak-ending verb; in the present such a verb's last vowel is not separately pronounced for case.
ai.r: ق-ض-ي (q-ḍ-y) — to decree, decide, carry out, bring to a conclusive end

ai.m: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
ai.g: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.
ai.r: — (preposition + pronoun)

ai.m: Its revelation, its inspiration — waḥy is the act and content of divine disclosure, words and meaning conveyed swiftly and secretly from Allah to a chosen recipient.
ai.g: A verbal noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u (ḍamma) before the pronoun is the nominative case ending, typically marking the subject of a sentence. The suffix -hu means 'his/its', showing possession.
ai.r: و-ح-ي (w-ḥ-y) — to disclose swiftly and secretly; divine inspiration, revelation

ai.m: And say — a command to one person to utter or speak words. The plain, central act of speaking aloud.
ai.g: A command (imperative) addressed to a single male, 'say!' from a hollow verb (middle root letter 'w' drops out in the command). The vowel-less ending is the standard singular masculine imperative. Prefixed wa- 'and' joins it to a preceding clause.
ai.r: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

ai.m: Lord and Master — the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and has full authority over a thing; a term combining ownership, care, and lordship that goes beyond any single English word.
ai.g: A noun with the -i (genitive) ending, which typically links the word to a following noun in an 'of / belonging to' relationship, or follows a preposition or oath particle. 'Rabb' denotes a master who owns, sustains, and nurtures what is under his charge.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, mastery and ownership

ai.m: Increase me, give me more, add to what I have — a request to be granted a greater measure of something.
ai.g: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single person ('increase!'), with no case vowel since commands rest on the bare verb form. The attached -nī means 'me,' the one receiving the action (its 'n' is a connector that protects the verb before the 'me').
ai.r: ز-ي-د (z-y-d) — to increase, add, grow, give more

ai.m: Knowledge — that which is known; firm, certain awareness and understanding.
ai.g: An abstract noun, 'knowledge.' The final -an is the accusative with indefinite 'nunation,' commonly marking the noun as a direct object, or as a specification ('in respect of knowledge').
ai.r: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know, knowledge

title: Adversity has touched me
situation: After long years of illness and loss borne with patience, he turned to God with gentle, uncomplaining words — and God restored him and removed his suffering.
arabic: وَاَيُّوۡبَ اِذۡ نَادٰى رَبَّهٗۤ اَنِّىۡ مَسَّنِىَ الضُّرُّ وَاَنۡتَ اَرۡحَمُ الرّٰحِمِيۡنَ​ ۖ​ۚ‏
translation: And ˹remember˺ when Job cried out to his Lord, “I have been touched with adversity, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.”
ai_translation: And remember when Job cried out to his Rabb, “I have been touched with adversity, and You are the the Rahim — special mercy for believers in the Akhirah — the everlasting life after death of the merciful.”

ai.m: A linking phrase 'and Job' — joining the proper name of the Prophet Ayyūb with 'and'.
ai.g: The connector wa- ('and') plus a proper name. The name ends in -a and is a 'diptote' — a noun that resists full case endings, so it shows -a (not -in) and takes no nunation; this -a form covers both the object and after-a-preposition roles.

ai.m: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
ai.g: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

ai.m: He called out, summoned, or cried aloud to someone — a completed act of calling, often invocation or summons. The Form III pattern adds the sense of directing the call toward another party.
ai.g: A Form III past-tense verb whose third root letter is weak (a defective verb), so the stem ends in the long vowel written as alif maqṣūra (ـى). It denotes a completed action by 'he' (one male); that 'he' subject is marked by a zero suffix (no added ending), the final long -ā being part of the stem itself, not a separate person/tense marker. Form III characteristically denotes doing an action toward or with another, hence 'to call OUT TO someone.'
ai.r: ن-د-و / ن-د-ي (n-d-w / n-d-y) — to call, summon

ai.m: The noun 'Lord' joined to a 'his' pronoun — 'his Lord'. Rabb conveys the Master and Sustainer who owns, nurtures, and brings a thing to its full development; far richer than 'lord' alone.
ai.g: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun -hu ('his'). The -a ending is accusative, the case used when the noun is an object of a verb or otherwise governed into that case; -hu means it belongs to 'him'.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, ownership, nurturing and sustaining to completion

ai.m: That I — the subordinating particle 'that' fused with the pronoun 'I', used to introduce a noun clause stating a fact about oneself.
ai.g: The particle 'anna' is a subordinating complementizer meaning 'that'; it introduces a factive noun clause (e.g. as the content of 'I inform you that …'). It is not in itself emphatic — its function is to subordinate the clause, not to assert 'indeed' (that sense belongs to the separate particle 'inna'). 'anna' governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative; the attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I/me') serving as its subject.

ai.m: It touched me / befell me — a verb meaning 'to touch, make contact with', often used of harm or a state reaching and affecting a person, here with the object 'me'.
ai.g: Past-tense verb; the -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular doer ('he/it'). The object 'me' is attached as -nī (the -n- is a connecting buffer before the 'me' pronoun, here voweled -niya).
ai.r: م-س-س (m-s-s) — to touch, make contact, afflict

ai.m: the harm, distress, injury, or adversity — affliction that touches a person, such as illness, hardship, or loss.
ai.g: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence (the doer or the thing 'that …'). The 'ḍ' absorbs the 'l' of 'al-' in pronunciation.
ai.r: ض-ر-ر (ḍ-r-r) — harm, injury, adversity

ai.m: 'And You' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'you' (addressing a single male). The independent pronoun stresses the subject, as in 'and You [Yourself] …'.
ai.g: A connective 'and' plus a detached subject pronoun. 'anta' is the masculine-singular 'you'; as a standalone pronoun it adds emphasis or introduces a statement about the addressee ('You are …').

ai.m: Most merciful / more merciful — the superlative or comparative of 'merciful': the one whose mercy surpasses all others'.
ai.g: A comparative/superlative adjective on the pattern afʿal ('most/more …'). The final -u (ḍamma) is the nominative ending, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a word standing as a predicate.
ai.r: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion

ai.m: Refers to those who show mercy and compassion — 'the merciful ones'. A plural describing people characterized by the quality of mercy.
ai.g: The l- prefix is 'the' (definite). The -īna ending is the masculine sound plural in its accusative/genitive form: it marks a plural of people in any role other than the subject (e.g. as an object, or after a preposition or in an 'of…' construction). Active participle of the form fāʿil, so 'the ones who show mercy'.
ai.r: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion

title: There is no god but You
situation: Swallowed by the great fish, in the layered darkness of the sea, he called out this prayer of God's oneness and his own wrongdoing — and was delivered. The Prophet said no distressed believer prays it without being answered.
arabic: وَ ذَا النُّوۡنِ اِذْ ذَّهَبَ مُغَاضِبًا فَظَنَّ اَنۡ لَّنۡ نَّـقۡدِرَ عَلَيۡهِ فَنَادٰى فِى الظُّلُمٰتِ اَنۡ لَّاۤ اِلٰهَ اِلَّاۤ اَنۡتَ سُبۡحٰنَكَ ​ۖ  اِنِّىۡ كُنۡتُ مِنَ الظّٰلِمِيۡنَ​ ۖ ​ۚ‏
translation: And ˹remember˺ when the Man of the Whale stormed off ˹from his city˺ in a rage, thinking We would not restrain him. Then in the ˹veils of˺ darkness he cried out, “There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except You. Glory be to You! I have certainly done wrong.”
ai_translation: And to Dhu'l-Nun, when he went off in anger and thought We would not restrict him — he cried out in the darkness: There is none worthy of worship except You. Glory be to You. I was among the wrongdoers.

ai.m: 'And the one possessing / owner of …' — dhā means 'possessor of' or 'the one endowed with,' and it must be followed by another noun to complete the sense. Opens with the connector 'and.'
ai.g: 'wa' means 'and.' 'dhā' is one of the special 'five nouns'; its long '-ā' is the accusative form, signalling it is functioning as an object or governed element, and it grammatically requires a following noun in the genitive ('possessor OF …').

ai.m: 'The Nūn' — literally 'the great fish / whale.' The word names a large sea creature and forms part of a prophet's title ('the man of the fish').
ai.g: 'l-' is the definite article 'the.' The '-i' ending is genitive, marking the word as possessed in a construct ('the one OF the fish') or as following a preposition.
ai.r: ن-و-ن (n-w-n) — the large fish/whale (a primitive noun)

ai.m: When — a particle pointing to a past moment or circumstance, 'at the time that …'. It situates an event in time, typically introducing something that occurred.
ai.g: A time particle/adverb meaning 'when' or 'at the time when,' generally pointing to the past. It is indeclinable — it never changes its ending — and serves to introduce a clause about when something happened.

ai.m: 'He went / departed' — a simple past-tense verb describing a single male subject leaving or going away.
ai.g: A completed (past) action. The bare '-a' ending with no added pronoun means the subject is 'he' (third-person masculine singular).
ai.r: ذ-ه-ب (dh-h-b) — going, departing

ai.m: 'Angry / enraged' — an active participle describing someone in a state of anger or indignation, often used to depict the manner in which an action is done (i.e., 'while angry').

p.en: angry / in a state of anger

ai.g: An active participle (one who is angry). The '-an' ending (accusative with tanwīn) commonly marks it as a circumstantial description — telling the state or manner of a person ('… while angry') — or as an object.
ai.r: غ-ض-ب (gh-ḍ-b) — anger, wrath

ai.m: 'So/then he thought / supposed / became convinced' — a past-tense verb of forming an opinion or assumption, with a 'he' subject, joined by 'so/then.'
ai.g: 'fa' means 'so' or 'then,' linking to what precedes as a consequence or sequence. The verb is a completed (past) action; the '-a' ending with no added pronoun means the subject is 'he.'
ai.r: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n) — to think, suppose, conjecture, presume

ai.m: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
ai.g: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
ai.r: — (particle; no root)

ai.m: A particle of strong negation directed at the future: 'never; will not at all.' It emphatically denies that something will ever happen and puts the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive.
ai.g: A negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb, denying it for the future and forcing that verb into the subjunctive mood (so the verb takes a final '-a' instead of '-u'). It has no ending of its own.

ai.m: 'We restrict / straiten / measure out (a tight measure upon)' — a verb from the root meaning to measure or limit; with a 'we' subject it conveys 'we would constrain / impose a tight measure.'
ai.g: The 'na-' prefix means the subject is 'we.' This is a present/future-type verb (Form I). In the full word naqdira the consonant 'q' closes the syllable with the prefix (naq-di-ra), which is why it carries no vowel of its own in this segment. The final '-a' is the subjunctive ending, which appears after certain particles and gives a hypothetical or intended sense ('that We would restrict').
ai.r: ق-د-ر (q-d-r) — to measure, decree, determine; power, capacity

ai.m: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
ai.g: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

ai.m: 'Then/so he called out / cried' — a past-tense verb of calling aloud or appealing, with a 'he' subject, prefaced by 'then/so.'
ai.g: 'fa' means 'then' or 'so,' marking sequence or consequence. The verb is a completed (past) action ending in a long '-ā,' with the subject 'he' (third-person masculine singular). The pattern (fā'ala) conveys calling out to or appealing to someone.
ai.r: ن-د-ي / ن-د-و (n-d-y) — to call, call out, summon

ai.m: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
ai.g: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
ai.r: — (particle)

ai.m: Darknesses, layers of gloom; the manifold states of being deprived of light, whether literal or as a figure for ignorance and error.
ai.g: A definite sound feminine plural noun ("the darknesses"). The -i ending here is genitive — the case taken by this plural after a preposition (the -āt plural shows genitive with -i rather than the -a it would take in the accusative). The al- prefix makes it definite ("the").
ai.r: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — darkness; also wrongdoing and injustice

ai.m: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
ai.g: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
ai.r: — (particle; no root)

ai.m: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
ai.g: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

ai.m: God / object of worship — a deity that is worshipped. The bare noun names the concept of a worshipped god.
ai.g: A singular noun carrying an -a ending. This short -a typically marks the accusative (object) case; it is also the form a noun takes immediately after the absolute-negation particle 'lā' to mean 'no … (at all).'
ai.r: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

ai.m: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
ai.g: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
ai.r: — (particle)

ai.m: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
ai.g: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

ai.m: 'Glory be to You / how far above all imperfection You are' — a set exclamation declaring Allah utterly free of any flaw, deficiency, or partner. It pairs the verbal noun of 'declaring transcendence' with a 'You' addressed to Allah.

p.en: utter transcendence / glory (free of all flaw)

ai.g: 'subḥāna' is a verbal noun in the accusative, used as an absolute exclamation of praise ('glorification be …'). The attached '-ka' is the possessive/object 'You(r),' so the whole means 'Your absolute freedom from imperfection' — i.e., 'Glory be to You.' Addressed to a single male listener.
ai.r: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to declare (Allah) free of all imperfection; to glorify

ai.m: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
ai.g: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

ai.m: A verb meaning 'I was / I had been,' the core verb of being placed in the past for the speaker. It links 'I' to a past state or description: 'I used to be / I came to be in such a condition.'
ai.g: The past-tense verb 'to be,' first-person singular. The suffix '-tu' is the past-tense ending that means 'I' (the one who did/was). It expresses a completed or settled past state — 'I was, I had been.'
ai.r: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

ai.m: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
ai.g: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

ai.m: The wrongdoers — those who do wrong or injustice; literally those who put things out of their rightful place, transgressing limits and harming themselves or others. The root sense is darkness.
ai.g: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', doubling it). The stem is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the object/genitive form of the sound masculine plural, marking the word as an object of a verb or governed by a preposition.
ai.r: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — darkness; wrongdoing, injustice

title: Do not leave me childless
situation: In old age and without an heir, he called upon God privately, asking not to be left alone and affirming that God is the best of inheritors.
arabic: وَزَكَرِيَّاۤ اِذۡ نَادٰى رَبَّهٗ رَبِّ لَا تَذَرۡنِىۡ فَرۡدًا وَّاَنۡتَ خَيۡرُ الۡوٰرِثِيۡنَ​ ۖ​ۚ‏
translation: And ˹remember˺ when Zachariah cried out to his Lord, “My Lord! Do not leave me childless, though You are the Best of Successors.”
ai_translation: And remember when Zachariah cried out to his Rabb, “My Rabb! Do not leave me childless, though You are the Best of Successors.”

ai.m: 'And Zechariah (Zakariyyā)' — the proper name of the prophet, prefixed with 'and'.
ai.g: A proper name of non-Arabic origin prefixed with 'wa' ('and'). It ends in a fixed long '-ā' and so shows no visible change for case.
ai.r: — (proper name, no Arabic root)

ai.m: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
ai.g: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

ai.m: He called out, summoned, or cried aloud to someone — a completed act of calling, often invocation or summons. The Form III pattern adds the sense of directing the call toward another party.
ai.g: A Form III past-tense verb whose third root letter is weak (a defective verb), so the stem ends in the long vowel written as alif maqṣūra (ـى). It denotes a completed action by 'he' (one male); that 'he' subject is marked by a zero suffix (no added ending), the final long -ā being part of the stem itself, not a separate person/tense marker. Form III characteristically denotes doing an action toward or with another, hence 'to call OUT TO someone.'
ai.r: ن-د-و / ن-د-ي (n-d-w / n-d-y) — to call, summon

ai.m: The noun 'Lord' joined to a 'his' pronoun — 'his Lord'. Rabb conveys the Master and Sustainer who owns, nurtures, and brings a thing to its full development; far richer than 'lord' alone.
ai.g: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun -hu ('his'). The -a ending is accusative, the case used when the noun is an object of a verb or otherwise governed into that case; -hu means it belongs to 'him'.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, ownership, nurturing and sustaining to completion

ai.m: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
ai.g: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
ai.r: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

ai.m: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
